column2: Tiếng Việt (zh). Machine-made by Claude: please have a native speaker check it.

column1: Very easy greetings for when you meet someone for the first time and when you say goodbye.
column2: 第一次见面和告别时用的非常简单的问候语。

column1: When you meet, say "안녕하세요?"; when you part, say "안녕히 가세요" or "안녕히 계세요".
column2: 见面时说 "안녕하세요?"，分别时说 "안녕히 가세요" 或 "안녕히 계세요"。

column1: 안녕하세요? can be used in the morning, afternoon and evening. It is like "Hello".
column2: 안녕하세요? 早上、下午、晚上都可以用，就像 "你好"。

column1: To the person leaving, say "안녕히 가세요"; to the person staying, say "안녕히 계세요".
column2: 对离开的人说 "안녕히 가세요"，对留下的人说 "안녕히 계세요"。

column1: I say hello with a smile.
I say hello in the morning.
I'm Sam. Nice to meet you.
column2: 我是山姆，很高兴见到你。

column1: How have you been? (after a long time)
Long time no see. How have you been?
to be well, to be at peace
Hello. I'm Minha. Nice to meet you.
column2: 你好，我是敏夏，很高兴见到你。

column1: Words for saying thank you and sorry, and how to answer them.
column2: 表示感谢和道歉的话，以及怎样回答。

column1: When you are thankful, say "감사합니다"; when you are sorry, say "죄송합니다".
To older people or people above you, use "감사합니다" and "죄송합니다".
column2: 对长辈或上级用 "감사합니다" 和 "죄송합니다"。

column1: The answer to "감사합니다" is "아니에요", and the answer to "죄송합니다" is "괜찮아요".
column2: 回答 "감사합니다" 用 "아니에요"，回答 "죄송합니다" 用 "괜찮아요"。

column1: I buy a gift for my friend.
I'm sorry. I'll do it again.

column2: 打扰一下 (打扰别人之前)

column1: Excuse me. May I come in?
column2: 打扰一下，我可以进来吗?

column1: Excuse me. Where is the restroom?
column2: 打扰一下，洗手间在哪里?

column1: Easy words for asking and answering about names and age.
column2: 询问和回答名字、年龄的简单说法。

column1: Ask a name with "이름이 뭐예요?" and age with "몇 살이에요?".
column2: 问名字用 "이름이 뭐예요?"，问年龄用 "몇 살이에요?"。

column1: 씨 goes only after other people's names. Don't use it with your own name.
column2: 씨 只用在别人的名字后面，不要用在自己的名字后面。

column1: For age, add "살", like "스무 살 (20 years old), 서른 살 (30 years old)".
column2: 说年龄要加 "살"，如 "스무 살 (20岁)、서른 살 (30岁)"。

column1: to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
column2: 给 (주세요 = 请给我 / 请做)

column1: How old is your younger brother or sister?
Easy words for saying which country you are from and which language you speak.
column2: 说自己是哪国人、说什么语言的简单说法。

column1: Answer "어느 나라 사람이에요?" with "미얀마 사람이에요" (I'm from Myanmar).
column2: 回答 "어느 나라 사람이에요?" 用 "미얀마 사람이에요" (我是缅甸人)。

column1: Add "사람" after a country name = a person from that country; add "어" = that country's language: 한국 사람 (Korean person), 한국어 (Korean language).
column2: 国名后加 "사람" = 那个国家的人；加 "어" = 那个国家的语言：한국 사람 (韩国人)、한국어 (韩语)。

column1: It's my first time in Korea.
to try, to have done (-아/어 보다)
Words for answering and for when you didn't understand. These are the most needed words when you start somewhere new.
column2: 回答时的说法，以及没听懂时的说法。这是刚到一个新地方时最需要的话。

column1: If you don't understand, say "다시 말해 주세요"; if you understand, say "알겠습니다".
column2: 听不懂时说 "다시 말해 주세요"，听懂了说 "알겠습니다"。

column1: If you say "네" when you didn't understand, there can be problems in class or at your part-time job. If you don't understand, always ask again.
column2: 没听懂却说 "네"，在课堂或打工时可能会出问题。听不懂一定要再问。

column1: If someone speaks fast, ask: "천천히 말해 주세요" (Please speak slowly).
column2: 对方说得快时，请说 "천천히 말해 주세요" (请说慢一点)。

column1: to be right, to be correct
to know (알겠어요 = I understand, got it)
column2: 知道 (알겠어요 = 我明白了，知道了)

column1: to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
Got it. I'll do it right away.
I don't know, I don't understand
I'm sorry, but please say it again.
to know (알겠습니다 = I understand, got it)
Easy words for saying how you feel in one word.
column2: 用一句话说心情或感受的简单说法。

column1: Say your feelings in one word, like "좋아요", "피곤해요". If your voice goes up at the end, it is a question.
column2: 用一个词说感受，如 "좋아요"、"피곤해요"。句尾语调上扬就是问句。

column1: Put "정말 (really)", "너무 (so, too)" or "조금 (a little)" in front to say how strong the feeling is.
column2: 在前面加 "정말 (真)"、"너무 (太)"、"조금 (有点)" 来表示感受的程度。

column1: Raise your voice at the end to make it a question: "피곤해요?" (Are you tired?), "맛있어요?" (Is it delicious?).
column2: 句尾语调上扬就变成问句："피곤해요?" (累吗?)、"맛있어요?" (好吃吗?)。

column1: I bought my friend some juice.
I drink milk in the morning.
Check the expiration date on the milk.
column2: 请确认一下牛奶的保质期。

column1: The drinks are in the fridge.
Drinks are buy one, get one free.
I eat bread in the morning.
I bought bread for breakfast at the bakery.
column2: 我在面包店买了早餐吃的面包。
我弟弟/妹妹喜欢吃零食。

column1: We share snacks during the break.
column2: 课间休息时我们一起分零食吃。

column1: I drink a cup of coffee.
Coffee from the vending machine is 300 won.
column2: 自动售货机的咖啡是300韩元。

column1: Please have a cup of tea.
Please give the guest some tea.
Let's have a beer after the exam.
column2: 考完试我们喝杯啤酒吧。

column1: If you can't drink soju at the after-party, have a soda.
column2: 聚餐后的续摊上如果不能喝烧酒，就喝汽水吧。

column1: Words for calling the staff and ordering food at a Korean restaurant.
column2: 在韩国餐厅叫服务员和点菜时用的话。

column1: At a restaurant, call the staff with "여기요" and order with "~ 주세요".
column2: 在餐厅用 "여기요" 叫服务员，用 "~ 주세요" 点菜。

column1: To call the staff, say "여기요" or "저기요". It is not rude to raise your hand and call a little loudly.
column2: 叫服务员时说 "여기요" 或 "저기요"。举手稍微大声叫也不算失礼。

column1: Unlike English, the number and the counter come after the food name. And "주세요" comes at the very end.
column2: 和中文不同，数量和量词放在食物名称的后面。而且 "주세요" 放在最后。

column1: Order grilled meat by "인분" (servings). Many restaurants take orders from 2 인분.
column2: 烤肉按 "인분" (份) 点。很多店从 2 인분 起点。

column1: Two servings of samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), please.
column2: 请给我两份五花肉 (samgyeopsal，烤五花肉)。

column1: How much is one serving of bulgogi?
You can order meat from two servings.

column2: 您是在这里吃还是打包？

column1: Can I take the leftovers home?
This restaurant has a lot of dishes.
Do you have an English menu?
Could I have more side dishes?
column2: 可以再给我一些小菜吗？

column1: One more bowl of rice, please.
Please put your dishes at the return counter.
Excuse me, I'd like to order.
Excuse me, a wet towel, please.
Two servings of samgyeopsal and one soybean paste stew (된장찌개), please.
column2: 请给我两份五花肉和一份大酱汤 (된장찌개)。

column1: Words for the taste and temperature of food.
column2: 描述食物味道和温度的词。

column1: To ask about taste, say "맛이 어때요?".
In "맵다, 싱겁다, 뜨겁다, 차갑다", ㅂ changes to "우": 매워요, 싱거워요, 뜨거워요, 차가워요.
column2: 在 "맵다, 싱겁다, 뜨겁다, 차갑다" 中，ㅂ 变成 "우"：매워요, 싱거워요, 뜨거워요, 차가워요。

column1: If you can't eat spicy food, say "안 맵게 해 주세요" (Please make it not spicy).
column2: 如果不能吃辣，就说 "안 맵게 해 주세요" (请做成不辣的)。

column1: Use "덥다" for hot weather and "뜨겁다" for hot food or things. English uses "hot" for both.
column2: 天气热用 "덥다"，食物或东西烫用 "뜨겁다"。中文两种都可以说 "热"，但韩语要区分。

column1: The milk went bad, so it tastes sour.
column2: 牛奶坏了，所以味道发酸。

column1: Even if the medicine is bitter, be sure to take it.
The soup is hot. Be careful.
The clay pot is hot, so don't touch it.
Cold drinks are in the fridge.
I can't eat spicy food. Please make it not spicy.
column2: 我不能吃辣。请做成不辣的。

column1: The school cafeteria food is good.
The food got cold, so it's not tasty.
If it's not tasty, you can leave it.
The soup is a little salty.
Eating salty food is not good.
Eating a lot of salty food is bad for your health.
column2: 吃太多咸的食物对健康不好。

column1: It's a little bland for me.
It's delicious. But it's a little spicy.
Words for paying at a restaurant or shop.
column2: 在餐厅或商店付钱时用的话。

column1: Say "계산해 주세요" and pay by card or in cash.
column2: 说 "계산해 주세요"，然后用卡或现金付款。

column1: At Korean restaurants, you don't pay at the table. You pay at the counter when you leave.
column2: 在韩国餐厅不在座位上结账，而是离开时在收银台付款。

column1: There is no tipping in Korea. Tax is included in the price.
column2: 韩国没有小费。价格里已经包含了税。

column1: If an older person says "내가 살게" (I'll pay), say "잘 먹었습니다" (Thank you for the meal).
column2: 如果长辈说 "내가 살게" (我请客)，就说 "잘 먹었습니다" (谢谢款待) 表示感谢。

column1: Can I pay with a transportation card too?
Is there a discount if I pay in cash?
I'll hand it in to the department office, so please give me a receipt.
column2: 我要交给系办公室，请给我收据。

column1: One bill for all of us, please.
How much is it for the two of us?
column2: 我们两个人一共多少钱？

column1: The bill, please. How much is it in total?
Words for ordering food to your home or dormitory.
column2: 把食物叫到家里或宿舍时用的话。

column1: For delivery, give your address and use "시키다".
Fried chicken is counted with "마리": 한 마리 (one whole), 반 마리 (half).
column2: 炸鸡用 "마리" 来数：한 마리 (一整只)，반 마리 (半只)。

column1: Addresses go from the biggest place: city, district, neighborhood, building name, room number.
column2: 地址从大的地方开始说：市、区、洞、楼名、房间号。

column1: At a restaurant people say "주문하다"; for delivery or in casual speech, "시키다" is common.
column2: 在餐厅点菜说 "주문하다"；叫外卖或口语中常说 "시키다"。

column1: Do you deliver to the dormitory?
I'm studying for an exam, so I'm ordering dinner.
column2: 我在准备考试，所以叫外卖当晚饭。

column1: When the delivery arrives, please leave it at the door.
I changed the delivery address to the dormitory.
column2: 我把外卖地址改成了宿舍。

column1: If you order more than 20,000 won, there is no delivery fee.
column2: 点满20,000韩元以上免配送费。

column1: I order with a delivery app.
I choose the food on the delivery app.
I registered my card on the delivery app.
column2: 我在外卖软件上绑定了银行卡。

column1: Four of us shared one chicken.
column2: 我们四个人分吃了一只炸鸡。

column1: Room 203 at the Hanguk Electronics dormitory. One fried chicken, please.
column2: 韩国电子宿舍203号。请给我一只炸鸡。

column1: Names of meat, fish and other protein foods we often eat.
column2: 肉、鱼等常吃的蛋白质食物的名称。

column1: Make the names of meats with "animal name + 고기".
column2: 用 "动物名称 + 고기" 来组成肉的名称。

column1: Put "고기" after the animal name: 돼지 (pig) + 고기 (meat) = 돼지고기 (pork). English uses special words like "pork" and "beef", but Korean just joins the two words.
column2: 在动物名称后面加 "고기"：돼지 (猪) + 고기 (肉) = 돼지고기 (猪肉)。这和中文 "猪 + 肉 = 猪肉" 的构词方式一样。

column1: A live fish is "물고기", and fish as food is "생선". English uses "fish" for both.
column2: 活鱼叫 "물고기"，作为食物的鱼叫 "생선"。中文两种都叫 "鱼"。

column1: 달걀 and "계란" mean the same thing (egg).
column2: 달걀 和 "계란" 意思一样 (鸡蛋)。

column1: One geun (600 g) of beef for soup, please.
column2: 请给我一斤 (600克) 煮汤用的牛肉。

column1: Do you sell halal chicken too?
Did this fish come in today?
column2: 这条鱼是今天进的货吗？

column1: One geun (600 g) of pork, please.
column2: 请给我一斤 (600克) 猪肉。

column1: Cook pork well before you eat it.
How much is a tray of eggs?
I put tofu in the stew.
Keep tofu in water and put it in the fridge.
column2: 豆腐要泡在水里放进冰箱。

column1: Is there any food you can't eat?
I don't eat beef. But I like chicken.
column2: 我不吃牛肉。但我喜欢鸡肉。

column1: Names of seasonings used in Korean food. You need them when you cook or work part-time in a restaurant kitchen.
column2: 韩国菜用的调料名称。做饭或在餐厅后厨打工时都需要。

column1: 간장, 고추장 and 된장 are the three basic seasonings of Korean food.
column2: 간장、고추장 和 된장 是韩国菜的三种基本调料。

column1: The basic seasonings of Korean food are 간장, 고추장 and 된장. They are made from fermented soybeans.
column2: 韩国菜的基本调料是 간장、고추장 和 된장。它们都是用发酵的大豆做的。

column1: Korean dishes rarely use fish sauce for taste. They use 간장 or 소금 instead.
column2: 韩国菜很少用鱼露调味，而是用 간장 或 소금。

column1: Put some oil in the pan.
to spread around (oil in a pan)
We are out of cooking oil.
Do not pour cooking oil down the drain.
column2: 不要把食用油倒进下水道。

column1: I put in too much salt.
I put sugar in my coffee.
No sugar in my coffee, please.
I add a little soy sauce.
Please go and buy a bottle of soy sauce.
Gochujang is on sale at the supermarket.
I put in a lot of garlic.
Pakistani food also uses a lot of garlic.
column2: 巴基斯坦菜也用很多大蒜。

column1: It tastes good with green onions.
I put green onions in my ramyeon.
Sam, please bring some garlic and green onions.
column2: 山姆，请拿点大蒜和葱来。

column1: Okay, shall I bring the soy sauce too?
Verbs for how to cook food.
썰다, 끓이다, 볶다, 굽다, 튀기다 are the basic cooking verbs.
column2: 썰다、끓이다、볶다、굽다、튀기다 是基本的烹饪动词。

column1: Use "끓이다" for soup or ramyeon, and "삶다" for cooking eggs or noodles in water. English uses "boil" for both.
column2: 煮汤或拉面用 "끓이다"，在水里煮鸡蛋或面条用 "삶다"。中文两种都可以说 "煮"。

column1: Boil tap water before you drink it.
I made fried rice with leftover rice.
When you deep-fry, it is dangerous if water gets in.
Do not grill meat in the dormitory.
Add red pepper powder to the soup.
Mix bibimbap well before you eat it.
Be careful with your hands when you cut with a knife.
Slice the onion and stir-fry it with the meat.
column2: 把洋葱切好，和肉一起炒。

column1: When do I add the soy sauce?
Add it at the end and mix well.
Basic words about places to shop and buying things.
column2: 关于购物地点和买东西的基本词汇。

column1: To look for something, say "~ 있어요?"; to see it, say "보여 주세요".
column2: 找东西时说 "~ 있어요?"；想看时说 "보여 주세요"。

column1: When you look for something, ask "~ 있어요?". If they don't have it, they say "없어요".
column2: 找东西时问 "~ 있어요?"。如果没有，对方会说 "없어요"。

column1: Korean convenience stores are open 24 hours and also take parcels and bill payments.
column2: 韩国的便利店24小时营业，还可以寄快递、交水电费等。

column1: There are a lot of things for sale.
Please put the things I bought in a bag.
column2: 请把我买的东西放进袋子里。

column1: The market is cheap and good.
I buy vegetables at the market.
The market sells things cheaper in the evening.
I go to the supermarket on the weekend.
I bought rice at the supermarket.
I collect points at the supermarket.
I buy water at the convenience store.
Convenience stores are open at night too.
You can also send parcels at a convenience store.
column2: 在便利店也可以寄快递。

column1: What time does the store open?
Is there an Asian food store nearby?
I need to buy a phone charger.
Do you sell fruit here too?
Do you sell SIM cards here too?
Please put it in a bag.
Please show me other colors too.
Please show me the cheapest one.
Welcome. What are you looking for?
Words for talking about prices and asking for a discount.
column2: 谈论价格和讲价时用的话。

column1: If it's expensive, say "비싸요"; if you want a discount, say "깎아 주세요".
column2: 贵的话说 "비싸요"；想讲价就说 "깎아 주세요"。

column1: At supermarkets, convenience stores and department stores, you don't bargain. You can say "깎아 주세요" only at markets.
column2: 在超市、便利店和百货商店不讲价。只有在市场才可以说 "깎아 주세요"。

column1: 일 더하기 일 (1+1) means buy one, get one free.
column2: 일 더하기 일 (1+1) 是买一送一的意思。

column1: There is no price tag. How much is it?
It was more expensive than I thought, so I didn't buy it.
Do you have a cheap one?

column2: 员工可以享受九折优惠。

column1: It was on sale, so I bought it cheaply.
column2: 因为打折，我买得很便宜。

column1: I'm buying a lot, so please give me a discount.
I'll buy two. Please give me a small discount.
column2: 我买两个。请便宜一点吧。

column1: That's expensive. Please take a little off.
column2: 太贵了。请稍微便宜一点。

column1: Then I'll give you one more.
Names of clothes, shoes and things you wear.
column2: 衣服、鞋子等穿戴物品的名称。

column1: You 입다 clothes, 신다 shoes and 쓰다 a hat.
column2: 衣服用 입다，鞋子用 신다，帽子用 쓰다。

column1: English uses "wear" or "put on" for everything, but in Korean the verb depends on the body part: clothes "입다", shoes and socks "신다", hats and glasses "쓰다", gloves "끼다".
column2: 中文用 "穿" 和 "戴"，而韩语的动词根据身体部位而不同：衣服 "입다"，鞋和袜子 "신다"，帽子和眼镜 "쓰다"，手套 "끼다"。

column1: In Korean homes and some restaurants, you take off your shoes before you go in.
column2: 在韩国家里和一些餐厅，要脱鞋才能进去。

column1: I wear pants more often than skirts.
column2: 比起裙子，我更常穿裤子。

column1: You must take off your shoes inside the dorm.
I wear thick socks in winter.
I carry a bag on my back.
to carry on the shoulder or back
Please put your bag in the locker.
I bought clothes to wear on my trip.
column2: 我买了旅行时穿的衣服。

column1: You stand for a long time, so comfortable sneakers are good.
column2: 要站很久，所以舒服的运动鞋比较好。

column1: The hat looks good on you.
to suit, to look good on
The sun is strong, so wear a hat.
May I try on the pants?
column2: 我可以试穿一下裤子吗？

column1: I buy several T-shirts in summer.
It's cold, so wear a jacket.

column2: 不要把衣服长时间放在洗衣房。

column1: It's warm when you turn on the heating.
If the heating breaks, tell the manager.
column2: 暖气坏了请告诉管理员。

column1: to come out, to happen (열이 나다 = to have a fever)
column2: 出现，发生 (열이 나다 = 发烧)

column1: Please turn on the air conditioning.
The air conditioning is too strong.
If the air conditioning is too strong, you'll catch a cold.
Put shared things back in their place.
column2: 共用的东西请放回原处。

column1: The shower room is at the end of the hallway.
There is no hot water in the shower room.
The shower room is crowded in the morning.
My roommate is sleeping, so I'm quiet.
column2: 室友在睡觉，所以我很安静。

column1: It's exam period, so please be quiet at night too.
column2: 现在是考试期间，晚上也请保持安静。

column1: The heating in my room doesn't work.
Words for finding a room and signing a contract. In Korea there is a large sum of money called "보증금".
column2: 找房和签合同时会遇到的词。韩国有一笔叫 "보증금" 的大额押金。

column1: When you look for a room, ask about the 보증금, 월세 and 관리비.
column2: 找房时要问清楚 보증금、월세 和 관리비。

column1: A 보증금 is money you leave when you move in and get back when you move out. Sometimes it is more than ten times the monthly rent.
column2: 보증금 是入住时交、搬走时退还的钱。有时会超过月租的十倍。

column1: Be sure to get a copy of the contract and keep it. If there are words you don't understand, ask before you sign.
column2: 一定要拿到合同并保管好。有不懂的词，签字前要问清楚。

column1: I asked the landlord to repair it.
to look for (a room, a job)
How much is the monthly rent for a studio?
column2: 单间公寓的月租是多少？

column1: Studios near the station are expensive.
column2: 车站附近的单间公寓很贵。

column1: How much is the monthly rent?
I pay the rent by the 5th of every month.
You get the deposit back when you move out.
When you move, you must report your new address.
column2: 搬家后必须申报新地址。

column1: Be sure to see the room before you sign the contract.
Is the internet included in the maintenance fee?
In winter, the maintenance fee is high.
How much is the monthly rent for this studio?
column2: 这个单间公寓的月租是多少？

column1: The deposit is 3,000,000 won and the monthly rent is 350,000 won.
Is there a maintenance fee too?
Names of things you use every day. These are the first things to buy when you arrive in Korea.
column2: 每天使用的物品名称。这些是刚到韩国时最先要买的东西。

column1: When something is all used up, say "떨어졌어요".
When something is all used up, say "떨어졌어요": 휴지가 떨어졌어요 (The toilet paper has run out).
column2: 东西用完了时说 "떨어졌어요"：휴지가 떨어졌어요 (卫生纸用完了)。

column1: In Korea, you throw toilet paper into the toilet. People also give toilet paper as a housewarming gift.
column2: 在韩国，卫生纸要扔进马桶。人们也会送卫生纸作为乔迁礼物。

column1: I dry myself with a towel.
I wash my hands with soap.
The hand soap has run out.
I bought shampoo and conditioner together.
column2: 我把洗发水和护发素一起买了。

column1: Toothpaste and toothbrushes are cheap at Daiso.
column2: 牙膏和牙刷在大创买很便宜。

column1: Pack your toothbrush when you go on a business trip.
The toilet paper has run out.
There is no toilet paper in the bathroom.

column2: 我需要一床冬天的被子。

column1: Please give me one more pillow.
The pillow is hard, so my neck hurts.
Put in only a little detergent.
The detergent in the laundry room has run out.
column2: 洗衣房的洗衣液用完了。

column1: I'm going to the supermarket. Do you need anything?
column2: 我去超市。你需要什么吗？

column1: Please buy me some toothpaste and toilet paper.
column2: 请帮我买点牙膏和卫生纸。

column1: Names of parts of the body. You need them when you are sick or hurt.
column2: 身体各部位的名称。生病或受伤时一定要用到。

column1: Say where it hurts with "body part + 이/가 아파요".
column2: 用 "身体部位 + 이/가 아파요" 说哪里疼。

column1: Say where it hurts with "~이/가 아파요". The order is the same as English: "My head hurts" = 머리가 아파요.
column2: 用 "~이/가 아파요" 说哪里疼。语序和中文一样："头疼" = 머리가 아파요。

column1: 머리 has two meanings: head and hair. 머리를 감다 (to wash your hair), 머리를 자르다 (to get a haircut).
column2: 머리 有两个意思：头和头发。머리를 감다 (洗头)，머리를 자르다 (剪头发)。

column1: 눈 (eye, snow), 배 (stomach, boat, pear) and 다리 (leg, bridge) have more than one meaning.
column2: 눈 (眼睛，雪)、배 (肚子，船，梨) 和 다리 (腿，桥) 都有好几个意思。

column1: I got dust in my eye.
If the smell is strong, cover your nose with a mask.
column2: 气味太重的话，请用口罩遮住鼻子。

column1: I have sores in my mouth, so I can't eat.
column2: 我嘴里长溃疡了，吃不了饭。

column1: My roommate snores, so I wear earplugs.
column2: 我室友打呼噜，所以我戴耳塞。

column1: to be dry (목이 마르다 = to be thirsty)
My throat hurts, so I can't talk.
I put a pain relief patch on my shoulder.
I wash my hands before I eat.
I have a stomachache, so I go to the bathroom often.
column2: 我肚子疼，所以经常去厕所。

column1: I lifted something heavy and hurt my back.
Be careful of your back when you lift things.
My leg hurts, so I can't walk.
I stood for a long time, so my legs are swollen.
Something heavy fell on my foot.
Expressions for saying how you feel sick.
column2: 说明身体哪里不舒服的表达。

column1: For symptoms, say "~이/가 나다"; for illnesses, say "~에 걸리다".
column2: 症状用 "~이/가 나다"，疾病用 "~에 걸리다"。

column1: Symptoms often use "나다": 열이 나다, 콧물이 나다, 피가 나다. It means something comes out of the body.
column2: 症状常用 "나다"：열이 나다 (发烧)、콧물이 나다 (流鼻涕)、피가 나다 (流血)。意思是有东西从身体里出来。

column1: Use "걸리다" for illnesses. Even if you are still sick now, use the past form "걸렸어요".
column2: 疾病用 "걸리다"。即使现在还病着，也用过去式 "걸렸어요"。

column1: If you're sick, don't put up with it. Tell your professor "몸이 안 좋아요" (I don't feel well).
column2: 生病了不要硬撑，要跟教授说 "몸이 안 좋아요" (我身体不舒服)。
我从昨天开始就不舒服。

column1: If you're sick, don't just put up with it. Tell someone.
column2: 生病了不要硬撑，要跟别人说。

column1: to put up with, to hold back
Be careful not to catch a cold.
I caught a cold, so I can't go to class today.
column2: 我感冒了，今天不能去上课。

column1: I had a fever at night.
If you have a fever, don't go to school. Go to the hospital.
column2: 发烧的话不要去学校，去医院吧。

column1: I studied a lot for the exam, so I'm tired.
column2: 我为了考试学了很多，所以很累。

column1: I ate bad food and got an upset stomach.
column2: 我吃了变质的食物，闹肚子了。

column1: I had an upset stomach, so I ate rice porridge.
I caught a cold, so I have a runny nose.
If you have a runny nose, wear a mask.
I coughed at night, so I couldn't sleep.
Cover your mouth when you cough.
If you feel dizzy, sit down.
I walked for a long time on a hot day, so I feel dizzy.
column2: 我在大热天走了很久，头很晕。

column1: I think I'm going to throw up.
I ate bad food and threw up.
column2: 我吃了变质的食物，吐了。

column1: Sam, you don't look well. Are you sick?
column2: 山姆，你脸色不太好。哪里不舒服吗？

column1: I caught a cold. I have a fever and a cough.
Words you hear when you check in and see a doctor at a hospital.
column2: 在医院挂号和看病时听到的词。

column1: At the hospital, the order is: check in, see the doctor, pay.
column2: 在医院的顺序是：挂号、看病、付费。

column1: When you go to the hospital, take your alien registration card and health insurance card.
column2: 去医院时请带上外国人登录证和医保卡。

column1: In Korea, if you are not very sick, you go to a local clinic first, not a big hospital. Clinics are divided by the part that hurts, such as 내과 (internal medicine), 정형외과 (orthopedics, bones) and 치과 (dentist).
column2: 在韩国，如果病得不重，先去社区诊所，而不是大医院。诊所按疼的部位分科，比如 내과 (内科)、정형외과 (骨科) 和 치과 (牙科)。

column1: For shots, use "맞다": 주사를 맞다 (to get a shot).
I have to go to the hospital.
I saw a doctor at the hospital.
Take your alien registration card when you go to the hospital.
column2: 去医院时请带上外国人登录证。

column1: Show the doctor where it hurts.
column2: 请给医生看看疼的地方。

column1: The nurse checked my blood pressure.
Show your health insurance card when you check in.
Don't eat anything tomorrow morning and come for the test.
column2: 明天早上请空腹来做检查。

column1: I was in the hospital for three days.
to be admitted to the hospital
I have to stay in the hospital for surgery.
If you are in the hospital, give a doctor's note to the school.
column2: 住院的话，要向学校提交诊断书。

column1: You have to wait to see the doctor.
On Saturdays, the clinic is open only in the morning.
If you have health insurance, hospital bills are cheap.
column2: 有医保的话，看病费用很便宜。

column1: I've had a fever and a sore throat since yesterday.
column2: 我从昨天开始发烧、喉咙疼。

column1: Please write your name here and wait.
column2: 请在这里写上名字，然后等候。

column1: Words for buying medicine at a pharmacy and hearing how to take it.
column2: 在药店买药和听服用方法时用的话。

column1: For medicine, listen carefully for "how many times a day, after meals".
column2: 买药时要仔细听 "一天几次，饭后" 等说明。

column1: You must give the prescription from the hospital to the pharmacy to get your medicine. You can buy cold medicine, headache medicine and digestive medicine without a prescription.
column2: 必须把医院开的处方交给药店才能拿药。感冒药、头疼药和消化药不用处方也能买。

column1: Use "먹다" for medicine, "바르다" for ointment and "붙이다" for patches. Even for liquid medicine, say "먹다".
column2: 吃药用 "먹다"，药膏用 "바르다"，膏药用 "붙이다"。即使是药水也说 "먹다"。

column1: 식후 means after meals, and "식전" means before meals.
column2: 식후 是饭后，"식전" 是饭前。

column1: How many times a day do I take the headache medicine?
I put ointment on the cut.
Do you have ointment for burns?
The pharmacy is next to the hospital.
Is there a pharmacy open on Sunday?
column2: 有星期天开门的药店吗？

column1: Take this medicine 30 minutes after meals.
column2: 这个药请饭后30分钟服用。

column1: Please give me some digestive medicine.
I took digestive medicine, so I'm OK now.
column2: 吃了消化药，现在没事了。

column1: I ate too much, so I bought digestive medicine.
column2: 我吃多了，所以买了消化药。

column1: Take this medicine twice a day.
Will this medicine make me sleepy?
Take it three times a day.
Take it three times a day after meals.
Take it three times a day for three days.
column2: 请一天三次，连续服用三天。

column1: You can't buy this medicine without a prescription.
column2: 没有处方买不了这种药。

column1: Give your prescription to the pharmacy and get your medicine.
column2: 把处方交给药店，然后拿药。

column1: Take this medicine three times a day, after meals.
column2: 这个药一天三次，饭后服用。

column1: For how many days do I take it?
Words for saying how you got hurt. If you get hurt, you must tell someone near you right away.
column2: 说明受伤原因的词。受伤后必须马上告诉周围的人。

column1: If you get hurt, tell someone right away. In an emergency, call 119.
column2: 受伤了要马上告诉别人。紧急情况拨打119。

column1: In an emergency, call 119. Say "여기 사람이 다쳤어요" (Someone is hurt here) and give the address.
column2: 紧急情况请拨打119。说 "여기 사람이 다쳤어요" (这里有人受伤了)，然后说地址。

column1: If you get hurt at your part-time job, tell the owner even if it's a small cut. Part-time workers can also get treatment with industrial accident insurance (산재 보험).
column2: 打工时受伤，哪怕只是小伤口也要告诉老板。打工的人也可以用工伤保险 (산재 보험) 接受治疗。

column1: Put ice on the swollen part.
Are you tired? Take a rest.
column2: 累了吗? 休息一下吧。

column1: I've been hungry since the morning.
Are you cold? Shall I close the door?
Ask with "뭐 (what), 어디 (where), 누구 (who), 언제 (when), 얼마 (how much)" and give short answers.
column2: 用 "뭐 (什么)、어디 (哪里)、누구 (谁)、언제 (什么时候)、얼마 (多少钱)" 提问，并简短回答。

column1: Ask with "뭐, 어디, 누구, 언제, 얼마" and answer briefly.
column2: 用 "뭐、어디、누구、언제、얼마" 提问并简短回答。

column1: Raise your voice at the end of a question. Short answers are fine: "어디 가요?" (Where are you going?) "시장이요." (To the market.)
column2: 问句句尾语调上扬。简短回答也可以："어디 가요?" (去哪里?) "시장이요." (去市场。)

column1: Question words do not come at the start of the sentence like in English. They usually come just before the verb: "뭐 먹어요?" (What are you eating?).
column2: 疑问词通常放在动词前面："뭐 먹어요?" (你吃什么?)。注意中文的 "什么" 在动词后面。

column1: How much is it all together?
Words for family members. The words for older brother and sister change depending on whether the speaker is a man or a woman.
column2: 称呼家人的词。称呼哥哥姐姐的词会因说话人是男是女而不同。

column1: Men say 형 and 누나; women say 오빠 and 언니.
column2: 男性说 형 和 누나，女性说 오빠 和 언니。

column1: English has only "brother" and "sister", but Korean has four words for older siblings. A man says 형, 누나; a woman says 오빠, 언니.
column2: 中文的哥哥、姐姐不分说话人的性别，但韩语的哥哥姐姐有四个词：男性说 형、누나，女性说 오빠、언니。

column1: 동생 is used for both boys and girls. To show which, say 남동생 (younger brother) or 여동생 (younger sister).
column2: 동생 男女都可以用。要区分时说 남동생 (弟弟) 或 여동생 (妹妹)。

column1: When you become close at school, you can call older seniors or friends 형, 누나, 언니 or 오빠 even if they are not family.
column2: 在学校关系变亲近后，即使不是家人，也可以叫学长学姐或年长的朋友 형、누나、언니、오빠。

column1: It was my father's birthday, so I made a video call.
column2: 今天是父亲的生日，所以我打了视频电话。

column1: (보고 싶다 = to miss, to want to see)
My mother is a good cook.
My mother is sick, so I'm worried.
column2: 我母亲病了，所以我很担心。

column1: I send money to my parents.
I send living money to my parents every month.
column2: 我每个月给父母寄生活费。

column1: My older brother is taller than me.
My older brother wants to study in Korea too.
column2: 我哥哥也想在韩国学习。

column1: My older brother is a university student.
I told my older brother the dates of my vacation.
column2: 我告诉了哥哥我休假的日期。

column1: to let someone know, to tell
My older sister is a nurse.
My older sister sent me wedding photos.
column2: 我姐姐发来了婚礼照片。

column1: I live with my older sister.
My older sister bought me clothes.
My older sister helps me a lot with life in Korea.
column2: 姐姐在韩国生活上给了我很多帮助。

column1: My younger brother is a high school student.
I have two younger brothers and sisters.
I pay my younger sibling's school fees.
column2: 我弟弟/妹妹的学费由我来付。

column1: My grandfather is sick, so I took time off.
column2: 我爷爷病了，所以我请了假。

column1: I'm going to my grandmother's house.
I bought Korean ginseng for my grandmother.
column2: 我给奶奶买了韩国人参。

column1: How many people are in your family?
Five. I have my parents, an older sister and a younger brother.
column2: 五口人。有父母、一个姐姐和一个弟弟。

column1: Words for talking about marriage and brothers and sisters.
column2: 谈论婚姻和兄弟姐妹时用的词。

column1: Ask and answer about marriage with "결혼했어요?".
column2: 用 "결혼했어요?" 询问和回答是否结婚。

column1: 결혼했어요 is in the past form, but it means "I am married now". If you are not married yet, say "아직 안 했어요".
column2: 결혼했어요 是过去形式，但意思是 "我现在已婚"。还没结婚就说 "아직 안 했어요"。

column1: Koreans often ask if you are married, even the first time they meet you. You don't need to think it is rude.
column2: 韩国人即使第一次见面也常问你结婚了没有，不必觉得没礼貌。

column1: When do you want to get married?
My older sister got married last year.
My older brother is getting married in our hometown next year.
column2: 我哥哥明年要在老家结婚。

column1: My older sister came to Korea with her husband.
column2: 我姐姐和她丈夫一起来了韩国。

column1: My older sister is preparing her husband's visa documents.
column2: 我姐姐在准备她丈夫的签证材料。

column1: My friend's wife is a good cook.
column2: 我朋友的妻子很会做饭。

column1: My senior's wife is in Nepal.
column2: 我学长的妻子在尼泊尔。

column1: Someday I want to travel the world with my wife.
column2: 以后我想和妻子去环游世界。

column1: I'm the youngest son in my family.
My parents have only two sons.
My aunt's daughter goes to high school.
column2: 我阿姨的女儿在上高中。

column1: I'm an only daughter, so my parents worry a lot.
column2: 我是独生女，所以父母很担心我。

column1: Do you have any brothers or sisters?
I miss my brothers and sisters back home.
column2: 我想念老家的兄弟姐妹。

column1: I have no brothers or sisters. I'm an only child.
column2: 我没有兄弟姐妹，我是独生子女。

column1: to not have, to not be (there)
how many people in the family
There are four people in my family.
Write on the form how many people are in your family.
column2: 请在表格上写家里有几口人。

column1: Sam, do you have any brothers or sisters?
Yes, I have one younger sister.
You must miss your younger sister.
Words for describing how people look.
For a person's height, use "크다, 작다".
In English you just say "tall", but Korean says "키가 크다", with the word "키" (height). "높다" (high) is not used for people.
column2: 和中文的 "个子高" 一样，韩语说 "키가 크다"，要加 "키" (个子)。说人不用 "높다" (高)。

column1: 잘생겼어요 and "닮았어요" use the past form to talk about how someone looks now.
column2: 잘생겼어요、"닮았어요" 用过去形式来说一个人现在的样子。

column1: I got slimmer because I exercise these days.
The man in the photo is handsome.
The tall person is the teaching assistant.
column2: 个子高的那个人是助教。

column1: The tall person tidies the top shelf.
column2: 个子高的人整理上层的架子。

column1: I'm short, so I can't reach the top of the shelf.
column2: 我个子矮，所以够不到架子上面。

column1: My older sister and I look very alike.
My younger sibling looks a lot like me.
column2: 我弟弟/妹妹长得很像我。

column1: My older sister has long hair.
My hair is long, so I tie it up.
If your hair is long, tie it up when you cook.
column2: 如果头发长，做饭时请扎起来。

column1: What does your younger brother look like?
He is tall and has short hair. He looks like me.
column2: 他个子高，头发短，长得像我。

column1: Words for describing a person's character. You hear them when people introduce friends or professors at school.
column2: 描述人性格的词。在学校介绍朋友或教授时常会听到。
很多描述性格的词以 "-하다" 结尾。

column1: At Korean schools and part-time jobs, the best praise is "성실하다" and "부지런하다".

I booked a table at a restaurant.
You make an appointment at the immigration office online.
column2: 出入境管理事务所要在网上预约。

column1: I'm going on a trip to Jeonju.
I'm going on a trip to Seoul during my vacation.
I want to visit an old palace.
I saw the sea for the first time.
At the beach, be careful of no-swimming areas.
column2: 在海边请注意禁止游泳区域。

column1: There are many mountains in Korea.
You must not make a fire in the mountains.
This neighborhood is famous for galbi (ribs).
I go to places with nice views.
We took a family photo at a place with a nice view.
column2: 我们在风景好的地方拍了全家福。

column1: No, not yet. I want to see the Hanok Village.
column2: 没有，还没去过。我想去看看韩屋村。

column1: Jeonju is famous for bibimbap. The scenery is nice too.
column2: 全州的拌饭很有名。风景也很好。

column1: Words for going to see a movie or a show.
column2: 去看电影或演出时用的词。

column1: For tickets, use "예매"; for restaurants and rooms, use "예약하다".
Count tickets and paper with "장": 표 한 장, 표 두 장.
column2: 票和纸用 "장" 来数：표 한 장 (一张票)，표 두 장 (两张票)。

column1: For restaurants or hotels, say "예약"; for movie or train tickets, say "예매".
column2: 餐厅或酒店说 "예약"；电影票或火车票说 "예매"。

column1: If you learn Korean with Korean dramas and songs, your listening improves quickly.
column2: 用韩剧和韩国歌曲学韩语，听力会提高得很快。

column1: I booked a train ticket in advance.
Book your holiday train tickets early.
column2: 节日的火车票请提前预订。

column1: Let's meet at the movie theater.
There are many people at the movie theater.
Please turn off your phone in the movie theater.
I watch Korean dramas during breaks.
The museum is closed on Mondays.
The museum is free for foreigners too.
column2: 博物馆对外国人也免费。

column1: If you buy tickets on the app, you get a discount.
Do you have a favorite singer?
An American singer is performing in Korea.
column2: 一位美国歌手在韩国演出。

column1: There is a free show in front of City Hall.
column2: 市政府前面有免费演出。

column1: Shall we see a movie on Saturday?
column2: 星期六我们去看电影吧？

column1: Sounds good. I'll book the tickets.
Please get seats in the back.
Words for setting a time and place to meet.
column2: 约定见面时间和地点时用的话。
用 "언제, 어디에서 만날까요?" 约时间地点。

column1: Question words don't come at the start of the sentence like in English. They come before the verb: "When do we meet?" = 언제 만나요?
column2: 疑问词不放在句首，而是放在动词前面，这一点和中文一样："我们什么时候见面？" = 언제 만나요?

column1: Use "-(으)ㄹ까요?" to suggest doing something together. The answer is "네, 좋아요" (Yes, sounds good).
column2: 提议一起做某事时用 "-(으)ㄹ까요?"。回答是 "네, 좋아요" (好啊)。

column1: In Korea, people are on time for appointments. If you might be late, contact them in advance.
column2: 在韩国，人们很守时。如果可能迟到，要提前联系。

column1: Where is a good place for you to meet?
If you will be late, contact them in advance.
column2: 如果约好的时间会迟到，请提前联系。

column1: Let's meet at the station after class.
column2: 下课后我们在车站见吧。

column1: to have time, to be free
Do you have a minute at lunchtime?
Do you want to go grocery shopping together?
I'll wait in front of the station.
I'll call you when I arrive, so please wait.
column2: 我到了会给你打电话，请等我。

column1: Are you free on Saturday? Let's have dinner together.
column2: 星期六你有空吗？我们一起吃晚饭吧。

column1: Sounds good. When and where shall we meet?
column2: 好啊。什么时候、在哪里见面？

column1: Let's meet at six in front of City Hall Station.
column2: 六点在市政府站前面见吧。

column1: Words for inviting people and visiting someone's home.
column2: 邀请别人和去别人家拜访时用的词。

column1: When you are invited, say "초대해 주셔서 감사합니다" and bring a small gift.
column2: 被邀请时说 "초대해 주셔서 감사합니다"，并带上一份小礼物。

column1: When you are invited to a Korean home, don't go empty-handed. Bring something like fruit, drinks or toilet paper.
column2: 被邀请去韩国人家里时不要空手去。可以带水果、饮料或卫生纸之类的东西。

column1: For a housewarming, people give toilet paper or detergent. It means "may everything go smoothly."
column2: 乔迁宴上人们会送卫生纸或洗衣液。寓意 "一切顺顺利利"。

column1: In Korea, people eat seaweed soup on their birthday.
column2: 在韩国，人们过生日时喝海带汤。

column1: I bought detergent as a housewarming gift.
column2: 我买了洗衣液作为乔迁礼物。

column1: Guests are coming, so I'm preparing food.
column2: 有客人要来，所以我在准备食物。

column1: I buy a cake for my classmate's birthday.
column2: 同系朋友过生日，我买蛋糕。

column1: I'm having a housewarming party on Saturday.
I'm bringing toilet paper to the housewarming party.
column2: 我买卫生纸带去乔迁宴。

column1: I invited my roommate and friends to my housewarming party.
column2: 我邀请了室友和朋友们来我的乔迁宴。

column1: I invited a friend to my home.
The professor invited me to dinner.
Thank you for inviting me to the party.
column2: 谢谢你邀请我参加派对。

column1: They threw me a farewell party.
We're having a housewarming at my place on Saturday. Can you come?
column2: 星期六在我家办乔迁宴。你能来吗？

column1: Yes, thank you for inviting me. What should I bring?
column2: 能，谢谢你邀请我。我该带点什么？

column1: Words for saying no to plans or changing them. It is important to say it softly.
column2: 拒绝或改约时用的话。说得委婉很重要。

column1: Say no softly with "미안하지만 + reason + 다음에".
column2: 用 "미안하지만 + 理由 + 다음에" 委婉地拒绝。

column1: In Korean, people don't say no directly, like "싫어요" or "안 가요". Start with "미안하지만" or "죄송하지만" and give a reason.
column2: 在韩语中，人们不会直接说 "싫어요"、"안 가요" 来拒绝。要用 "미안하지만" 或 "죄송하지만" 开头，然后说明理由。

column1: Using "-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요" sounds softer: 못 갈 것 같아요 (I don't think I can go).
column2: 用 "-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요" 听起来更委婉：못 갈 것 같아요 (我恐怕去不了)。

column1: With older people or professors, use "죄송하지만" instead of "미안하지만".
column2: 对长辈或教授要用 "죄송하지만" 代替 "미안하지만"。

column1: I'm tired today. See you next time.
I want to cancel my reservation.
I called to cancel my hospital appointment.
column2: 我打电话想取消医院的预约。

column1: We put off our group meeting until tomorrow.
column2: 我们把小组会议推迟到明天了。

column1: We'll put off our plans until next week.
column2: 我们把约会推迟到下周吧。

column1: I put off my vacation until next month.
column2: 我把休假推迟到下个月了。

column1: I'm busy, so I can't go.
The library is busy during exam period.
I think I'll be about 10 minutes late.
column2: 我可能会晚到10分钟左右。

column1: There's a traffic jam, so I'll be a little late.
Sorry, but could you help me?
column2: 不好意思，能帮我一下吗？

column1: I'm sorry, but today is not OK.
I'm sorry, but I can't come to the group meeting today.
column2: 不好意思，今天的小组会议我去不了。

column1: I have something to do that day.
Something came up suddenly, so I can't go.
I have to go to the immigration office, so I can't go to my afternoon class.
column2: 我要去出入境管理事务所，所以下午的课去不了。

column1: Shall we have dinner together this evening?
I'm sorry, but I have something to do today.
Yes, let's definitely go next time.
Words for happy and sad events, like weddings, first birthday parties and funerals. People also go to the events of their seniors and TAs at school.
column2: 用于婚礼、周岁宴、葬礼等喜事和丧事的词。学长学姐或助教的这类活动大家也会一起去。

column1: At a wedding, give 축의금 and say "축하합니다".
column2: 参加婚礼要送 축의금，并说 "축하합니다"。

column1: At a wedding, you put money in a white envelope and write your name on it. It is money instead of a gift.
column2: 参加婚礼时，把钱装进白色信封里，在信封上写上自己的名字。这是代替礼物的礼金。

column1: At a funeral, you must not say "축하합니다". Greet quietly and give money (조의금).
column2: 在葬礼上绝对不能说 "축하합니다"。要安静地致意，并送上钱 (조의금)。

column1: Korean weddings are short, about one hour. After the ceremony, guests eat and then leave.
column2: 韩国的婚礼很短，大约一个小时。仪式结束后，客人吃完饭就离开。

column1: How much wedding gift money do people give?
I put the wedding gift money in an envelope.
I gave 50,000 won as gift money at my senior's wedding.
column2: 学长的婚礼我随了50,000韩元的礼金。

column1: I gave my friend a wedding invitation.
I got a mobile wedding invitation.
I'm going to a wedding on Saturday.
Don't wear white to a wedding.
column2: 参加婚礼不要穿白色衣服。

column1: I went to the funeral hall.
People wear black to a funeral.
column2: 参加葬礼要穿黑色衣服。

column1: I went to the funeral of our TA's father.
column2: 我去参加了助教父亲的葬礼。

column1: I was invited to my professor's baby's first birthday party.
column2: 我被邀请参加教授孩子的周岁宴。

column1: At the first birthday party, the baby picked up the money.
column2: 在周岁宴上，宝宝抓了钱。

column1: People give a gold ring as a first birthday gift.
column2: 人们送金戒指作为周岁礼物。

column1: Our TA's wedding is next Saturday.
Can I go too? How much gift money do people give?
column2: 我也可以去吗？礼金给多少？

column1: Of course. People usually give about 50,000 won.
column2: 当然可以。一般给50,000韩元左右。

column1: Manners and greetings for eating in Korea. You really need them at department dinners and MT (student retreats).
column2: 在韩国吃饭时要遵守的礼仪和问候语。系里聚餐或MT (学生集体旅行) 时一定用得上。

column1: Say "잘 먹겠습니다" before eating and "잘 먹었습니다" after eating.
column2: 吃饭前说 "잘 먹겠습니다"，吃完后说 "잘 먹었습니다"。

column1: Start eating after the oldest person picks up their spoon.
column2: 等最年长的人拿起勺子后再开始吃。

column1: When you pour a drink for an older person or take one from them, use both hands. When you drink, turn your head to the side.
column2: 给长辈倒酒或接长辈倒的酒时要用双手。喝酒时把头转向一侧。

column1: If you can't drink alcohol, you can say "저는 술을 못 마십니다".
column2: 如果不能喝酒，可以说 "저는 술을 못 마십니다"。

column1: Don't lift your rice bowl while eating. Don't stick your spoon upright in the rice.
column2: 吃饭时不要端起饭碗。不要把勺子竖着插在饭里。

column1: I'll leave first. (said politely when leaving)
column2: 我先走了。(离开时礼貌地说)

column1: I start eating after the professor starts eating.
column2: 教授先动筷子后我再吃。

column1: When you eat with older people, eat slowly.
column2: 和长辈吃饭时请慢慢吃。

column1: to eat, to have a meal (polite)
I pour a drink for the professor.
Let me pour you a drink.
If you can't drink, you can just take the glass and put it down.
column2: 如果不能喝酒，可以只接过酒杯然后放下。

column1: I take the glass with both hands.
Take a glass from an older person with both hands.
column2: 长辈递来的酒杯要用双手接。

column1: Thank you for the food (said before eating)
Thank you for the food, professor.
Thank you for buying me this meal. (to an older student)
column2: 谢谢学长请客，我开动了。(对学长学姐说)

column1: Thank you, I enjoyed the meal (said after eating)
column2: 谢谢款待，我吃好了 (吃完饭后说)

column1: Thank you for the meal, Mom.
Thank you for the meal. It was delicious.
Thank you for the meal. Next time, it's my treat.
These are manners for treating older people and people above you. Some are similar to your country and some are different.
column2: 对待年长的人和地位高的人的礼仪。有些和你的国家相似，有些不同。

column1: With senior people, bow your head to greet, give things with both hands, and use polite speech.
column2: 对长辈要低头行礼，用双手递东西，并使用敬语。

column1: In Korea, instead of waving or shaking hands, people bow their head and upper body to greet. The more senior the person, the deeper you bow.
column2: 在韩国，人们不太挥手或握手，而是弯腰低头行礼。对方地位越高，鞠躬越深。

column1: When you give or take something, use both hands, or give it with your right hand while your left hand touches your right arm.
column2: 递东西或接东西时要用双手，或者用右手递的同时左手扶着右臂。

column1: The rule about not touching people's heads is not as strong as in Myanmar, but you don't touch an older person's body.
column2: 不能摸头的规矩没有缅甸那么严格，但不要碰长辈的身体。

column1: In front of senior people, "주다" becomes "드리다", "먹다" becomes "드시다", and "있다" becomes "계시다".
column2: 在长辈面前，"주다" 变成 "드리다"，"먹다" 变成 "드시다"，"있다" 变成 "계시다"。

column1: On New Year's Day, we bow to our elders.
column2: 过年时我们给长辈磕头拜年。

column1: At the wedding, they bow to their parents.
column2: 在婚礼上，他们向父母行大礼。

column1: They bow at the 폐백 (a traditional wedding ceremony).
column2: 他们在 폐백 (传统婚礼仪式) 上行大礼。

column1: The senior person sits down first.
I am polite to my seniors.
When a senior person is talking, listen until the end.
column2: 长辈说话时要听到最后。

column1: I give the documents with both hands.
I give my business card with both hands.
I gave the report with both hands.
Use polite speech with older people.
Use polite speech with people you meet for the first time.
column2: 对初次见面的人要用敬语。

column1: You must use polite speech with your professor.
I greet my professor every morning.
column2: 我每天早上向教授问好。

column1: When you meet an older person, greet them first.
When class is over, I say goodbye to the professor before I leave.
column2: 下课后我向教授道别再走。

column1: Good morning, professor. This is for you.
Thank you. Sam, you are very polite.
to be right, proper (예의가 바르다 = to be polite)
column2: 端正，正确 (예의가 바르다 = 有礼貌)

column1: Words about Korea's big holidays, Seollal and Chuseok. Schools and shops close for a few days at these times.
column2: 关于韩国两大节日春节和中秋节的词。这期间学校和商店会休息几天。

column1: People eat tteokguk at Seollal and songpyeon at Chuseok.
column2: 春节吃年糕汤，中秋节吃松饼。

column1: Seollal is the 1st day of the 1st lunar month, and Chuseok is the 15th day of the 8th lunar month. Like New Year or big holidays in many countries, the whole family gets together.
column2: 春节是农历正月初一，中秋节是农历八月十五。和很多国家的新年或重大节日一样，全家人会团聚。

column1: The New Year greeting is "새해 복 많이 받으세요" (Happy New Year).
column2: 新年问候语是 "새해 복 많이 받으세요" (新年快乐)。

column1: During the holidays, there is a lot of traffic and shops close. Buy food in advance.
column2: 节日期间路上很堵，商店也关门。要提前买好吃的。

column1: We eat tteokguk on New Year's Day.
On New Year's Day, the family gets together.
I bought a ticket home for the Lunar New Year holidays.
column2: 我买了春节假期回老家的票。

column1: I go to my hometown for Chuseok.
At Chuseok, the department handed out songpyeon.
column2: 中秋节时系里分发了松饼。

column1: My neighbor shared songpyeon with me.
When I come back from my hometown, I'll bring you a gift.
column2: 我从老家回来时给你带礼物。

column1: We hold the memorial service in the morning.
column2: 我们早上举行祭祖仪式。

column1: We hold the memorial service at Chuseok too.
We made the food for the memorial service together.
column2: 我们一起做了祭祖用的食物。

column1: I bow to my elders for the New Year.
to give a New Year's bow
When you do the New Year's bow, you get New Year's money.
column2: 拜年的话会收到压岁钱。

column1: I gave a New Year's bow to the professor and heard his good wishes.
column2: 我给教授拜了年，听了他的新年祝福。

column1: Please have a bowl of tteokguk.
When you eat tteokguk, you become one year older.
On New Year's morning, the dormitory cafeteria served tteokguk.
column2: 春节早上，宿舍食堂供应了年糕汤。

column1: to come out, to be served
What are you doing for the Chuseok holiday?
I'm resting in the dormitory. I want to go home.
column2: 我在宿舍休息。我想回家。

column1: Then come to my house and eat songpyeon with us.
column2: 那来我家一起吃松饼吧。

column1: Rules you must follow in places that many people share. If you break them, you may have to pay a fine.
column2: 在许多人共用的场所必须遵守的规则。违反的话可能要交罚款。

column1: No smoking, standing in line and recycling are rules everyone follows in Korea.
column2: 禁烟、排队和垃圾分类是在韩国人人都遵守的规则。

column1: In Korea, smoking is not allowed inside buildings, at bus stops or at subway entrances. You can smoke only in smoking areas.
column2: 在韩国，建筑物内、公交车站和地铁站入口都禁止吸烟。只能在指定的吸烟区吸烟。

column1: Trash is sorted into paper, plastic, cans, bottles, food waste and general trash.
column2: 垃圾分为纸类、塑料、易拉罐、瓶子、厨余垃圾和一般垃圾。

column1: Buses and subways have special seats for older people and pregnant women. It is better not to sit there even when they are empty.
column2: 公交车和地铁上有专门给老人和孕妇的座位。即使空着也最好不要坐。

column1: Please be quiet in the hospital.
Please be quiet on the subway.
In the library, talk quietly on the phone too.
column2: 在图书馆打电话也要小声。

column1: Separate plastic and cans for recycling.
column2: 塑料和易拉罐请分类回收。

column1: You have to pay a fine.
If you throw trash anywhere, you pay a fine.
Smoking is not allowed anywhere inside the school buildings.
column2: 学校建筑内全部禁止吸烟。

column1: Bus stops are no-smoking areas too.
Throw your trash in the trash can.
Don't throw trash on the street.
Put your trash in a pay-as-you-throw bag.
column2: 垃圾要装进计量收费垃圾袋里扔。

column1: I stand in line to get on the bus.
When you pay, line up in front of the counter.
column2: 结账时请在收银台前排队。

column1: If you jaywalk, you pay a fine.
No. This is a no-smoking area. The fine is 100,000 won.
column2: 不行。这里禁止吸烟。罚款是100,000韩元。

column1: Please smoke in the smoking area over there.
These are the six basic vowels of Hangul. When you write a vowel alone, put a silent ㅇ in front of it.
column2: 这是韩文的六个基本元音。单独写元音时，前面要加一个不发音的 ㅇ。

column1: There are six basic vowels: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ.
column2: 基本元音有六个：ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ。

column1: ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ are written to the right of the consonant, and ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ are written below it.
column2: ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ 写在辅音的右边，ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ 写在辅音的下面。

column1: For ㅓ, open your mouth a little; for ㅗ, round your lips. English has no exact ㅓ: it is between the "o" in "hot" and the "u" in "cup". ㅗ is like the "o" in "go", but without the "w" at the end.
column2: 发 ㅓ 时嘴巴稍微张开；发 ㅗ 时嘴唇要撮圆。中文里没有和 ㅓ 完全一样的音，它介于拼音 "o" 和 "e" 之间。ㅗ 有点像拼音 "o"，但嘴唇更圆，结尾不要滑向 "u"。

column1: My tooth hurts. I'm going to the dentist.
It is raining. Do you have an umbrella?
These are ㅐ and ㅔ. Today, Korean people say these two sounds almost the same way.
column2: 这是 ㅐ 和 ㅔ。现在韩国人发这两个音几乎一样。

column1: ㅐ and ㅔ sound almost the same, so we tell them apart by spelling.
column2: ㅐ 和 ㅔ 发音几乎一样，所以靠拼写来区分。

column1: Both sound like the "e" in "bed" (ㅐ used to be more open, like the "a" in "cat"). It is OK if you cannot hear the difference. Learn them by their spelling.
column2: 两个音都像拼音 "ye" 里的 "e" (ㅐ 以前开口更大)。听不出区别也没关系，按拼写记住它们。

column1: 네 is an answer (yes), and "내" means "my".
column2: 네 是回答 (是的)，"내" 是 "我的" 的意思。

column1: My stomach hurts, so I take medicine.
I learn Korean with Korean songs.
to know (알겠어요 = I see, I understand)
column2: 知道 (알겠어요 = 知道了，明白了)

column1: I buy crabs at the market.
If you add one more stroke to a basic vowel, a [y] sound (as in "yes") comes in front.
column2: 在基本元音上再加一笔，前面就多了一个 [y] 音 (像拼音 "ya" 里的 y)。

column1: ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ are ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ with [y] in front.
column2: ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ 是在 ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ 前面加上 [y] 的音。

column1: ㅏ → ㅑ, ㅓ → ㅕ, ㅗ → ㅛ, ㅜ → ㅠ: when one short stroke becomes two, a [y] sound comes in front.
column2: ㅏ → ㅑ，ㅓ → ㅕ，ㅗ → ㅛ，ㅜ → ㅠ：一个短笔画变成两个时，前面就加上 [y] 音。

column1: 요 at the end of a sentence makes it polite. You will hear it very often.
column2: 句末的 "요" 使句子变得礼貌。你会经常听到。

column1: I saw a fox at the zoo.
column2: 我在动物园看到了狐狸。

column1: The women's restroom is this way.
I am good at cooking Greek food.
The milk is in the fridge.
to know (알겠습니다 = I see, I understand)
column2: 知道 (알겠습니다 = 知道了，明白了)

column1: Yes, I will come at nine o'clock tomorrow.
If you join another vowel to ㅗ or ㅜ, a [w] sound (as in "we") comes in front.
column2: 在 ㅗ 或 ㅜ 后面加上别的元音，前面就会发出 [w] 音 (像拼音 "wa" 里的 w)。

column1: ㅘ ㅝ ㅙ ㅞ are sounds with [w] in front.
column2: ㅘ ㅝ ㅙ ㅞ 是前面带 [w] 的音。

column1: ㅗ goes only with ㅏ ㅐ, and ㅜ goes only with ㅓ ㅔ.
column2: ㅗ 只和 ㅏ ㅐ 组合，ㅜ 只和 ㅓ ㅔ 组合。

column1: Do not read the two vowels separately. Say them together in one sound.
column2: 不要把两个元音分开读，要连成一个音发出来。

column1: I bought snacks at the convenience store.
A bag of apples is 5,000 won.
The bus is coming. Get on quickly.
to ride, to get on (a bus, boat)
What are you eating for lunch?
Thank you for showing me the way.
These are ㅚ, ㅟ, ㅢ. ㅚ sounds almost the same as ㅙ and ㅞ.
column2: 这是 ㅚ、ㅟ、ㅢ。ㅚ 的发音和 ㅙ、ㅞ 几乎一样。

column1: ㅚ sounds like [웨], ㅟ like [위], and ㅢ is [으이] said quickly.
column2: ㅚ 读作 [웨]，ㅟ 读作 [위]，ㅢ 是把 [으이] 快速连读的音。

column1: For ㅢ, say "으" and "이" quickly together. Do not round your lips.
column2: 发 ㅢ 时，把 "으" 和 "이" 快速连起来读。嘴唇不要撮圆。

column1: ㅢ changes its sound by position. At the start of a word it is [의], in other places [이], and "~의" (of, 's) is said [에].
column2: ㅢ 的发音随位置而变。在词首读 [의]，在其他位置读 [이]，表示 "的" 的 "~의" 读 [에]。

column1: There are many international students at our school.
column2: 我们学校有很多留学生。

column1: My ear hurts, so I go to the hospital.
The key is on the desk.
Today is Sunday, so I rest.
column2: 今天是星期天，所以我休息。

column1: There is no chair. Please give me one.
No, I am an international student.
These are the basic consonants ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ. A consonant needs a vowel to make a sound.
column2: 这是基本辅音 ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ。辅音必须和元音一起写才能发音。

column1: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ sound similar to English g/k, n, d/t, r/l, m.
column2: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ 的发音类似拼音的 g/k、n、d/t、l、m。

column1: At the start of a word, ㄱ and ㄷ have a little breath, so they can sound like English "k" and "t". Between vowels they sound soft, like "g" and "d".
column2: 在词首，ㄱ 和 ㄷ 带一点气，听起来可能像拼音的 "k" 和 "t"。在元音之间发音较软，像拼音的 "g" 和 "d"。

column1: ㄹ is between English "r" and "l". Tap the tip of your tongue lightly once, like the "tt" in American "better".
column2: ㄹ 介于 "l" 和 "r" 之间。用舌尖在上齿龈轻轻弹一下。

column1: My older sister is a university student.
My older sister lives in Pakistan.
The weather in my country is hot.
I have a headache. Do you have medicine?
These are the basic consonants ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ.
column2: 这是基本辅音 ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ。

column1: ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ ㅎ are similar to English b/p, s, j, h, and ㅇ has no sound at the start of a syllable.
column2: ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ ㅎ 类似拼音的 b/p、s、j、h；ㅇ 在音节开头不发音。

column1: ㅇ has no sound at the start of a syllable. As a final consonant (받침), it sounds like the "ng" in "sing".
column2: ㅇ 在音节开头不发音。作为韵尾 (받침) 时，发音像拼音 "ang" 里的 "ng"。

column1: ㅅ in "시" is not [s]; it is close to the English "sh" sound.
column2: 시 的 ㅅ 不是 [s]，而是接近拼音 "x" 的音。

column1: Can I try on these pants?
column2: 我可以试穿这条裤子吗？
这路公交车去市中心吗？

column1: My younger sibling likes the lion doll.
column2: 我弟弟/妹妹喜欢狮子玩偶。

column1: I send money to my father.
I find the way with the map on my phone.
ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ are ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ with one more stroke. Say them with a strong puff of air.
column2: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ 是在 ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ 上加一笔的字母。发音时要送出很强的气。

column1: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ are sounds with a strong puff of air.
column2: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ 是送气很强的音。

column1: At the start of a word, ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ sound almost like English "k", "t", "p" in "kit", "top", "pin" (with a puff of air).
column2: 在词首，ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ 的发音几乎和拼音的 "k"、"t"、"p" 一样 (送气)。

column1: ㅊ is like the "ch" in "church", with a strong puff of air. In the readings it is written "ch". Do not confuse it with ㅈ (j).
column2: ㅊ 像拼音的 "q" 或 "ch"，要送出很强的气。注音中写作 "ch"。不要和 ㅈ (j) 混淆。

column1: Hold a thin piece of paper in front of your mouth and say "카, 타, 파, 차". If the paper moves a lot, you are doing it right.
column2: 在嘴前放一张薄纸，说 "카, 타, 파, 차"。如果纸晃得很厉害，就说明发音对了。

column1: I caught a cold, and my nose is blocked.
How much is a box of tomatoes?
I am going to buy grapes.
Please wash the grapes before you eat them.
to eat, to drink (honorific of 먹다)
Do you have this skirt in another color?
column2: 这条裙子有别的颜色吗？

column1: It takes three hours to Jeonju by train.
column2: 坐火车到全州要三个小时。

column1: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are the same consonant written twice. Tighten your throat and say them with no puff of air.
column2: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ 是把同一个辅音写两次的字母。发音时喉咙用力，不要送气。

column1: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are sounds made with a tight throat and no puff of air.
column2: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ 是喉咙紧张、不送气的音。

column1: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ are close to the "k", "t", "p" after "s" in English "skin", "stop", "spin" (no puff of air), but tighter.
column2: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ 接近拼音不送气的 "g"、"d"、"b"，但喉咙更紧。

column1: English speakers should also be careful with the plain sounds ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ. Say plain sounds softly, without tension.
column2: 说中文的人也要注意平音 ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ。平音不像紧音那样用力，要放松、轻轻地发。

column1: I give a carrot to the rabbit.
Dad, I arrived in Korea safely.
column2: 爸爸，我已经平安到韩国了。
哥哥个子很高。(女性称呼)

column1: My older brother is in Korea.
My older brother came to meet me at the airport.
It is a little salty. Some water, please.
Yes, they are cheap. Please come again.
A consonant written under a syllable is called 받침 (final consonant). First, ㅁ and ㅇ.
column2: 写在音节下面的辅音叫 받침 (韵尾/收音)。先学 ㅁ 和 ㅇ。

column1: Final ㅁ sounds "m", and final ㅇ sounds "ng".
column2: 韵尾 ㅁ 发 "m"，韵尾 ㅇ 发 "ng"。

column1: Final ㅁ is like the "m" at the end of English "home", and final ㅇ is like the "ng" in "sing".
column2: 韵尾 ㅁ 发音时双唇闭合，发出 "m"；韵尾 ㅇ 像拼音 "ang" 里的 "ng"。

column1: ㅇ has no sound at the front. It sounds "ng" only as a final consonant. Compare "아" and "앙".
column2: ㅇ 在前面不发音，只有作韵尾时才发 "ng"。比较一下 "아" 和 "앙"。

column1: I have a video call with my mom.
Do not go out alone at night.
I'm going to the library to study.
These are the final consonants ㄴ and ㄹ. Final ㄹ is similar to English "l". Practice so that it does not sound like "r".
column2: 这是韵尾 ㄴ 和 ㄹ。韵尾 ㄹ 和 "l" 相似。练习时注意不要发成卷舌的 "儿 (er)"。

column1: Final ㄹ is not "n". It is an [l] sound with the tip of the tongue held on the gum.
column2: 韵尾 ㄹ 不是 "n"。它是舌尖抵住齿龈的 [l] 音。

column1: For final ㄹ, keep the tip of your tongue on the gum behind your upper teeth. If you say it as "n", "물" sounds like "문", which is a different word.
column2: 发韵尾 ㄹ 时，舌尖要抵住上齿后面的齿龈。如果发成 "n"，"물" (水) 听起来就像 "문" (门)，是另一个词。

column1: Final ㄴ is the same as the "n" at the end of English words.
column2: 韵尾 ㄴ 和拼音 "an" 里的 "n" 一样。

column1: It snowed a lot, so the road is slippery.
On the weekend, I go to the mountains with my friends.
column2: 周末我和朋友们去爬山。

column1: I have a lot of work.
Today's work ends at five o'clock.
I write my name in Hangul.
Final ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ are not released: stop the sound and hold it. It is like "k", "p", "t" at the end of "book", "cup", "cat" when you do not let the air out.
column2: 韵尾 ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ 不爆破：把气流堵住并停住。就像准备发 "k"、"p"、"t" 时口型摆好，但不把气放出来。

column1: Final ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ end with the sound held, like an unreleased "k", "p", "t".
column2: 韵尾 ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ 以堵住气流结束，就像不爆破的 "k"、"p"、"t"。

column1: Final ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ all end with a ㄷ (t) sound: 옷[옫], 낮[낟], 꽃[꼳].
column2: 韵尾 ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ 都以 ㄷ (t) 音结束：옷[옫]、낮[낟]、꽃[꼳]。

column1: Be careful not to add "으" after a final consonant, like "채그" or "바브".
column2: 注意不要在韵尾后面加 "으"，读成 "채그"、"바브"。

column1: I take my younger sibling to school.
My house is close to the school.
I change into my gym clothes.
I give flowers to my mother.
It is hot during the day, so drink a lot of water.
These syllables have two consonants in the 받침. When you say the word alone, you pronounce only one of them.
column2: 这些字的韵尾有两个辅音。单独说这个词时，只发其中一个音。

column1: A double final consonant: alone, only one sounds; before a vowel, both sound.
column2: 双韵尾：单独时只发一个音；在元音前两个都发音。

column1: Only one is pronounced, as in 닭[닥], 여덟[여덜], 값[갑]. Learn which one for each word.
column2: 只发一个音，比如 닭[닥]、여덟[여덜]、값[갑]。发哪一个，要每个词分别记。

column1: If a vowel comes after, the second consonant moves to the next syllable and both are pronounced: 읽어요[일거요], 앉아요[안자요].
column2: 如果后面接元音，第二个辅音就移到下一个音节，两个都发音：읽어요[일거요]、앉아요[안자요]。

column1: Half a geun of chicken, please.
geun (unit of weight, 600 g for meat)
Please be sure to read the notice.
I get up at eight in the morning.
There are many customers on weekends.
Thank you. There are a lot of people.
In Hangul, consonants and vowels are written together in one square block. One block is one syllable.
column2: 韩文把辅音和元音组合写在一个方块里。一个方块就是一个音节。

column1: One syllable is consonant + vowel, or consonant + vowel + 받침.
column2: 一个音节由 "辅音 + 元音" 或 "辅音 + 元音 + 받침" 组成。

column1: Write from left to right and from top to bottom. The 받침 goes at the very bottom.
column2: 书写顺序是从左到右、从上到下。받침 写在最下面。

column1: English writes letters in one line, but in Hangul the vowel goes only to the right of the consonant or below it.
column2: 和汉字一样，韩文也写成一个个方块；元音只放在辅音的右边或下面。

column1: My younger sibling sleeps holding a teddy bear.
column2: 我弟弟/妹妹抱着玩具熊睡觉。

column1: to hug, to hold in one's arms
Can I go with you too?
Please lock the door when you go out.
I am going to the hospital tomorrow.
When a syllable starting with ㅇ comes after a 받침, the 받침 moves over and becomes the first sound of the next syllable.
column2: 받침 后面接以 ㅇ 开头的字时，받침 会移过去，成为后一个字的首音。

column1: When a vowel comes after it, the 받침 moves to the next syllable.
column2: 后面接元音时，받침 移到下一个音节发音。

column1: The spelling stays the same; only the sound changes: 한국어[한구거], 먹어요[머거요], 있어요[이써요].
column2: 拼写不变，只是发音变了：한국어[한구거]、먹어요[머거요]、있어요[이써요]。

column1: Final ㅇ does not move: 가방에[가방에].
I can speak a little Korean.
I listen to music while I work.
I sit in a seat on the bus.
Let's read some first words with the letters you have learned.
column2: 用目前学过的字母读一读最初的单词。

column1: You have learned all of Hangul. Now you can read words.
column2: 你已经学完了全部韩文字母。现在可以读单词了。

column1: At first, read slowly one syllable at a time. Then read them together.
column2: 一开始一个字一个字慢慢读，然后再连起来读。

column1: 감사합니다 is pronounced [감사함니다]. You will learn why in the pronunciation rules unit later.
column2: 감사합니다 读作 [감사함니다]。原因会在后面的发音规则单元里学习。

column1: I want to work in Korea.
I am Sam. I am American.
ㄱ, ㅋ, ㄲ differ in the strength of the breath and the tension in the throat. English has only one "k" sound, so it is hard to hear ㄱ and ㄲ.
column2: ㄱ、ㅋ、ㄲ 的区别在于送气的强弱和喉咙的紧张程度。中文只区分送气 (k) 和不送气 (g)，所以很难听出 ㄱ 和 ㄲ 的区别。

column1: ㄲ is a tight "k" (as in "skin"), ㅋ is a strong "k" (as in "kit"), and ㄱ is soft and low.
column2: ㄲ 是紧的不送气音 (像拼音 "g" 但更紧)，ㅋ 是强送气音 (像拼音 "k")，ㄱ 柔和、音调低。

column1: ㄲ is like the "k" in "skin" but tighter, and ㅋ is like the "k" in "kit" with a puff of air. ㄱ is in between: say it relaxed and soft, with a low pitch.
column2: ㄲ 像拼音 "g" 但喉咙更紧；ㅋ 像拼音 "k"，送气很强。ㄱ 介于两者之间：放松、柔和地发，音调较低。

column1: At the start of a word, the vowel after ㄱ starts low, and the vowel after ㅋ and ㄲ starts high. Listening for high and low pitch is the easiest way.
column2: 在词首，ㄱ 后面的元音起调低，ㅋ 和 ㄲ 后面的元音起调高。听音调高低是最容易的区分方法。

column1: Honey water is good for a cold.
I fold the laundry and put it away.
column2: 我把洗好的衣服叠好收起来。

column1: On the weekend, I dig sweet potatoes with my friends.
column2: 周末我和朋友们去挖红薯。

column1: We dug potatoes on a field trip.
column2: 我们在体验学习时挖了土豆。

column1: I broke a plate. I am sorry.
Do you have a bigger size?
It is honey. It is sweet.
These are ㄷ, ㅌ, ㄸ. ㅌ is like the "t" in "top", ㄸ is like the "t" in "stop" but tighter, and ㄷ at the start of a word has a little breath.
column2: 这是 ㄷ、ㅌ、ㄸ。ㅌ 像拼音的 "t"，ㄸ 像拼音的 "d" 但更紧，词首的 ㄷ 带一点气。

column1: ㅌ is the "t" in "top", ㄸ is the "t" in "stop", and ㄷ between vowels is "d".
column2: ㅌ 是拼音的 "t"，ㄸ 是更紧的 "d"，元音之间的 ㄷ 是浊音 "d"。

column1: ㄷ between vowels sounds like English "d": 바다, 어디.
column2: 元音之间的 ㄷ 发音更柔和，像浊音 "d"：바다、어디。

column1: If you say "딸" as "달", the meaning changes. Say ㄸ tight and strong, like the "t" in "stop".
column2: 如果把 "딸" (女儿) 说成 "달" (月亮)，意思就变了。ㄸ 要发得又紧又有力，不送气。

column1: I get my allowance once a month.
column2: 我每个月领一次零花钱。

column1: I saw Korean masks at the museum.
column2: 我在博物馆看到了韩国的面具。

column1: I'm the eldest daughter in my family.
I fell down and hurt my chin.
We eat rice cakes on holidays.
to happen (고장이 나다 = to break down)
No, there are two daughters in my family.
These are ㅂ, ㅍ, ㅃ. ㅍ is like the "p" in "pin", and ㅃ is like the "p" in "spin" but tighter.
column2: 这是 ㅂ、ㅍ、ㅃ。ㅍ 像拼音的 "p"，ㅃ 像拼音的 "b" 但更紧。

column1: ㅍ is the "p" in "pin", ㅃ is the "p" in "spin", and ㅂ between vowels is "b".
column2: ㅍ 是拼音的 "p"，ㅃ 是更紧的 "b"，元音之间的 ㅂ 是浊音 "b"。

column1: 불 (fire) and "풀" (grass) mean very different things, and mishearing them can be dangerous. ㅍ has a strong puff of air.
column2: 불 (火) 和 "풀" (草) 意思完全不同，听错了可能会很危险。ㅍ 要送出很强的气。

column1: ㅂ between vowels sounds like English "b": 아버지, 가방.
column2: 元音之间的 ㅂ 发音更柔和，像浊音 "b"：아버지、가방。

column1: to turn on (a light, a machine)
Please turn off the light when you go out.
There is a lot of grass in the park.
Watch out for the cow's horns.
I am looking for a room.
For breakfast, I eat bread and milk.
No, I am eating a meal in my room.
These are ㅈ, ㅊ, ㅉ. English has only "j" and "ch", so you need to practice all three.
column2: 这是 ㅈ、ㅊ、ㅉ。中文有 "j" 和 "q"，但没有紧音，所以三个音都要练习。

column1: ㅉ is a tight "j", ㅊ is "ch" with a strong breath, and ㅈ is a soft "j".
column2: ㅉ 是紧的 "j"，ㅊ 是送气很强的 "q/ch"，ㅈ 是柔和的 "j"。

column1: ㅉ is a tight "j" with no breath. ㅊ is like the "ch" in "church" with a strong puff of air. ㅈ is a soft, low sound between "j" and "ch".
column2: ㅉ 是不送气的紧 "j"。ㅊ 像拼音的 "q" 或 "ch"，送气很强。ㅈ 柔和、音调低，介于 "j" 和 "q" 之间。

column1: Be careful not to say ㅊ as "s" or "sh". "차" is not "사".
column2: 注意不要把 ㅊ 发成 "s" 或 "sh"。"차" 不是 "사"。

column1: I was tired, so I went to bed early.
The wind is cold. Put on a jacket.

If the soup is salty, add water.

I steam dumplings and eat them.
It is a little salty. And it is cold.
These are ㅅ and ㅆ. Say ㅆ as a clear, strong "s", like in "see". Say ㅅ softly, with some breath.
column2: 这是 ㅅ 和 ㅆ。ㅆ 要发成清晰有力的 "s"，像拼音的 "s"。ㅅ 要发得轻柔，带一点气。

column1: ㅆ is a strong "s", and ㅅ is a soft sound with breath.
column2: ㅆ 是有力的 "s"，ㅅ 是轻柔带气的音。

column1: If you say "쌀" as "살", "rice" becomes "flesh". Say ㅆ strongly and a little longer.
column2: 如果把 "쌀" 说成 "살"，"大米" 就变成了 "肉"。ㅆ 要发得有力，稍微长一点。

column1: In "있어요" and "했어요", final ㅆ moves to the next syllable and sounds [써].
column2: 在 "있어요"、"했어요" 中，韵尾 ㅆ 移到下一个音节，读作 [써]。

column1: The market is cheaper than the supermarket.
Sam, you have a phone call.
These are ㅓ and ㅗ. They can sound alike to English speakers, and the letters are easy to mix up. ㅓ is like the "u" in "cup" with the mouth more open; ㅗ is like the "o" in "go" with round lips.
column2: 这是 ㅓ 和 ㅗ。对说中文的人来说它们可能听起来很像，字母也容易混淆。发 ㅓ 时嘴巴张得较大，介于拼音 "o" 和 "e" 之间；ㅗ 像拼音的 "o"，嘴唇撮圆。

column1: ㅓ is "eo" (open mouth, like "u" in "cup"), and ㅗ is "o" (round lips, like "o" in "go").
column2: ㅓ 写作 "eo" (张嘴，介于 o 和 e 之间)，ㅗ 写作 "o" (圆唇，像拼音 "o")。

column1: For ㅓ, open your mouth and keep your lips relaxed; for ㅗ, round your lips and push them forward. Practice in front of a mirror.
column2: 发 ㅓ 时张开嘴，嘴唇放松；发 ㅗ 时嘴唇撮圆并向前突出。请对着镜子练习。

column1: If you read Korean words from romanization (eo, o), it is easy to make mistakes. Read them in Hangul.
column2: 看着罗马字 (eo、o) 读韩语单词很容易读错。请用韩文来读。

column1: If your nose bleeds, lower your head.

column2: 我妈妈在乌兹别克斯坦。

column1: I bought a birthday present for my mother.
column2: 我给妈妈买了生日礼物。

column1: These are ㅡ and ㅜ. ㅜ is like the "oo" in "food". English has no ㅡ: say "oo", but keep your lips flat, as if smiling.
column2: 这是 ㅡ 和 ㅜ。ㅜ 像拼音的 "u"。中文里没有和 ㅡ 完全相同的音：舌头位置像发 "u"，但嘴唇要平展，像微笑一样 (有点像拼音 "zi" 里的 "i")。

column1: ㅡ is "eu" (flat lips), and ㅜ is "u" (like "oo" in "food").
column2: ㅡ 写作 "eu" (嘴唇平展)，ㅜ 写作 "u" (像拼音 "u")。

column1: For ㅡ, spread your lips to the sides; for ㅜ, round your lips and push them forward.
column2: 发 ㅡ 时嘴唇向两边展开；发 ㅜ 时嘴唇撮圆并向前突出。

column1: Many loanwords end with ㅡ, like "스", "크", "트": 버스, 마스크.
column2: 很多外来词以 ㅡ 结尾，比如 "스"、"크"、"트"：버스 (公交车)、마스크 (口罩)。

column1: Do you know that person's phone number?
column2: 你知道那个人的电话号码吗？

column2: 请帮我读一下这段文字。

column2: 请给我两杯咖啡、一杯果汁。

Today ㅐ and ㅔ are said almost the same. Tell them apart by spelling and context, not by sound.
column2: 现在 ㅐ 和 ㅔ 的发音几乎一样。要靠拼写和上下文来区分，而不是靠发音。

column1: ㅐ and ㅔ sound the same, so learn them by spelling.
column2: ㅐ 和 ㅔ 发音相同，所以要按拼写来记。

column1: Even Korean people cannot tell them apart well by sound. So when they say "네가" (you), they say [니가].
column2: 连韩国人也很难靠发音区分它们。所以说 "네가" (你) 时，他们会说成 [니가]。

column2: 这是听写时很容易写错的字母。请记住每个单词的拼写。

column1: Soy sauce crab is a little salty.

ㅚ, ㅙ, ㅞ are all said close to [웨]. ㅢ has three sounds depending on its position.
column2: ㅚ、ㅙ、ㅞ 的发音都接近 [웨]。ㅢ 根据位置有三种读法。

column1: ㅚ ㅙ ㅞ are said [웨], and ㅢ is said [의], [이], or [에] depending on its position.
column2: ㅚ ㅙ ㅞ 读作 [웨]，ㅢ 根据位置读作 [의]、[이] 或 [에]。

column1: The three sounds of ㅢ: at the start of a word [의] 의사; from the second syllable [이] 회의[회이]; "~의" (of, 's) [에] 저의[저에].
column2: ㅢ 的三种读法：在词首读 [의]，如 의사；从第二个音节开始读 [이]，如 회의[회이]；表示 "的" 的 "~의" 读 [에]，如 저의[저에]。

column1: ㅢ written with a consonant is said [이]: 희망[히망].
column2: 和辅音一起写的 ㅢ 读作 [이]：희망[히망]。

column1: I have a Korean conversation class on Monday.

column2: 有一个团队项目的会议。

column1: What time does the meeting start?

Tell the final consonants ㄴ, ㅇ, ㅁ apart. They are like the n, ng, m at the end of English "sun", "sung", "sum", so they are easy.
column2: 区分韵尾 ㄴ、ㅇ、ㅁ。ㄴ 和 ㅇ 就像拼音 "an"、"ang" 里的 n 和 ng；ㅁ 是闭上双唇的 m。中文没有 m 韵尾，要注意把嘴闭上。

column1: Final ㄴ is "n", ㅇ is "ng", and ㅁ is "m".
column2: 韵尾 ㄴ 是 "n"，ㅇ 是 "ng"，ㅁ 是 "m"。

column1: The sounds are easy, but people often mix up ㄴ and ㅇ when they write them in Hangul.
column2: 发音不难，但用韩文书写时，很多人会把 ㄴ 和 ㅇ 写混。

column1: Final ㄴ can change a little depending on the next consonant. Even if it sounds like 한국[항국], you write "한국".
column2: 韵尾 ㄴ 有时会因后面的辅音而稍有变化。即使听起来像 한국[항국]，也要写成 "한국"。

column2: 韵尾 ㄹ 是学习者最常读错的音。不要把它变成 "n" 或卷舌的 "儿 (er)"。要以 [l] 结尾，舌尖抵住齿龈。

column1: Final ㄹ is not "n" but [l]. Keep the tip of your tongue on the gum at the end.
column2: 韵尾 ㄹ 不是 "n"，而是 [l]。结尾时舌尖要抵住齿龈。

column1: If you say "일" as "인" or "물" as "문", it becomes a different word: 물 (water) and 문 (door).
column2: 如果把 "일" 说成 "인"，或把 "물" 说成 "문"，就变成另一个词了：물 (水) 和 문 (门)。

column1: When two ㄹ come together, say a long [ll]: 빨리, 몰라요.
column2: 两个 ㄹ 连在一起时，读成长的 [ll]：빨리、몰라요。

column1: I am going to Nepal next month.
What kind of work do you do?
I can do it by myself.
Yes, I can. I will do it quickly.
Final ㄷ ㅅ ㅆ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ ㅎ are written differently, but they all sound [ㄷ] (t).
column2: 韵尾 ㄷ ㅅ ㅆ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ ㅎ 写法不同，但都读作 [ㄷ] (t)。

column1: Final ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ ㅎ sound [ㄷ] alone, but keep their own sound before a vowel.
column2: 韵尾 ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ ㅎ 单独时读 [ㄷ]，在元音前保留原来的音。

column1: Alone, they all sound [ㄷ], but when a vowel comes after, the original sound comes back: 옷[옫], 옷이[오시], 꽃이[꼬치], 끝에[끄테].
column2: 单独时都读 [ㄷ]，但后面接元音时，原来的音就会恢复：옷[옫]、옷이[오시]、꽃이[꼬치]、끝에[끄테]。

column1: So in dictation, think of the sound with "이" or "에" added after it, and you will know the letter.
column2: 所以听写时，想一想后面加上 "이" 或 "에" 时的发音，就能知道是哪个字母。

column2: 韵尾 ㅂ ㄷ ㄱ 后面接 ㄴ 或 ㅁ 时，韵尾会变成 ㅁ ㄴ ㅇ。这就是 "합니다" 读作 [함니다] 的原因。

column1: Final ㅂ ㄷ ㄱ sound like ㅁ ㄴ ㅇ before ㄴ ㅁ.
column2: 韵尾 ㅂ ㄷ ㄱ 在 ㄴ ㅁ 前读作 ㅁ ㄴ ㅇ。

The spelling does not change. You write "합니다"; only when you read it is it [함니다].
column2: 拼写不变。写的时候是 "합니다"，只有读的时候才是 [함니다]。

column1: I will contact you again tomorrow.
I am the person in charge today.

column2: 我给巴基斯坦汇了100,000韩元。

column2: ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ 出现在韵尾 ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ 后面时，读作 ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ。

column2: ㅎ 和 ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ 相遇时，两个音合在一起读作 ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ。

column1: ㅎ + ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ become ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ.
column2: ㅎ + ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ 变成 ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ。

column1: It is the same whether ㅎ comes first or second: 좋다[조타], 축하[추카], 입학[이팍], 못하다[모타다].
column2: ㅎ 不管在前还是在后都一样：좋다[조타]、축하[추카]、입학[이팍]、못하다[모타다]。

column1: Say them like a strong English "k", "t", "p", "ch", with a puff of air.
column2: 发音像拼音送气的 "k"、"t"、"p"、"q"，送气很强。

column1: Final ㅎ is silent before a vowel.
column2: 韵尾 ㅎ 在元音前不发音。

column1: When said fast, "전화" and "은행" sound like [저놔] and [으냉]. When said slowly, the ㅎ is pronounced.
column2: 说得快时，"전화" 和 "은행" 听起来像 [저놔] 和 [으냉]。慢慢说时要发出 ㅎ 音。

column1: Is this time OK? Yes, that's good.

韵尾 ㄷ ㅌ 在 "이" 前面变成 [ㅈ]、[ㅊ]。

column1: You hear "같이" very often at school. It is not [가티] but [가치].

column2: ㄴ 和 ㄹ 相遇时，两个都读作 ㄹ。

column2: [ㄹㄹ] 是舌尖抵住齿龈、拉长的 [ll] 音。

column1: It is convenient to have a transportation card.
Sentences ending in "-아요/어요" look the same, but if the end goes up, it is a question; if it goes down, it is an answer.
column2: 以 "-아요/어요" 结尾的句子写法一样，但句末语调上扬就是问句，下降就是回答。

column1: If the end goes up, it is a question; if it goes down, it is an answer.
column2: 句末上扬是问句，下降是回答。

column1: English often adds "do" or changes the word order to ask a question, but Korean adds no word. You just raise your voice at the end.
column2: 中文的问句常在句末加 "吗"，而韩语不用加任何词，只要把句末的语调上扬就可以了。

column1: Korean has no tones. Even if the pitch of a word is different, the meaning does not change.
column2: 和中文不同，韩语没有声调。即使单词的音高不同，意思也不会改变。

column1: Does this bus go to the airport?

column2: 在带有 "어디、뭐、언제" 的问句中，要把这个词说得高而有力，句末只稍微上扬或下降。

column1: If there is a question word, say it strongly.
column2: 如果有疑问词，要把疑问词说得重一些。

column1: Even "어디 가요?" means "Are you going somewhere?" if you raise the end high.

column2: 同样的 "-세요" 根据语气不同，可以是请求，也可以是指示。练习在学校和打工的地方听懂语气。

column1: When Koreans speak fast and strongly, it often means they are in a hurry, not angry.
