column2: 我室友睡觉的时候请保持安静。

column1: I drank coffee while I waited.
I lived in Jeonju for three years.
Did anything happen while I was away?
column2: 我不在的时候发生什么事了吗？

column1: Please wait here while the professor is in a meeting.
column2: 教授开会期间，请在这里等。

column1: Yes. How long is the meeting?
Used when the first and second parts contrast. It is like "but" in English.
column2: 用于前后两部分形成对比。相当于中文的 "但是，虽然……但……"。

column1: -지만 means "but" and is added to the end of the first part.
column2: -지만 意思是 "但是"，加在前半句的末尾。

column1: Take "-다" off a verb or adjective and add "-지만". It does not depend on 받침. For the past, use "-았/었지만".
column2: 去掉动词或形容词的 "-다"，加上 "-지만"。和有没有韵尾无关。过去的事用 "-았/었지만"。

column1: In English "but" comes at the start of the second part, but "-지만" is added to the end of the first part.
column2: 中文的 "但是" 放在后半句的开头，而 "-지만" 加在前半句的末尾。

column1: To split it into two sentences, use "하지만" or "그렇지만": "힘들어요. 하지만 재미있어요."
column2: 要分成两个句子时，用 "하지만" 或 "그렇지만"："힘들어요. 하지만 재미있어요." (很累。但是很有意思。)

column1: Starting with "죄송하지만" or "실례지만" (Excuse me, but…) sounds polite.
column2: 开口时用 "죄송하지만" 或 "실례지만" (不好意思，……) 开头，听起来很礼貌。

column1: Studying is hard, but it's fun.
column2: 学习虽然辛苦，但很有意思。

column1: Kimchi is spicy, but it's tasty.
I took medicine, but it still hurts.
I miss my family, but I'm okay.
column2: 我虽然想家人，但我没事。

column1: It was hard at first, but now I'm used to it.
column2: 一开始很辛苦，但现在已经习惯了。

column1: Used to give the background situation first, before what you say next. It is also used for contrast (but). There is no exact match in English.
column2: 用于先交代背景情况，再说接下来的话。也用于对比 (但是)。中文里没有完全对应的说法。

column1: -는데/(으)ㄴ데 first gives the background situation for what comes next.
column2: -는데/(으)ㄴ데 先说出作为后文背景的情况。

column1: Add "-는데" to verbs and "있다/없다"; to adjectives add "-은데" after a 받침 and "-ㄴ데" with no 받침; to nouns add "인데"; for the past add "-았/었는데".
column2: 动词和 "있다/없다" 加 "-는데"；形容词有韵尾加 "-은데"，没有韵尾加 "-ㄴ데"；名词加 "인데"；过去的事加 "-았/었는데"。

column1: It is used most when you explain the situation before asking for help or asking a question: "길을 잘 모르는데 좀 가르쳐 주세요." (I don't know the way well. Could you tell me?)
column2: 最常用于请求帮助或提问之前说明情况："길을 잘 모르는데 좀 가르쳐 주세요." (我不太认识路，能告诉我一下吗？)

column1: Ending a sentence with "-는데요" makes a soft answer that leaves the rest unsaid: "지금 없는데요." (He's not here right now…)
column2: 以 "-는데요" 结尾的句子，是省略了后半句的委婉回答："지금 없는데요." (他现在不在……)

column1: I'm busy now, so let's talk later.
column2: 我现在很忙，我们以后再聊吧。

column1: It's raining. Do you have an umbrella?
I worked hard, but it didn't go well.
column2: 我很努力了，但结果不太好。

column1: This is Sam. Is the professor there?
Professor, I have something to tell you. Do you have time?
column2: 教授，我有件事想跟您说，您现在方便吗？

column1: I have to go to the hospital next week. Could I miss class for one day?
column2: 我下周得去医院，可以请一天假不上课吗？

column1: Used when choosing one of two actions. It is like "or" in English.
column2: 用于在两个动作中选择一个。相当于中文的 "或者"。
动词 + -거나 意思是 "动词 + 或者"。

column1: Take "-다" off a verb or adjective and add "-거나". It does not depend on 받침.
column2: 去掉动词或形容词的 "-다"，加上 "-거나"。和有没有韵尾无关。

column1: Nouns use "(이)나", and verbs and adjectives use "-거나": "커피나 차" (coffee or tea), "마시거나 먹거나" (drink or eat).
column2: 名词用 "(이)나"，动词和形容词用 "-거나"："커피나 차" (咖啡或者茶)，"마시거나 먹거나" (喝或者吃)。

column1: English "or" stands alone in the middle, but "-거나" is attached to the first verb.
column2: 中文的 "或者" 单独放在中间，而 "-거나" 附在第一个动词的后面。

column1: To split it into two sentences, use "아니면" or "또는".
column2: 要分成两个句子时，用 "아니면" 或 "또는"。

column1: On weekends I rest or meet friends.
column2: 周末我休息或者见朋友。

column1: In the evening I watch TV or listen to music.
column2: 晚上我看电视或者听音乐。

column1: If you are sick or get hurt, tell us right away.
column2: 如果生病或受伤，请马上告诉我们。

column1: If you don't know something, ask or look it up in a dictionary.
column2: 不知道的东西请问别人或者查词典。

column1: What do you usually do on your day off?
I sleep at home or do the laundry.
column2: 我在家睡觉或者洗衣服。

column1: Sometimes I go to the market or meet friends.
column2: 有时去市场或者见朋友。

column1: Used to give a reason. It is like "because…, so…" in English.
column2: 用于说明理由。相当于中文的 "因为……所以……"。

column1: -아서/어서 shows a reason, and the second part cannot be an order.
column2: -아서/어서 表示理由，后面不能接命令。

column1: Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "서". For nouns, use "(이)라서".
column2: 去掉 "-아요/어요" 形式中的 "요"，加上 "서"。名词用 "(이)라서"。

column1: English "because" comes before the reason, but Korean adds "-아서/어서" to the end of the reason part. The reason comes first, and the result comes after.
column2: 和中文 "因为……所以……" 一样，原因在前、结果在后；但韩语要把 "-아서/어서" 加在原因部分的末尾。

column1: The second part cannot be an order (-세요) or a suggestion (-ㅂ시다). In that case use "-(으)니까". "추워서 문을 닫으세요" is wrong.
column2: 后半句不能是命令 (-세요) 或提议 (-ㅂ시다)。这时要用 "-(으)니까"。"추워서 문을 닫으세요" 是错的。

column1: Before 고맙다, 미안하다, 죄송하다, 반갑다, always use "-아서/어서": "만나서 반갑습니다." (Nice to meet you.)
column2: 在 고맙다、미안하다、죄송하다、반갑다 前面总是用 "-아서/어서"："만나서 반갑습니다." (很高兴见到你。)

column1: I couldn't go because I was sick.
I was late because of the traffic.
I'm sorry. I missed the bus, so I was late.
column2: 对不起。我没赶上公交车，所以迟到了。

column1: From next time, please come earlier.
Yes, I'm sorry to have worried you.
column2: 好的，让您担心了，对不起。

column1: Used to give a reason. Used when the second part is an order or a suggestion. It is like "because…, since…" in English.
column2: 用于说明理由。当后半句是命令或提议时使用。相当于中文的 "因为……，既然……"。

column1: When you give a reason before an order, use "-(으)니까".
column2: 在命令前面说明理由时，用 "-(으)니까"。

column1: After a 받침 add "-으니까"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-니까". A ㄹ 받침 drops (멀다 → 머니까). For the past, use "-았/었으니까".
column2: 有韵尾加 "-으니까"；没有韵尾或韵尾是 ㄹ 时加 "-니까"。韵尾 ㄹ 会脱落 (멀다 → 머니까)。过去的事用 "-았/었으니까"。

column1: Safety warnings are almost always in the form "-(으)니까 + -(으)세요/-지 마세요".
column2: 安全提示几乎都是 "-(으)니까 + -(으)세요/-지 마세요" 的形式。

column1: When you give your own reason to a senior, "-(으)니까" can sound like you are arguing. "아파서 못 가요" is softer than "아프니까 못 가요".
column2: 向长辈或上级说明自己的理由时，用 "-(으)니까" 可能听起来像在争辩。"아파서 못 가요" 比 "아프니까 못 가요" 更委婉。

column1: It's hot, so don't touch it.
It's raining, so take an umbrella with you.
This pot is hot, so be sure to wear gloves.
column2: 这个锅很烫，一定要戴手套。

column1: Yes, I understand. Should I wear an apron too?
column2: 好的，明白了。我也要穿围裙吗？

column1: Yes, oil splashes, so wear an apron too.
column2: 是的，油会溅出来，请也穿上围裙。

column1: Used to state a reason clearly. Often used in writing, reports and presentations. It is like "because, due to" in English.
column2: 用于明确地说明理由。常用于书面语、报告和发表中。相当于中文的 "因为，由于"。

column1: -기 때문에 is a formal way to state a reason clearly.
column2: -기 때문에 是明确说明理由的正式说法。

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-기 때문에". For the past, use "-았/었기 때문에"; for nouns, use "noun + 때문에".
column2: 去掉 "-다"，加上 "-기 때문에"。过去的事用 "-았/었기 때문에"；名词用 "名词 + 때문에"。

column1: The second part cannot be an order or a suggestion.
column2: 后半句不能是命令或提议。

column1: Noun + 때문에 is usually the cause of something bad. For the cause of something good, use "덕분에".
column2: 名词 + 때문에 通常表示坏事的原因。好事的原因用 "덕분에"。

column1: To ask for a reason, say "왜요?" or "무엇 때문에요?", and you can end the answer with "~기 때문입니다".
column2: 问原因时说 "왜요?" 或 "무엇 때문에요?"，回答可以用 "~기 때문입니다" 结尾。

column1: Because it is raining, the festival was canceled.
column2: 由于下雨，庆典被取消了。

column1: Because I have a lot of assignments, I'm going to the library.
column2: 因为作业很多，所以我去图书馆。

column1: I went to the hospital because of a cold.
Because the bus broke down, I was late for class.
column2: 由于公交车出了故障，我上课迟到了。

column1: Sam, why did you hand in the assignment late?
column2: 山姆，你为什么迟交作业？

column1: It's because my laptop broke down yesterday.
column2: 因为我的笔记本电脑昨天坏了。

column1: Yes, I had it repaired, so there is no problem.
column2: 是的，已经修好了，所以没问题。

column1: Gives a condition. It is like "if" in English.
column2: 表示条件。相当于中文的 "如果"。

column1: -(으)면 means "if…" and is added to the end of the condition.
column2: -(으)면 意思是 "如果……"，加在条件的末尾。

column1: After a 받침 add "-으면"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면". For nouns, use "(이)면".
column2: 有韵尾加 "-으면"；没有韵尾或韵尾是 ㄹ 时加 "-면"。名词用 "(이)면"。

column1: English "if" comes at the start of the condition, but "-(으)면" is added to its end: "if you don't know" = "모르면".
column2: 中文的 "如果" 放在条件的开头，而 "-(으)면" 加在条件的末尾 (有点像中文的 "……的话")："不知道的话" = "모르면"。

column1: It is also used for things that will surely happen. Then it means "when": "봄이 되면 따뜻해져요." (When spring comes, it gets warm.)
column2: 也用于一定会发生的事，这时意思是 "……的时候"："봄이 되면 따뜻해져요." (到了春天就会变暖和。)

column1: You can add "만약, 만일, 혹시" in front to make the condition clear: "혹시 늦으면 연락하세요." (If you are late, please contact me.)
column2: 可以在前面加 "만약、만일、혹시"，使条件更明确："혹시 늦으면 연락하세요." (如果迟到了，请联系我。)

column1: If you have time, let's go together.
column2: 有时间的话，我们一起去吧。

column1: If it hurts, don't put up with it. Tell us.
column2: 如果疼，别忍着，要说出来。

column1: to put up with, hold back
What do you do if there is a fire in the dorm?
to break out (불이 나다 = a fire breaks out)
I go outside right away and call 119.
Right. If the stairs are dark, turn on your phone's light.
column2: 对。如果楼梯很黑，就打开手机的手电筒。

column1: Means "if you want to…". Used to tell how to reach a goal. It is like "if you want to…, (in order) to…" in English.
column2: 意思是 "如果想……"。用于说明达到目的的方法。相当于中文的 "如果想……，要……的话"。

column1: -(으)려면 means "if you want to…", and the way to do it comes after.
column2: -(으)려면 意思是 "如果想……"，后面接做法。

column1: After a 받침 add "-으려면"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-려면". After it comes "-아/어야 해요", "-(으)세요" or "-(으)면 돼요".
column2: 有韵尾加 "-으려면"；没有韵尾或韵尾是 ㄹ 时加 "-려면"。后面接 "-아/어야 해요"、"-(으)세요" 或 "-(으)면 돼요"。

column1: It is the most useful pattern for asking the way or asking about procedures: "~(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?" (What do I have to do to…?)
column2: 这是问路或询问办事流程时最有用的句型："~(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?" (要……的话，我该怎么做？)

column1: To go to Korea, you have to take a test.
column2: 要去韩国的话，得参加考试。

column1: To open a bank account, you need your residence card.
column2: 要开银行账户的话，需要外国人登录证。

column1: Which bus do I have to take to go to City Hall?
column2: 去市政府要坐几路公交车？

column1: If you want to be good at Korean, practice every day.
column2: 想学好韩语的话，请每天练习。

column1: if you want to be good at
What do I have to do to extend my period of stay?
column2: 要延长滞留期限的话，我该怎么做？

column1: You have to apply at the immigration office.
column2: 您需要到出入境管理事务所申请。

column1: What do I need to apply?
You need your passport, residence card and certificate of enrollment.
column2: 需要护照、外国人登录证和在读证明。

column1: Tells the purpose of going or coming. It is like "go/come to + verb" (go to eat) in English.
column2: 表示去或来的目的。相当于中文的 "去/来 + 做某事" (去吃饭)。
-(으)러 가요/와요 意思是 "去/来 + 做某事"。

column1: After a 받침 add "-으러"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-러", then use "가다, 오다, 다니다".
column2: 有韵尾加 "-으러"；没有韵尾或韵尾是 ㄹ 时加 "-러"，后面接 "가다、오다、다니다"。

column1: In English "go" comes first (go to eat), but in Korean "가요" comes at the end (먹으러 가요).
column2: 中文的 "去" 放在前面 (去吃饭)，而韩语的 "가요" 放在最后 (먹으러 가요)。

column1: Only verbs of movement (가다, 오다, 다니다, 나가다, 들어오다) can come after it. With other verbs, use "-(으)려고".
column2: 后面只能接表示移动的动词 (가다、오다、다니다、나가다、들어오다)。如果是其他动词，要用 "-(으)려고"。

column1: Say the place you go to with "에": "식당에 밥 먹으러 가요." (I'm going to a restaurant to eat.)
column2: 要去的地方用 "에" 表示："식당에 밥 먹으러 가요." (我去餐厅吃饭。)

column1: I came to Korea to study.
Come over and visit on the weekend.
I'm going to the bank to take out money.
go out (to have fun), go on a trip
I'm going to the post office to send a package.
I have to go mail a letter too, so let's go together.
column2: 我也得去寄信，一起去吧。

column1: Tells the purpose of an action. It is like "to…, in order to…" in English.
column2: 表示动作的目的。相当于中文的 "为了……"。

column1: -(으)려고 means "in order to…", and the purpose is said first.
column2: -(으)려고 意思是 "为了……"，目的放在前面说。

column1: After a 받침 add "-으려고"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-려고". Any verb can come after it.
column2: 有韵尾加 "-으려고"；没有韵尾或韵尾是 ㄹ 时加 "-려고"。后面可以接任何动词。

column1: In English you usually say the action first and then the purpose after "to, in order to", but in Korean the purpose comes first and the action comes after.
column2: 和中文 "为了……" 一样，韩语也是目的在前、动作在后。

column1: Orders and suggestions are not usually used after it. In that case, use "-(으)려면".
column2: 后面一般不接命令或提议。这时要用 "-(으)려면"。

column1: At a counter, to say why you came, say "~(으)려고 왔어요" or "~(으)려고요".
column2: 在窗口说明来意时，说 "~(으)려고 왔어요" 或 "~(으)려고요"。

column1: I came to open a bank account.
I'm saving money to send to my family.
column2: 我在攒钱，为了寄给家人。

column1: I'm learning Korean to study at a Korean university.
column2: 为了在韩国大学学习，我在学韩语。

column1: I went to bed early so I could get up early.
How can I help you? (Why did you come?)
column2: 您有什么事吗？(您来办什么事？)

column1: I came to pay my tuition.
Please give me your bankbook and ID card.
column2: 请给我您的存折和身份证件。

column1: Used to add the reason for what you just said. It tells something the listener does not know. It feels like "…, you see" or "because…" in English.
column2: 用于补充说明刚才所说的话的理由，告诉对方不知道的情况。感觉像中文的 "……嘛" 或 "因为……"。

column1: -거든요 adds the reason for what was said before, after it.
column2: -거든요 在后面补充说明前面那句话的理由。

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-거든요". For the past, use "-았/었거든요"; for nouns, use "(이)거든요".
column2: 去掉 "-다"，加上 "-거든요"。过去的事用 "-았/었거든요"；名词用 "(이)거든요"。

column1: The reason comes after. The order is the opposite of "-아서/어서": "약속이 있어서 일찍 가요" = "일찍 가요. 약속이 있거든요."
column2: 理由放在后面，和 "-아서/어서" 的顺序相反："약속이 있어서 일찍 가요" = "일찍 가요. 약속이 있거든요." (我早点走。因为我有约嘛。)

column1: I'm leaving early today. I have plans, you see.
column2: 我今天早点走。我有约嘛。

column1: I won't eat. I ate a little while ago, you see.
column2: 我不吃了。我刚才吃过了嘛。

column1: I'm not sure. It's my first time here, you see.
column2: 我不太清楚。我是第一次来这里嘛。

column1: I'm a little tired these days. I have a lot of assignments, you see.
column2: 我最近有点累。作业太多了嘛。
因为 (我) 已经吃过了嘛

column1: because it's (my) first time, you see
column2: 因为是 (我) 第一次嘛

column1: Sam, aren't you going to the club meeting today?
column2: 山姆，你今天不去社团聚会吗？

column1: No, I can't go. I'm not feeling well, you see.
column2: 嗯，去不了。我身体有点不舒服。

column1: (몸이 안 좋다 = to not feel well)
column2: 好 (몸이 안 좋다 = 身体不舒服)

column1: I've had a headache since yesterday, you see.
Used to give the reason for a good result, with thanks. It is like "thanks to…" in English.
column2: 用于带着感谢说明好结果的原因。相当于中文的 "多亏了……，托……的福"。

column1: 덕분에 gives the reason for a good result, with thanks.
column2: 덕분에 带着感谢说明好结果的原因。

column1: After a 받침 add "-은 덕분에"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ 덕분에". For nouns, use "noun + 덕분에".
column2: 有韵尾加 "-은 덕분에"；没有韵尾加 "-ㄴ 덕분에"。名词用 "名词 + 덕분에"。

column1: Use it only for good things. For bad things, use "때문에" or "-는 바람에".
column2: 只用于好事。坏事用 "때문에" 或 "-는 바람에"。

column1: 덕분에 잘 지냈어요 and "덕분입니다" are set phrases used to answer "How have you been?"
column2: 덕분에 잘 지냈어요、"덕분입니다" 是回答 "过得好吗？" 的固定说法。

column1: Thanks to your help, we finished quickly.
column2: 多亏你帮忙，我们很快就做完了。

column1: Thanks to the professor, I learned Korean well.
column2: 多亏了教授，我学好了韩语。

column1: I've been well, thanks to you.
Thanks to practicing hard, I passed the test.
column2: 多亏努力练习，我通过了考试。

column1: Sam, you got 100 points on this exam. Well done.
column2: 山姆，你这次考试得了100分。很棒。

column1: Thank you. It's thanks to Jinha teaching me well.
column2: 谢谢。这都多亏了珍夏教得好。

column1: to give (-아/어 주다 = do for someone)
Keep working hard from now on too.
A verb describes a noun. It shows something happening now or done regularly. It is like "the … who/that …" in English.
column2: 用动词来修饰名词，表示现在正在发生或经常做的事。相当于中文的 "……的 + 名词"。
动词 + -는 + 名词 意思是 "动词 + 的 + 名词"。

column1: Take "-다" off verbs and "있다/없다", add "-는", then put the noun. A ㄹ 받침 drops (살다 → 사는).
column2: 去掉动词和 "있다/없다" 的 "-다"，加上 "-는"，后面接名词。韵尾 ㄹ 会脱落 (살다 → 사는)。

column1: In English the describing part comes after the noun (a person who works), but in Korean it comes before (일하는 사람). There is no separate word for "who, that".
column2: 和中文一样，修饰部分放在名词前面 (工作的人 = 일하는 사람)。韩语不用 "的"，而是在动词后面加 "-는"。

column1: 맛있다, 재미있다 also end in "있다", so they use "-는": "맛있는 음식" (tasty food), "재미없는 영화" (a boring movie).
column2: 맛있다、재미있다 也以 "있다" 结尾，所以用 "-는"："맛있는 음식" (好吃的食物)，"재미없는 영화" (无聊的电影)。

column1: What is the work you are doing now?
column2: 你现在做的是什么工作？

column1: The person standing over there is the teaching assistant.
The place where I live is Jeonju.
If there is something you don't know, ask.
column2: 有不知道的东西就问吧。

column1: Who is the person wearing a hat over there?
That's Aisha, who studies with me.
column2: 是和我一起学习的爱莎。

column1: What part-time job does Aisha do?
She makes coffee at a cafe.
It is used in two ways: ① An adjective describes a noun (큰 상자, a big box). ② Added to a verb, it shows the past (어제 만난 사람, the person I met yesterday).
column2: 有两种用法：① 形容词修饰名词 (큰 상자 大箱子)。② 加在动词后面表示过去 (어제 만난 사람 昨天见的人)。

column1: Adjective + "-(으)ㄴ" describes; verb + "-(으)ㄴ" shows the past.
column2: 形容词 + "-(으)ㄴ" 表示修饰；动词 + "-(으)ㄴ" 表示过去。

column1: After a 받침 add "-은"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ". A ㄹ 받침 drops (길다 → 긴), and ㅂ irregular becomes "-운" (덥다 → 더운).
column2: 有韵尾加 "-은"，没有韵尾加 "-ㄴ"。韵尾 ㄹ 会脱落 (길다 → 긴)，ㅂ 不规则变成 "-운" (덥다 → 더운)。

column1: As in English "big box", the adjective comes before the noun, but in Korean the adjective changes its form (크다 → 큰 상자).
column2: 和中文 "大箱子" 一样，形容词放在名词前面，但韩语的形容词要变形 (크다 → 큰 상자)。

column1: It is the same "-(으)ㄴ", but with adjectives it is a present quality, and with verbs it is the past: "바쁜 사람" (a busy person), "온 사람" (a person who came).
column2: 同样是 "-(으)ㄴ"，用于形容词时表示现在的性质，用于动词时表示过去："바쁜 사람" (忙碌的人)，"온 사람" (来了的人)。

column1: Who is the person you met yesterday?
The shoes I bought last week are small.
Sam, where are the books you borrowed yesterday?
column2: 山姆，你昨天借的书在哪里？

column1: I put them in that big box.
column2: 我放进那个大箱子里了。

column1: Did you put the small ones in too?
column2: 小的也一起放进去了吗？

column1: No, I put the small ones in the blue box.
column2: 没有，小的我放进蓝色箱子里了。

column1: Describes a noun with something you will do or that has not happened yet. It is like "… to do, … that (I) will…" in English.
column2: 用将要做的或还没发生的事来修饰名词。相当于中文的 "要……的 + 名词"。

column1: Verb + -(으)ㄹ + noun means "noun + to + verb" (work to do).
column2: 动词 + -(으)ㄹ + 名词 意思是 "要 + 动词 + 的 + 名词" (要做的事)。

column1: After a 받침 add "-을"; with no 받침 add "-ㄹ". A ㄹ 받침 stays as it is (만들다 → 만들).
column2: 有韵尾加 "-을"，没有韵尾加 "-ㄹ"。韵尾 ㄹ 保持不变 (만들다 → 만들)。

column1: Compare the three forms: 하는 일 (work I'm doing), 한 일 (work I did), 할 일 (work I will do).
column2: 比较这三种形式：하는 일 (正在做的事)，한 일 (做过的事)，할 일 (要做的事)。

column1: After "-(으)ㄹ", ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅅ, ㅈ become tense sounds: 갈 곳 [갈 꼳], 먹을 것 [머글 껃].
column2: -(으)ㄹ 后面的 ㄱ、ㄷ、ㅂ、ㅅ、ㅈ 变成紧音：갈 곳 [갈 꼳]，먹을 것 [머글 껃]。

column1: -(으)ㄹ 때, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 all come from this form.
column2: -(으)ㄹ 때、-(으)ㄹ 수 있다、-(으)ㄹ 거예요 都是从这个形式来的。

column1: I have a lot of work to do tomorrow.
I have no time to rest.
I have something to tell you. (humble)
I'll tell you the work to do today.
column2: 我来告诉你今天要做的事。

column1: This morning there are 50 cups to wash.
I understand. Is there work to do in the afternoon too?
column2: 明白了。下午也有要做的事吗？

column1: Lets a verb be used like a noun. It is like "…ing" (cooking) or "to…" in English.
column2: 让动词可以像名词一样使用。中文的动词可以直接当名词用 (如 "做饭很有意思")，韩语则要变换形式。
动词 + -는 것 把动词变成名词，意思是 "……(这件事)"。

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-는 것". In speech, shorten "것이 → 게", "것을 → 걸", "것은 → 건".
column2: 去掉动词的 "-다"，加上 "-는 것"。说话时缩略为 "것이 → 게"、"것을 → 걸"、"것은 → 건"。

column1: Like English "-ing", "-는 것" comes after the verb: "learning" = "배우는 것".
column2: 中文的动词可以直接当名词用，而韩语要在动词后面加 "-는 것"："学习" = "배우는 것"。

column1: It is often used before "좋아하다, 싫어하다, 잘하다, 못하다": "운전하는 것을 잘해요." (I'm good at driving.)
column2: 常用在 "좋아하다、싫어하다、잘하다、못하다" 前面："운전하는 것을 잘해요." (我很会开车。)

column1: 것 also means "thing, one": "이것, 그것, 먹을 것, 큰 것" (this, that, something to eat, a big one).
column2: 것 也有 "东西，……的" 的意思："이것、그것、먹을 것、큰 것" (这个、那个、吃的东西、大的)。

column1: Sam, what do you like to do on your days off?
column2: 山姆，休息日你喜欢做什么？

column1: I like playing soccer. What about you, Minha?
column2: 我喜欢踢足球。敏夏你呢？

column1: I like watching movies at home.
-기 also turns a verb into a noun. Before "쉽다, 어렵다, 좋다, 편하다, 힘들다" it means "easy/hard/good… to do".
column2: -기 也能把动词变成名词。在 "쉽다、어렵다、좋다、편하다、힘들다" 前面，表示 "做起来容易/难/好……"。
动词 + -기 쉽다/어렵다 意思是 "容易/难 + 动词"。

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-기". It does not depend on 받침.
column2: 去掉动词的 "-다"，加上 "-기"。和有没有韵尾无关。

column1: The order is the opposite of English "hard to learn": add "-기" to the verb and put "어렵다, 쉽다" after it. "hard to learn" = "배우기 어려워요".
column2: 中文说 "难学"，"难" 放在前面；韩语则是在动词后加 "-기"，再接 "어렵다、쉽다"："难学" = "배우기 어려워요"。

column1: In lists, titles and notes, end with "-기": "말하기 (speaking), 듣기 (listening), 읽기 (reading), 쓰기 (writing)", "과제 내기" (hand in the assignment), "손 씻기" (wash hands).
column2: 在清单、标题和笔记中用 "-기" 结尾："말하기 (口语)、듣기 (听力)、읽기 (阅读)、쓰기 (写作)"，"과제 내기" (交作业)，"손 씻기" (洗手)。

column1: This laptop is easy to use.
column2: 这台笔记本电脑很好用。

column1: This neighborhood is a good place to live.
It's hot today, so it's hard to study.
column2: 今天很热，所以很难学习。

column1: How is your Korean study going?
Reading is easy, but speaking is hard.
column2: 阅读很容易，但口语很难。

column1: ㅓ and "ㅗ" are hard to tell apart.
Turns an adjective into a word that tells "how" something is done. It is like "-ly" (safely, loudly) in English.
column2: 把形容词变成表示 "怎样" 做某事的词。相当于中文的 "……地" (安全地、大声地)。

column1: Adjective + -게 + verb means "verb + -ly" (speak loudly, ride safely).
column2: 形容词 + -게 + 动词 意思是 "……地 + 动词" (大声地说、安全地骑)。

column1: Take "-다" off the adjective and add "-게". It does not depend on 받침.
column2: 去掉形容词的 "-다"，加上 "-게"。和有没有韵尾无关。

column1: In English it often comes after the verb (wipe it clean, speak loudly), but in Korean it comes before the verb (깨끗하게 닦아요).
column2: 和中文的 "……地 + 动词" 一样，韩语也放在动词前面 (깨끗하게 닦아요 擦干净)。

column1: Some words use another form instead of "-게": 많다 → 많이, 빠르다 → 빨리, 멀다 → 멀리, 깨끗하다 → 깨끗이 (깨끗하게 is also fine).
column2: 有些词不用 "-게"，而用别的形式：많다 → 많이，빠르다 → 빨리，멀다 → 멀리，깨끗하다 → 깨끗이 (깨끗하게 也可以)。

column1: Sam, please wipe this table cleaner.
column2: 山姆，请把这张桌子擦得更干净一些。

column1: Yes. Is this okay? (Should I do it like this?)
Good. And don't stack the cups high.
column2: 很好。还有，杯子不要叠得太高。

column1: Tells the time when something happens. It is like "when" in English.
column2: 表示事情发生的时间。相当于中文的 "……的时候"。
动词 + -(으)ㄹ 때 意思是 "动词 + 的时候"。

column1: After a 받침 add "-을 때"; with no 받침 add "-ㄹ 때". For the past, use "-았/었을 때"; for nouns, use "noun + 때".
column2: 有韵尾加 "-을 때"，没有韵尾加 "-ㄹ 때"。过去的事用 "-았/었을 때"；名词用 "名词 + 때"。

column1: English "when" comes first, but "-(으)ㄹ 때" is added at the end: "when eating" = "먹을 때".
column2: 和中文的 "……的时候" 一样，"-(으)ㄹ 때" 加在后面："吃饭的时候" = "먹을 때"。

column1: 갈 때 is on the way there; "갔을 때" is after you get there: "집에 갈 때 샀어요" (I bought it on my way home), "집에 갔을 때 없었어요" (When I got home, it wasn't there).
column2: 갈 때 是去的路上；"갔을 때" 是到了之后："집에 갈 때 샀어요" (我在回家的路上买的)，"집에 갔을 때 없었어요" (我到家时它不在)。

column1: It is the basic pattern of rules and notices: "~할 때는 ~하십시오." (When you…, do….)
column2: 这是规则和通知的基本句型："~할 때는 ~하십시오." (……的时候，请……。)

column1: I drink a lot of water when I exercise.
column2: 运动的时候我会喝很多水。

column1: When you are sick, you have to rest.
When I first came to Korea, it was very cold.
column2: 我刚来韩国的时候很冷。

column1: Call me when you have time.
column2: 有时间的时候给我打电话吧。

column1: What should I do when I lift something heavy?
column2: 搬重东西的时候应该怎么做？

column1: Keep your back straight, bend your knees and lift.
Right. When it's hard to lift alone, be sure to ask for help.
column2: 对。一个人搬不动的时候，一定要请别人帮忙。

column1: to ask (for something) (-아/어 달라고 = ask someone to…)
Tells your feeling about something you just found out by seeing or hearing it. It is like "Oh, …!" or "…, isn't it!" in English.
column2: 表示对刚刚看到或听到而得知的事情的感受。相当于中文的 "哦，……啊！" 或 "……呢！"。

column1: -네요 shows your feeling about something you have just found out.
column2: -네요 表示对刚刚得知的事的感受。

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-네요". A ㄹ 받침 drops (멀다 → 머네요). For the past, use "-았/었네요"; for nouns, use "(이)네요".
column2: 去掉 "-다"，加上 "-네요"。韵尾 ㄹ 会脱落 (멀다 → 머네요)。过去的事用 "-았/었네요"；名词用 "(이)네요"。

column1: The sound changes: 좋네요 [존네요], 맛있네요 [마신네요], 춥네요 [춤네요].
When you get a compliment, answer "아니에요, 아직 멀었어요" (No, I still have a long way to go) or "감사합니다".
column2: 受到称赞时，回答 "아니에요, 아직 멀었어요" (哪里，我还差得远呢) 或 "감사합니다"。

column1: It is not used for things you already knew.
column2: 不用于自己早就知道的事。

column1: Sam, you've already finished it all! You're fast!
column2: 山姆，你已经全都做完了！手真快啊！

column1: No. I still have a long way to go.
Your Korean has improved a lot too!
column2: 你的韩语也进步了很多啊！

column1: Used to check something you think the listener also knows, or to ask them to agree. It is like "…, right?" or "…, isn't it?" in English.
column2: 用于确认你认为对方也知道的事，或请对方表示同意。相当于中文的 "……吧？" 或 "……对吧？"。

column1: -지요? is a checking question, like "…, right?".
column2: -지요? 是确认性的问句，相当于 "……对吧？"。

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-지요?". In speech it is shortened to "-죠?". For nouns, use "(이)지요?".
column2: 去掉 "-다"，加上 "-지요?"。说话时缩略为 "-죠?"。名词用 "(이)지요?"。

column1: The answer is "네, 추워요" or "네, 맞아요". If not, say "아니요, 괜찮아요".
column2: 回答是 "네, 추워요" 或 "네, 맞아요"。如果不是，就说 "아니요, 괜찮아요"。

column1: With question words it becomes a soft question: "이게 얼마지요?" (How much is this?), "화장실이 어디죠?" (Where is the restroom?)
column2: 和疑问词一起使用时，就成了柔和的问句："이게 얼마지요?" (这个多少钱？)，"화장실이 어디죠?" (洗手间在哪里？)

column1: When a Korean says "힘들지요?", it is a greeting that shows care. You can just answer "괜찮습니다".
column2: 韩国人说 "힘들지요?" (很辛苦吧？) 时，是表示关心的问候。回答 "괜찮습니다" 就可以了。

column1: There's a group meeting tomorrow, right?
Sam, this is your first Korean winter, right?
column2: 山姆，这是你第一次在韩国过冬吧？

column1: Yes, it's cold, but the snow is pretty.
column2: 是的，虽然冷，但雪很漂亮。

column1: Tells a guess based on what you see or hear. It is like "I think…, It seems…" in English.
column2: 表示根据所见所闻做出的推测。相当于中文的 "我觉得……，好像……"。

column1: -는 것 같아요 means "I think…, It seems…" and tells a guess.
column2: -는 것 같아요 意思是 "我觉得……，好像……"，表示推测。

column1: Add "-는 것 같아요" to verbs, "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요" to adjectives, "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요" for the past (verbs), and "noun + 같아요" to nouns.
column2: 动词加 "-는 것 같아요"，形容词加 "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요"，过去的事 (动词) 加 "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요"，名词加 "名词 + 같아요"。

column1: It is also used to give your opinion softly. "이게 더 좋은 것 같아요" (I think this is better) sounds less stiff than "이게 더 좋아요".
column2: 也用于委婉地表达自己的意见。"이게 더 좋은 것 같아요" (我觉得这个更好) 比 "이게 더 좋아요" 听起来不那么生硬。

column1: It is useful for reporting problems: "소리가 이상한 것 같습니다" (The sound seems strange), "고장 난 것 같습니다" (It seems to be broken).
column2: 用于报告问题时很有用："소리가 이상한 것 같습니다" (声音好像有点奇怪)，"고장 난 것 같습니다" (好像坏了)。

column1: In speech, "것" is shortened to "거": "오는 거 같아요".
column2: 说话时把 "것" 缩略为 "거"："오는 거 같아요"。

column1: It seems to be raining outside.
I think this printer is broken.
I think I've caught a cold.
Excuse me (TA), I think this printer is making a strange sound.
column2: 助教，这台打印机好像发出了奇怪的声音。

column1: (a sound) to come out, be made

column2: 是吗？从什么时候开始的？

column1: I think since ten minutes ago.
column2: 好像是从十分钟前开始的。

column1: Turn it off for now. It seems the paper is stuck.
A guess that something will happen. It is like "I think … will…, It looks like… will…, probably" in English.
column2: 推测某事将会发生。相当于中文的 "我看……会……，大概……"。

column1: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 means "I think … will…, probably".
column2: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 意思是 "我看……会……，大概……"。

column1: After a 받침 add "-을 것 같아요"; with no 받침 add "-ㄹ 것 같아요".
column2: 有韵尾加 "-을 것 같아요"，没有韵尾加 "-ㄹ 것 같아요"。

column1: It is a soft way to say no or give bad news. "못 갈 것 같아요" (I don't think I can go) is more polite than "못 가요".
column2: 这是拒绝或告知坏消息时的委婉说法。"못 갈 것 같아요" (我恐怕去不了) 比 "못 가요" 更礼貌。

column1: When you will be late, always tell them in advance: "차가 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같습니다." (There's traffic, so I think I'll be a little late.)
column2: 要迟到时一定要提前告知："차가 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같습니다." (堵车了，我可能会晚一点到。)

column1: It is also used for a guess from what you see in front of you. Seeing food, you say "맛있을 것 같아요" (It looks tasty).
column2: 也用于根据眼前看到的东西做推测。看到食物时说 "맛있을 것 같아요" (看起来很好吃)。

column1: I'm sorry. I think I'll be about ten minutes late.
column2: 对不起。我可能会晚到十分钟左右。

column1: It looks like it's going to rain.
I think it will be finished today.
I don't think I can go tomorrow.
It looks like it will rain
It looks like it will be tasty
I think it will be finished
I think it will be hard
Professor, I'm sorry. The bus isn't coming, so I think I'll be a little late.
column2: 教授，对不起。公交车一直没来，我可能会晚一点到。

column1: How late do you think you'll be?
I think it will take about twenty minutes.
Means it seems so from the outside. It is like "look…" (look tired) in English.
column2: 表示从外表看起来是那样。相当于中文的 "看起来……" (看起来很累)。
形容词 + -아/어 보여요 意思是 "看起来 + 形容词"。

column1: Take "요" off the adjective's "-아요/어요" form and add "보여요".
column2: 去掉形容词 "-아요/어요" 形式中的 "요"，加上 "보여요"。

column1: It is used only with adjectives. With verbs, use "-는 것 같아요".
column2: 只用于形容词。动词用 "-는 것 같아요"。

column1: It is only for what you see with your eyes. For what you know by hearing or tasting, use "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요".
column2: 只用于眼睛看到的。通过听或尝而知道的，要用 "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요"。

column1: When a friend says "피곤해 보여요" or "아파 보여요", they are showing they care about you.
column2: 朋友说 "피곤해 보여요" (你看起来很累) 或 "아파 보여요" (你看起来不舒服) 时，是在表示关心。

column1: You look like you're in a good mood.
You don't look well. Are you sick?
column2: 你脸色不太好。哪里不舒服吗？

column1: Sam, you look very tired today.
column2: 山姆，你今天看起来很累。

column1: Yes, I studied for an exam until late last night, so I couldn't sleep.
column2: 是的，我昨晚复习考试到很晚，没睡好。

column1: You don't look well either. Rest early today.
column2: 你脸色也不太好。今天早点休息吧。

column1: Used to remind the listener of something they already know. It feels like "…, you know" or "As you know…".
column2: 用于提醒对方他们已经知道的事。感觉像中文的 "……嘛" 或 "你也知道……"。

column1: -잖아요 reminds the other person of something they also know, and is not used with seniors.
column2: -잖아요 用于提醒对方也知道的事，不能对长辈或上级使用。

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-잖아요". For the past, use "-았/었잖아요"; for nouns, use "(이)잖아요".
column2: 去掉 "-다"，加上 "-잖아요"。过去的事用 "-았/었잖아요"；名词用 "(이)잖아요"。

column1: Used with seniors, it sounds like you are arguing. Use it only with close friends; don't use it with professors.
column2: 对长辈或上级使用，听起来像在争辩。只在亲近的朋友之间用，不要对教授用。

column1: 있잖아요 is also used to start talking: "저, 있잖아요…" = Um, you know…
column2: 있잖아요 也用来开启话题："저, 있잖아요…" = 那个，我跟你说……

column1: It's cold outside, you know. Put on more clothes.
column2: 外面很冷嘛。多穿点衣服。

column1: There's a test tomorrow, you know.
I told you yesterday, you know.
column2: 我昨天就跟你说过了嘛。

column1: Sam, why aren't you going to school today?
column2: 山姆，你今天为什么不去学校？

column1: Today is a day off, you know.
Oh, right. It's the school's founding day!
column2: 啊，对了。今天是校庆日呢。

column1: Shows the feeling "Oh, I see" about something you have just learned. It is like "Oh, I see. / So…!" in English.
column2: 表示对刚刚得知的事 "哦，原来如此" 的感受。相当于中文的 "哦，原来如此。/ 原来……啊！"。

column1: -군요 is a feeling about something you just realized, and "그렇군요" is a reply (Oh, I see).
column2: -군요 是对刚意识到的事的感受，"그렇군요" 是附和的话 (哦，原来如此)。

column1: Add "-는군요" to verbs, "-군요" to adjectives, "-았/었군요" for the past, and "(이)군요" to nouns.
column2: 动词加 "-는군요"，形容词加 "-군요"，过去的事加 "-았/었군요"，名词加 "(이)군요"。

column1: 아, 그렇군요 is a reply that means you understood after hearing an explanation. It is used very often.
column2: 아, 그렇군요 是听了解释后表示明白了的附和语。非常常用。

column1: -네요 is a feeling you have right now; "-군요" is something you realize by hearing or thinking. "-군요" is a little more polite.
column2: -네요 是当下直接的感受；"-군요" 是通过听或思考而意识到的。"-군요" 稍微更稳重一些。

column1: So you've already finished it all!
column2: 原来你已经全都做完了！

column1: Oh, so your hometown is Yangon.
column2: 原来你的家乡是仰光啊。

column1: to be so, be like that
Sam, what work did you do in the USA?
column2: 山姆，你在美国做过什么工作？

column1: I worked part-time at a hotel for one year.
Oh, I see. So that's why you know hotel work well.
column2: 哦，原来如此。所以你很了解酒店的工作啊。

column1: Used to pass on what someone else said or what you heard. It is like "(He) said that…, I heard that…" in English.
column2: 用于转述别人说的话或听到的话。相当于中文的 "(他) 说……，听说……"。

column1: Pass on what you heard with "-다고 했어요".
column2: 用 "-다고 했어요" 转述听到的话。

column1: For verbs add "-는다고" after a 받침 and "-ㄴ다고" with no 받침; for adjectives "-다고"; for the past "-았/었다고"; for the future "-(으)ㄹ 거라고"; for nouns "(이)라고", then use "해요/했어요".
column2: 动词有韵尾加 "-는다고"，没有韵尾加 "-ㄴ다고"；形容词加 "-다고"；过去的事加 "-았/었다고"；将来的事加 "-(으)ㄹ 거라고"；名词加 "(이)라고"，然后接 "해요/했어요"。

column1: In English "said (that)" comes first, but in Korean the reported words come first and "-다고 했어요" comes at the end.
column2: 中文的 "他说" 放在前面，而韩语是转述的内容在前，"-다고 했어요" 放在最后。

column1: To give your name, say "저는 샘이라고 합니다" (I'm called Sam). "이것은 한국어로 뭐라고 해요?" (What is this called in Korean?) uses the same pattern.
column2: 介绍名字时说 "저는 샘이라고 합니다" (我叫山姆)。"이것은 한국어로 뭐라고 해요?" (这个用韩语怎么说？) 也是同样的句型。

column1: It is very important when interpreting or passing on what the professor said to friends.
column2: 做口译或向朋友转达教授的话时一定用得到。

column1: The teaching assistant said he is off tomorrow.
Aisha said she is busy today.
The weather forecast said it will rain tomorrow.
column2: 天气预报说明天会下雨。

column1: Sam, what did the professor say?
He said the library is closed tomorrow.
He said they are checking the computers.
Used to pass on someone else's order. It is like "(He) told me to…" in English.
column2: 用于转述别人的命令。相当于中文的 "(他) 叫我……"。

column1: Pass on orders with "-(으)라고 했어요", and "don't" orders with "-지 말라고 했어요".
column2: 转述命令用 "-(으)라고 했어요"，转述禁止用 "-지 말라고 했어요"。

column1: After a 받침 add "-으라고"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-라고". For "not to", use "-지 말라고".
column2: 有韵尾加 "-으라고"；没有韵尾或韵尾是 ㄹ 时加 "-라고"。"叫别人不要……" 用 "-지 말라고"。

column1: To pass on "-아/어 주세요", use "-아/어 달라고 하다" (for the speaker) and "-아/어 주라고 하다" (for someone else): "도와 달라고 했어요" = He asked (me) to help him.
column2: 转述 "-아/어 주세요" 时，为说话人自己做的事用 "-아/어 달라고 하다"，为别人做的事用 "-아/어 주라고 하다"："도와 달라고 했어요" = 他请 (我) 帮他。

column1: To check an instruction again, ask "~(으)라고 하셨지요?": "세 시까지 끝내라고 하셨지요?" (You told me to finish by three, right?)
column2: 再次确认指示时问 "~(으)라고 하셨지요?"："세 시까지 끝내라고 하셨지요?" (您是说让我三点前做完，对吧？)

column1: The professor told me to wait.
The doctor told me to take the medicine.
The head of the department told you to come to the department office.
column2: 系主任让你到系办公室去。

column1: They told us not to touch this computer.
column2: 他们叫我们不要碰这台电脑。

column1: (He) told me not to touch it
(He) asked (me) to give it to him
He told me to move this box to the department office.
column2: 他叫我把这个箱子搬到系办公室。

column1: No, he told me not to touch that one.
Used to pass on a suggestion. It is like "(He) suggested…, (He) said let's…" in English.
column2: 用于转述别人的提议。相当于中文的 "(他) 提议……，(他) 说我们……吧"。

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-자고 해요/했어요". It does not depend on 받침. For "let's not", use "-지 말자고".
column2: 去掉动词的 "-다"，加上 "-자고 해요/했어요"。和有没有韵尾无关。"我们别……" 用 "-지 말자고"。

column1: When passing on "-(으)ㅂ시다, -아요/어요 (let's), -(으)ㄹ까요?", they all become "-자고 하다".
column2: 转述 "-(으)ㅂ시다、-아요/어요 (……吧)、-(으)ㄹ까요?" 时，都变成 "-자고 하다"。

column1: If a senior said it, show respect with "-자고 하셨어요".
column2: 如果是长辈或上级说的，要用敬语 "-자고 하셨어요"。

column1: My senior says let's have an after-party today.
column2: 学长说今天一起去聚餐。

column1: Minha suggested going hiking on the weekend.

column2: 我朋友提议我们一起住。

column1: Aisha says let's rest a little.
column2: 爱莎说我们休息一会儿吧。

column1: Aisha, the professor suggested having dinner together tonight.
column2: 爱莎，教授说今晚一起吃晚饭。

column1: He said to meet at six at the samgyeopsal restaurant in front of the school.
column2: 他说六点在学校前面的五花肉店见。

column1: Used to pass on someone else's question. It is like "(He) asked…" in English.
column2: 用来转述别人的提问，相当于中文的 "(他)问…"。

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-냐고 하다/묻다/물어보다". For the past, use "-았/었냐고"; for nouns, use "(이)냐고".
column2: 去掉 "-다"，加上 "-냐고 하다/묻다/물어보다"。过去的事用 "-았/었냐고"，名词用 "(이)냐고"。

column1: Remember the four reporting forms together: statements "-다고", orders "-(으)라고", suggestions "-자고", questions "-냐고".
column2: 四种转述形式一起记：陈述 "-다고"，命令 "-(으)라고"，提议 "-자고"，提问 "-냐고"。

column1: When you didn't catch it, ask again: "지금 뭐라고 하셨어요?" (What did you just say?)
column2: 没听清时，再问一遍："지금 뭐라고 하셨어요?" (您刚才说什么？)

column1: The professor asked where I was sick.
The (shop) owner asked if I had eaten.
My friend asked how life in Korea is.
column2: 朋友问我在韩国的生活怎么样。

column1: What did the professor ask you, Sam?
He asked if I would take his class next semester too.
column2: 他问我下学期还会不会上他的课。

column1: I said I really want to take it.
These are short forms of reported speech. In speaking, these short forms are used much more.
column2: 这是转述句的缩略形式。说话时更常用这种短形式。

column1: -대요 is short for "-다고 해요", and "-(으)래요" is short for "-(으)라고 해요".
column2: -대요 是 "-다고 해요" 的缩略，"-(으)래요" 是 "-(으)라고 해요" 的缩略。

column1: It feels like English "I heard…, They say…", passing on what you heard.
column2: 感觉像中文的 "听说…，据说…"，用来转述听到的内容。

column1: -(으)ㄹ래요 (your own wish) and "-(으)래요" (passing on an order) are different: "갈래요" (I'll go), "가래요" (He says to go).
column2: -(으)ㄹ래요 (自己的意愿) 和 "-(으)래요" (转述命令) 不同："갈래요" (我要去)，"가래요" (他叫我去)。

column1: For the past, use "-았/었대요": "어제 조별 모임을 했대요." (I heard they had a group meeting yesterday.)
column2: 过去的事用 "-았/었대요"："어제 조별 모임을 했대요." (听说他们昨天开了小组会。)

column1: They say it will rain tomorrow.
The professor says to come quickly.
I heard Aisha is sick today.
Yes, I heard there is. They say there's a make-up class.
Until what time did they say it goes?
They said to stay in the classroom until six.
column2: 他们说在教室待到六点。

column1: Added to adjectives to show something gradually changes that way. It is like "get…, become…" (get colder) in English.
column2: 加在形容词后面，表示逐渐变成那样，相当于中文的 "变得…，…起来" (变冷了)。

column1: Adjective + -아/어지다 means it changes to that.
column2: 形容词 + -아/어지다 表示变成那样。

column1: Take "요" off the adjective's "-아요/어요" form and add "져요". For something already changed, use "-아/어졌어요".
column2: 去掉形容词 "-아요/어요" 形式中的 "요"，加上 "져요"。已经变化了的用 "-아/어졌어요"。

column1: English uses "get, become" (get colder, get fewer), and Korean uses "-아/어지다" for both: "get colder" = "추워지다", "get fewer" = "적어지다".
column2: 中文说 "变冷了、变少了"，韩语都用 "-아/어지다"："变冷" = "추워지다"，"变少" = "적어지다"。

column1: It is added only to adjectives. For change with verbs, use "-게 되다".
column2: 只加在形容词后面。动词表示变化时用 "-게 되다"。

column1: Your Korean skills have gotten much better.
column2: 你的韩语水平提高了很多。

column1: There have been more assignments lately.
I took medicine and got better.
Is your cold a bit better?
Yes, I took medicine and it got much better.
The weather suddenly got colder these days, didn't it?
column2: 最近天气突然变冷了，是吧？

column1: Yes, so more people have caught colds.
column2: 是啊，所以感冒的人变多了。

column1: Means things turned out that way, not by your own choice. It is like "came to…, ended up…, got to…" in English.
column2: 表示事情变成了那样，不是出于自己的选择，相当于中文的 "变得…，最后…，有机会…"。

column1: Verb + -게 됐어요 means things came to be that way.
column2: 动词 + -게 됐어요 表示事情变成了那样。

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-게 됐어요". It does not depend on 받침.
column2: 去掉动词的 "-다"，加上 "-게 됐어요"。与有无받침无关。

column1: It is used to humbly announce something that has been decided: "다음 달에 고향에 돌아가게 됐습니다." (I will be going back home next month.) It is common in farewell speeches.
column2: 用来谦虚地宣布已经决定的事："다음 달에 고향에 돌아가게 됐습니다." (我下个月要回国了。) 常用于告别致辞。
分开记："形容词 + -아/어지다"，"动词 + -게 되다"。

column1: I came to study in Korea.
I got to know Aisha at school.
At first I couldn't eat kimchi, but now I've come to like it.
column2: 一开始我不能吃泡菜，但现在喜欢上了。

column1: From next month, I will be living in the dormitory.
column2: 从下个月开始，我要住宿舍了。

column1: I came to know, I found out
I got to go, I ended up going
column2: 我有机会去了，我最后去了

column1: It turned out I can't go
Sam, how did you come to Korea?
column2: 山姆，你是怎么来韩国的？

column1: I was accepted to Jeonju University, so I came.
column2: 我被全州大学录取了，所以就来了。

column1: How did you come to learn Korean?
column2: 你是怎么开始学韩语的？

column1: I watched Korean dramas and came to like it.
column2: 我看了韩剧，就喜欢上了。

column1: Means you do something and leave the result as it is. Used when preparing something in advance. It is like "leave it (open), do it in advance" in English.
column2: 表示做完某事后让结果保持原样。用于提前准备某事，相当于中文的 "(开)着放，提前做好"。

column1: Verb + -아/어 놓다 means "leave it…, do it in advance".
column2: 动词 + -아/어 놓다 表示 "放着…，提前做好…"。

column1: Take "요" off the verb's "-아요/어요" form and add "놓다". "-아/어 두다" means the same.
column2: 去掉动词 "-아요/어요" 形式中的 "요"，加上 "놓다"。"-아/어 두다" 意思相同。

column1: It is used much like English "leave… open, have… ready": "leave it open" = "열어 놓다".
column2: 用法很像中文的 "…着、…好"："开着" = "열어 놓다"。

column1: In speech, "놓아" is shortened to "놔": "열어 놔요", "해 놨어요".
column2: 说话时 "놓아" 缩成 "놔"："열어 놔요"，"해 놨어요"。

column1: You often hear it in instructions: "미리 해 놓으세요" (Do it in advance), "여기에 놓아 두세요" (Leave it here).
column2: 在指示中经常听到："미리 해 놓으세요" (请提前做好)，"여기에 놓아 두세요" (请放在这里)。

column1: I have the materials for tomorrow's presentation ready.
column2: 明天发表的资料我已经准备好了。

column1: Don't leave the computer on and walk away.
Sam, did you get the chairs ready for tomorrow morning?
column2: 山姆，明天早上用的椅子准备好了吗？

column1: Yes, I stacked them in front of the lecture room.
column2: 嗯，我把它们摞在讲堂前面了。

column1: Well done. When you leave, close the windows.
column2: 做得好。走的时候把窗户关上。

column1: Means that after something is done, the state stays. It is like "is open, is sitting" in English.
column2: 表示动作完成后状态保持着，相当于中文的 "开着，坐着"。

column1: -아/어 있다 shows that the state after an action stays.
column2: -아/어 있다 表示动作完成后状态持续。

column1: Take "요" off the verb's "-아요/어요" form and add "있어요". It is used with verbs like "열리다, 닫히다, 켜지다, 꺼지다, 앉다, 서다, 걸리다, 놓이다, 쓰이다".
column2: 去掉动词 "-아요/어요" 形式中的 "요"，加上 "있어요"。用于 "열리다，닫히다，켜지다，꺼지다，앉다，서다，걸리다，놓이다，쓰이다" 等动词。

column1: -고 있다 is an action in progress; "-아/어 있다" is the state after it is done: "문을 열고 있어요" (I'm opening the door), "문이 열려 있어요" (The door is open).
column2: -고 있다 是正在进行的动作；"-아/어 있다" 是动作完成后的状态："문을 열고 있어요" (我正在开门)，"문이 열려 있어요" (门开着)。

column1: What someone did and left is "-아/어 놓다" (a person is the subject); the result is "-아/어 있다" (a thing is the subject): "문을 열어 놓았어요. 문이 열려 있어요." (I left the door open. The door is open.)
column2: 某人做了并保持原样用 "-아/어 놓다" (主语是人)；结果用 "-아/어 있다" (主语是物)："문을 열어 놓았어요. 문이 열려 있어요." (我把门开着了。门开着。)

column1: The professor is sitting over there.
Sam, did you check before leaving?
Yes, all the computers are off.
to go off, be turned off
One was open, so I closed it.
When a word's stem ends in "ㅡ", the "ㅡ" drops when "-아/어" is added.
column2: 词干以 "ㅡ" 结尾时，加 "-아/어" 时 "ㅡ" 脱落。

column1: A stem ending in "ㅡ" drops "ㅡ" before "-아/어".
column2: 以 "ㅡ" 结尾的词干在 "-아/어" 前 "ㅡ" 脱落。

column1: Drop "ㅡ". If the vowel of the syllable before it is ㅏ or ㅗ, add "-아요"; otherwise, or if there is no syllable before it, add "-어요": 바쁘다 → 바빠요, 예쁘다 → 예뻐요, 쓰다 → 써요.
column2: 去掉 "ㅡ"。如果前一个音节的元音是 ㅏ 或 ㅗ，加 "-아요"；否则或前面没有音节时，加 "-어요"：바쁘다 → 바빠요，예쁘다 → 예뻐요，쓰다 → 써요。

column1: It changes only before endings that start with "-아/어". It does not change before "-고, -지만, -습니다, -(으)면": 바쁘고, 바쁩니다, 바쁘면.
column2: 只在以 "-아/어" 开头的词尾前变化。在 "-고，-지만，-습니다，-(으)면" 前不变：바쁘고，바쁩니다，바쁘면。

column1: The past is the same: 바빴어요, 아팠어요, 썼어요, 컸어요.
This rule has no exceptions, so it is called "탈락" (dropping), not "irregular".
column2: 这条规则没有例外，所以叫 "탈락" (脱落)，而不叫 "不规则"。

column1: I had a headache, so I took medicine.
Sam, are you busy these days?
Yes, very busy. Yesterday my back hurt too.
When a word's stem ends in a ㄹ 받침, the ㄹ drops before endings that start with ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ.
column2: 词干以 ㄹ 받침结尾时，在以 ㄴ、ㅂ、ㅅ 开头的词尾前 ㄹ 脱落。

column1: A ㄹ 받침 drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ.
column2: ㄹ 받침在 ㄴ、ㅂ、ㅅ 前脱落。

column1: 살다 + -ㅂ니다 → 삽니다, 살다 + -세요 → 사세요, 살다 + -는 → 사는, 살다 + -니까 → 사니까. With "-(으)" endings, do not add "으" (살면, 살러, 살려고).
column2: 살다 + -ㅂ니다 → 삽니다，살다 + -세요 → 사세요，살다 + -는 → 사는，살다 + -니까 → 사니까。遇到 "-(으)" 词尾时不加 "으" (살면，살러，살려고)。

column1: It does not drop before "-아요/어요, -고, -지만": 살아요, 살고, 살지만.
With "-(으)ㄹ" endings, only one ㄹ remains: 살 거예요, 만들 수 있어요, 알 때.
column2: 遇到 "-(으)ㄹ" 词尾时只保留一个 ㄹ：살 거예요，만들 수 있어요，알 때。

column1: Common words with a ㄹ 받침: 살다, 알다, 만들다, 열다, 팔다, 놀다, 울다, 들다, 걸다, 멀다, 길다, 힘들다.
I don't know a single person.
column2: 我一个认识的人都没有。

column1: If you open the door, it gets cold.
Do you know anyone in Korea?
column2: 你在韩国有认识的人吗？

column1: Yes, my older cousin lives in Jeonju.
Many adjectives whose stem ends in a ㅂ 받침 change ㅂ to "우" before a vowel.
column2: 很多词干以 ㅂ 받침结尾的形容词，在元音前 ㅂ 变成 "우"。

column1: In ㅂ irregular words, ㅂ changes to "우" before a vowel.
column2: ㅂ 不规则词在元音前 ㅂ 变成 "우"。

column1: 덥다 + -어요 → 더워요, 덥다 + -(으)면 → 더우면, 덥다 + -(으)ㄴ → 더운, 덥다 + -(으)니까 → 더우니까. Only "돕다, 곱다" become "도와요, 고와요".
column2: 덥다 + -어요 → 더워요，덥다 + -(으)면 → 더우면，덥다 + -(으)ㄴ → 더운，덥다 + -(으)니까 → 더우니까。只有 "돕다，곱다" 变成 "도와요，고와요"。

column1: It does not change before endings that start with a consonant: 덥고, 덥지만, 덥습니다.
column2: 在以辅音开头的词尾前不变：덥고，덥지만，덥습니다。

column1: Some words with a ㅂ 받침 follow the regular rule: 입다 → 입어요, 잡다 → 잡아요, 좁다 → 좁아요, 씹다 → 씹어요.
column2: 有些 ㅂ 받침词按规则变化：입다 → 입어요，잡다 → 잡아요，좁다 → 좁아요，씹다 → 씹어요。

column1: This box is heavy, so let's lift it together.
column2: 这个箱子很重，我们一起抬吧。

column1: Pakistani food is spicier. But the Korean winter is too cold.
column2: 巴基斯坦菜更辣。不过韩国的冬天太冷了。

column1: Some verbs whose stem ends in a ㄷ 받침 change ㄷ to ㄹ before a vowel.
column2: 有些词干以 ㄷ 받침结尾的动词，在元音前 ㄷ 变成 ㄹ。

column1: In ㄷ irregular words, ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel.
column2: ㄷ 不规则词在元音前 ㄷ 变成 ㄹ。

column1: It does not change before endings that start with a consonant: 듣고, 듣지만, 듣습니다, 듣는.
column2: 在以辅音开头的词尾前不变：듣고，듣지만，듣습니다，듣는。

column1: ㄷ 받침 verbs that follow the regular rule: 닫다 → 닫아요, 받다 → 받아요, 믿다 → 믿어요, 얻다 → 얻어요.
column2: 按规则变化的 ㄷ 받침动词：닫다 → 닫아요，받다 → 받아요，믿다 → 믿어요，얻다 → 얻어요。

column1: If you don't know, ask the professor.
Load the boxes onto the truck.
to hang, to make (a phone call)
Sam, did you hear what I said?
column2: 山姆，你听到我说的话了吗？

column1: I'm sorry. I didn't hear it well. Please say it again.
column2: 对不起，我没听清楚。请再说一遍。

column1: Load these boxes onto that truck. And ask if there's anything you don't know.
column2: 把这些箱子装到那辆卡车上。有不知道的就问。

column1: For words whose stem ends in "르", before "-아/어" the "ㅡ" drops and one more ㄹ is added.
column2: 词干以 "르" 结尾的词，在 "-아/어" 前 "ㅡ" 脱落，并再加一个 ㄹ。

column1: If the vowel before "르" is ㅏ or ㅗ, it becomes "-ㄹ라요"; otherwise "-ㄹ러요": 모르다 → 몰라요, 빠르다 → 빨라요, 부르다 → 불러요.
column2: 르 前的元音是 ㅏ 或 ㅗ 时变成 "-ㄹ라요"，否则变成 "-ㄹ러요"：모르다 → 몰라요，빠르다 → 빨라요，부르다 → 불러요。

column1: It changes only before "-아/어": 모르고, 모르면, 모릅니다, 모르는.
Past: 몰랐어요, 빨랐어요, 불렀어요, 잘랐어요, 눌렀어요.
배가 불러요 means "I'm full", "노래를 불러요" means "I sing a song", and "이름을 불러요" means "I call (someone's) name".
column2: 배가 불러요 是 "我饱了"，"노래를 불러요" 是 "我唱歌"，"이름을 불러요" 是 "我叫(某人的)名字"。

column1: Korea and Greece have different cultures.
column2: 韩国和希腊的文化不同。

column1: Sam, do you know how to use this kiosk?
column2: 山姆，你知道这个自助点餐机怎么用吗？

column1: (-ㄹ 줄 알다 = to know how to)
column2: (-ㄹ 줄 알다 = 会，知道怎么做)

column1: No, I don't really know. It's different from the one I used before.
column2: 不，我不太清楚。和我以前用的不一样。

column1: First press this red button. If there is anything you don't know, call me.
column2: 先按这个红色按钮。有不知道的就叫我。

column1: Some words whose stem ends in a ㅅ 받침 drop the ㅅ before a vowel.
column2: 有些词干以 ㅅ 받침结尾的词，在元音前 ㅅ 脱落。

column1: In ㅅ irregular words, ㅅ drops before a vowel.
column2: ㅅ 不规则词在元音前 ㅅ 脱落。

column1: 낫다 + -아요 → 나아요, 낫다 + -(으)면 → 나으면, 낫다 + -았어요 → 나았어요. Even when ㅅ drops, the vowels are not shortened ("나아요", not "나요").
column2: 낫다 + -아요 → 나아요，낫다 + -(으)면 → 나으면，낫다 + -았어요 → 나았어요。ㅅ 脱落后元音也不缩合 (是 "나아요"，不是 "나요")。

column1: It does not change before a consonant: 낫고, 낫지만, 낫습니다.
ㅅ 받침 words that follow the regular rule: 씻다 → 씻어요, 벗다 → 벗어요, 웃다 → 웃어요.
column2: 按规则变化的 ㅅ 받침词：씻다 → 씻어요，벗다 → 벗어요，웃다 → 웃어요。

column1: Often used at the hospital: "언제 나아요?" (When will it get better?), "빨리 나으세요" (Get well soon), "부었어요" (It's swollen).
column2: 在医院常用："언제 나아요?" (什么时候能好？)，"빨리 나으세요" (祝你早日康复)，"부었어요" (肿了)。

column1: I plan to build a house in my hometown.
Pour in water and stir well.
What's bothering you? (Where does it hurt?)
I fell yesterday, and my wrist is swollen.
column2: 我昨天摔倒了，手腕肿了。

column1: The bone is fine. If you rest for about a week, it will get better.
column2: 骨头没事。休息一个星期左右就会好的。

column1: Color words and "이렇다, 그렇다, 저렇다, 어떻다" drop ㅎ and change form before a vowel.
column2: 颜色词和 "이렇다，그렇다，저렇다，어떻다" 在元音前 ㅎ 脱落，形式发生变化。

column1: In ㅎ irregular words, ㅎ drops before a vowel: 빨갛다 → 빨개요, 빨간.
column2: ㅎ 不规则词在元音前 ㅎ 脱落：빨갛다 → 빨개요，빨간。

column1: Before "-아/어", ㅎ drops and the vowel becomes "ㅐ" (빨갛다 → 빨개요, 어떻다 → 어때요). Only 하얗다 becomes "ㅒ" (하얘요). Before "-(으)", only ㅎ drops (빨갛다 → 빨간, 그렇다 → 그러면).
column2: 在 "-아/어" 前，ㅎ 脱落，元音变成 "ㅐ" (빨갛다 → 빨개요，어떻다 → 어때요)。只有 하얗다 变成 "ㅒ" (하얘요)。在 "-(으)" 前只脱落 ㅎ (빨갛다 → 빨간，그렇다 → 그러면)。

column1: It does not change before a consonant: 빨갛고, 그렇지만, 어떻게 [어떠케].
좋다, 놓다, 넣다, 많다 follow the regular rule: 좋아요, 놓아요, 넣어요.
그래요, 그러면, 그런데, 그래서, 그러니까 all come from "그렇다".
On this washing machine, when the red light comes on, you must not open the door.
column2: 这台洗衣机亮红灯的时候，不能开门。

column1: The yellow light means it will finish soon.
column2: 黄灯表示马上就结束了。

column1: The same meaning can be said with several patterns. Choose the right one for who you are talking to and where.
column2: 同样的意思可以用几种句型来表达。要根据说话对象和场合选择合适的句型。

column1: Remember patterns with the same meaning as a group, and choose the speech style that fits the listener.
column2: 把意思相同的句型放在一起记，并选择适合听话人的语体。

column1: Remember the patterns in groups by meaning: orders, prohibition, permission, obligation, reason, condition, wishes, guessing. In the table below, each row has patterns with the same or similar meaning.
column2: 按意思分组记句型：命令、禁止、允许、义务、原因、条件、愿望、推测。下表中每一行是意思相同或相近的句型。

column1: At school, the safest speech style is "-습니다/-습니까" with professors and "-아요/어요" with friends. Use casual speech (반말) only when the other person suggests it first.
column2: 在学校，对教授用 "-습니다/-습니까"，对朋友用 "-아요/어요" 最稳妥。只有对方先提出时才用非敬语 (반말)。

column1: The three biggest differences between Korean and English: ① The verb comes at the end. ② Particles come after nouns (English prepositions come before nouns). ③ The words for "will, want to, must, don't, if" all come after the verb.
column2: 韩语和中文最大的三个区别：① 动词放在句末。② 名词后面要加助词 (中文没有助词)。③ "会、想、必须、不、如果" 等意思都放在动词后面表达。

column1: Don't touch it. You must not touch it.
It's dangerous, so please be careful.
Sam, can you come early tomorrow?
column2: 山姆，你明天能早点来吗？

column1: Yes, I can come. By what time should I come?
You have to come by seven. You must not be late.
column2: 你得七点之前来。不能迟到。

column1: I understand. I will make sure not to be late.
Learn words for size and amount in pairs of opposites. Like in English, the describing word comes before the noun.
column2: 表示大小和数量的词要成对记反义词。和中文一样，修饰词放在名词前面。

column1: For size use "크다·작다"; for amount use "많다·적다".
Before a noun they become "큰, 작은, 많은, 적은, 긴, 짧은, 높은, 낮은, 넓은, 좁은": "big box" = "큰 상자".
column2: 在名词前变成 "큰，작은，많은，적은，긴，짧은，높은，낮은，넓은，좁은"："大箱子" = "큰 상자"。

column1: 작다 (small in size) and "적다" (little in amount) sound similar, but they are different words.
column2: 작다 (尺寸小) 和 "적다" (数量少) 发音相近，但是不同的词。

column1: This T-shirt is too big. Please change it for a smaller size.
column2: 这件T恤太大了。请给我换小一号的。

column1: Your voice is quiet. Please speak loudly.
column2: 你的声音太小了。请大声说。

column1: The letters are small, so I can't see them well.
I have a lot of homework today.
There are many people at the market.
There are many people at the supermarket on weekends.
I had few part-time hours this month, so my part-time pay went down.
column2: 这个月我打工时间少，所以打工的工资减少了。

column1: The line at the bank was long, so I waited for an hour.
column2: 银行排队的人很多，我等了一个小时。

column1: Lunch break is short, so I have to eat quickly.
column2: 午休时间短，所以得快点吃。

column1: The shelf is high, so I need a ladder.
The chair is a little low.
The temperature is low today, so dress warmly.
The school sports field is wide.
The new dorm rooms are spacious, so it's nice.
column2: 新宿舍的房间很宽敞，很好。

column1: The hallway is narrow, so don't run.
Sam, please bring the big box.
column2: 山姆，请把大箱子拿过来。

column1: This one? Is this one too small?
Yes, there are a lot of books, so we need a bigger one.
column2: 是的，书很多，需要更大的。

column1: Learn words for price, weight and thickness in pairs of opposites.
column2: 表示价格、重量和厚度的词要成对记反义词。

column1: For price use "비싸다·싸다", for weight "무겁다·가볍다", for thickness "두껍다·얇다".
무겁다, 가볍다, 두껍다 are ㅂ irregular: 무거워요, 가벼워요, 두꺼워요, 무거운, 가벼운, 두꺼운.
column2: 무겁다，가볍다，두껍다 是 ㅂ 不规则：무거워요，가벼워요，두꺼워요，무거운，가벼운，두꺼운。

column1: When you bargain, say "너무 비싸요. 좀 싸게 해 주세요" (It's too expensive. Please give me a discount).
column2: 讲价时说 "너무 비싸요. 좀 싸게 해 주세요" (太贵了。请便宜一点)。

column1: 싸다 means "cheap" and is used only for prices. For "right, correct" Korean uses "맞다".
column2: 싸다 的意思是 "便宜"，只用于价格。"对，正确" 在韩语里用 "맞다"。

column1: Taxis are expensive. Take the bus.
column2: 出租车很贵。坐公交车吧。

column1: Exchanging money at the airport is expensive.
These clothes are cheap and good.
If you go late in the evening, side dishes at the supermarket are cheap.
column2: 晚上很晚去的话，超市的小菜很便宜。

column1: My bag is heavy, so it's hard.
If it's heavy, lift it together, two people.
This box is light, so I can lift it alone.
column2: 这个箱子很轻，我一个人能抬。

column1: Stack the light boxes on top.
In winter we wear thick clothes.
In winter you need a thick blanket.
If you wear thin clothes, you will be cold.
It's 120,000 won. It's thick and light.
It's a bit expensive. Do you have a cheaper one?
column2: 有点贵。有便宜一点的吗？

column1: This one is 80,000 won, but it's a little thin.
English uses "hot" and "cold" for both weather and things, but Korean uses different words for weather and for things.
column2: 中文的 "热" 和 "冷" 天气和东西都能用，但韩语里天气和东西用不同的词 (就像中文的 "冷" 和 "凉" 也有区别)。

column1: For weather use "덥다·춥다"; for things use "뜨겁다·차갑다".
English "hot" is two words in Korean. For weather use "덥다"; for things you touch and feel use "뜨겁다". Don't say "날씨가 뜨거워요".
column2: 中文的 "热" 在韩语里是两个词。天气用 "덥다"；摸到、感觉到的东西用 "뜨겁다"。不要说 "날씨가 뜨거워요"。

column1: Koreans eat hot soup and say "시원하다". It means their stomach feels good and they feel refreshed.
column2: 韩国人喝着热汤说 "시원하다"。意思是肚子舒服、感觉很爽快。

column1: Four of the six words are ㅂ irregular: 더워요, 추워요, 뜨거워요, 차가워요.
column2: 这六个词中有四个是 ㅂ 不规则：더워요，추워요，뜨거워요，차가워요。

column1: If it's hot, rest in the shade during your break.
column2: 热的话，休息时间去阴凉处休息。

column1: It's cold, so wear a lot of clothes.
Even if it's cold, don't turn the boiler up too high.
column2: 就算冷，也不要把锅炉开得太高。

column1: A bowl taken out of the microwave is hot.
column2: 从微波炉里拿出来的碗很烫。

column1: If you drink too much cold water, you'll get a stomachache.
If you catch a cold, drink warm water often.
A glass of cool water, please.
After class, let's have a cool drink.
It's really cold today, isn't it?
Yes, my hands are so cold.
Do you want to drink some warm coffee?
Sounds good. It's hot, so I'll drink it slowly.
Learn words for good and bad in pairs of opposites.
column2: 表示好与坏的词要成对记反义词。

column1: English often makes opposites with "not" or "un-" (not good, unhappy), but Korean often has a separate word (나쁘다). "안 좋아요" can also be used, and it sounds softer.
column2: 中文常用 "不" 构成反义 (不好、不开心)，韩语则常有单独的词 (나쁘다)。也可以用 "안 좋아요"，听起来更委婉。

column1: Pairs with "있다 ↔ 없다": 재미있다·재미없다, 맛있다·맛없다. Words that become opposite with "불-": 편하다·불편하다, 가능하다·불가능하다.
column2: 있다 ↔ 없다 构成的对：재미있다·재미없다，맛있다·맛없다。加 "불-" 变成反义的词：편하다·불편하다，가능하다·불가능하다。

column1: This department has a good atmosphere.
This app is good because the transfer fee is cheap.
column2: 这个应用转账手续费便宜，很好用。

column1: Smoking is bad for your health.
I'm in a bad mood today.
On days with bad fine dust, wear a mask.
column2: 雾霾严重的日子要戴口罩。

column1: It was hard at first, but now it's easy.
column2: 一开始很难，现在很简单了。

column1: If the documents are difficult, take them to the center.
column2: 资料看不懂的话，就拿到中心去。
在韩国的生活很有意思。

column1: Studying with Korean dramas is fun.
Only studying is boring, so let's go out on the weekend.
column2: 光学习太无聊了，周末出去玩吧。

column1: If you live near the school, getting to school is easy.
column2: 住在学校附近的话，上学很方便。

column1: We don't understand each other's language, so it's hard.
to get through, to understand each other
If anything is inconvenient, please tell me.
column2: 有什么不方便的地方请告诉我。

column1: How is your new part-time job? Is it hard?
No, it's easy. But the uniform is a bit uncomfortable.
column2: 不累，很轻松。不过制服有点不舒服。

column1: Are the people you work with nice?
Yes, they are all nice and fun.
column2: 嗯，大家都很好，很有意思。

column1: Learn words for the condition of things and people in pairs of opposites.
column2: 表示事物和人的状态的词要成对记反义词。

column1: 빠르다 is 르 irregular (빨라요), "바쁘다" drops ㅡ (바빠요), and "더럽다, 시끄럽다" are ㅂ irregular (더러워요, 시끄러워요).
column2: 빠르다 是 르 不规则 (빨라요)，"바쁘다" 是 ㅡ 脱落 (바빠요)，"더럽다，시끄럽다" 是 ㅂ 不规则 (더러워요，시끄러워요)。

column1: To describe a verb: 빨리 (quickly), 천천히 (slowly), 깨끗이 (cleanly), 조용히 (quietly): "조용히 하세요."
column2: 修饰动词时用：빨리 (快)，천천히 (慢慢地)，깨끗이 (干净地)，조용히 (安静地)："조용히 하세요."

column1: In restaurant work, your hands must be clean.
column2: 在餐厅工作，手必须干净。

column1: The floor is dirty. Please clean it.
Put dirty clothes in the laundry basket.
column2: 把脏衣服放进洗衣篮里。

column1: Sam works fast with his hands.
If you're in a hurry, a taxi is faster.
I'm busy these days because of exams.
I was busy, so I couldn't eat.
At the end of the semester there are many assignments, so I'm busy.
column2: 学期末作业很多，所以很忙。

column1: When I'm free, I study Korean.
Please be quiet in the library.

column2: 晚上10点以后请保持安静。

column1: The noise from the next room is loud.
It was noisy outside, so I couldn't sleep.
It's hard to study in a noisy place.
column2: 在吵闹的地方很难学习。

column1: Sam, the table is a bit dirty. Please wipe it clean.
column2: 山姆，桌子有点脏。请擦干净。

column1: Okay. I'm busy now. Can I do it a little later?
column2: 好的。我现在很忙。可以晚一点做吗？

column1: Yes, do it when you're free.
Learn words for states you check and talk about at school and in the dorm, in pairs of opposites.
column2: 在学校和宿舍里要确认、谈论的状态词，成对记反义词。

column1: Use "다르다" (different) and "틀리다" (wrong) correctly. Koreans also often mix them up, but the meanings are different.
column2: 要正确使用 "다르다" (不同) 和 "틀리다" (错)。韩国人也常常混用，但意思不同。

column1: When checking, ask "맞아요?" (Is it right?) or "이거하고 같아요?" (Is it the same as this?). When you compare answers with a friend, say "제 답은 달라요" (My answer is different).
column2: 确认时问 "맞아요?" (对吗？) 或 "이거하고 같아요?" (和这个一样吗？)。和朋友对答案时说 "제 답은 달라요" (我的答案不一样)。

column1: Korea is safe even at night.
At night it's safer to take the main road.
Looking at your phone while riding a bike is dangerous.
column2: 骑自行车时看手机很危险。

column1: Motorbikes are dangerous on rainy days.
column2: 下雨天骑摩托车很危险。

column1: Does this bus go to Jeonju University?
column2: 这辆公交车去全州大学吗？

column1: If the account number is wrong, the money won't go through.
column2: 账号错了的话，钱就转不过去。

column1: The two are the same size.
Korea and Myanmar have different cultures.
column2: 韩国和缅甸的文化不同。

column1: In Korea, the garbage day is different in each neighborhood.
column2: 在韩国，每个小区扔垃圾的日子都不一样。

column1: The fridge is full of food.
If the trash can is full, please empty it.
column2: 垃圾桶满了的话，请倒掉。

column1: Collect empty bottles separately and throw them away.
column2: 空瓶子要另外收集起来扔掉。

column1: Sam, is this answer the same as mine?
column2: 山姆，这个答案和我的一样吗？

column1: The first part is the same, but the end is a little different.
column2: 前面一样，最后有点不一样。

column1: That's right. My answer was wrong. I'll solve it again.
column2: 对了。我的答案错了。我再做一遍。

column1: Learn verbs of movement in pairs of opposites.
column2: 移动动词要成对记反义词。

column1: It is made like English "go in, come out, go up": 들다 (in) + 가다 (go) = 들어가다. So there are also "들어오다, 나가다, 올라오다, 내려오다".
column2: 构词方式和中文的 "进去、出来、上去" 很像：들다 (进) + 가다 (去) = 들어가다。所以也有 "들어오다，나가다，올라오다，내려오다"。

column1: Choose "가다" or "오다" from where the speaker is. On the phone say "지금 갈게요" (I'm coming now), not "올게요". In English you say "coming", but in Korean you "go" to the other person.
column2: 根据说话人所在的位置选择 "가다" 或 "오다"。在电话里说 "지금 갈게요" (我现在过去)，不说 "올게요"。和中文一样，是往对方那里 "去"。

column1: I go to the market on the weekend.
If you are sick, don't put up with it. Go to the hospital.
column2: 不舒服的话别忍着。去医院吧。

column1: A friend is coming to my house.
If a package comes, please leave it at the security office.
column2: 有快递来的话，请放在保安室。

column1: Please go into the department office.
Take off your shoes and go into the room.
Knock when you go into a room.
I came out of the lecture room.
Go up the stairs, and the department office is right there.
column2: 上楼梯，系办公室就在那里。

column1: Please go down to the basement.
If there is a fire, go down the stairs.
column2: 发生火灾的话，走楼梯下去。

column1: I take the school shuttle bus at 7:30.
Please call me before you leave.
Please text me when you arrive.
Where do I get off to go to City Hall?
column2: 去市政府要在哪里下车？

column1: Take bus number 10 and get off at the third stop.
column2: 坐10路公交车，在第三站下车。

column1: About how many minutes does it take?
If you leave now, you'll arrive in 20 minutes.
column2: 现在出发的话，20分钟就到了。

column1: Learn verbs of giving and receiving in pairs.
column2: 给予和接受的动词要成对记。

column1: For the receiver use "한테/에게"; for the giver (from) use "한테서/에게서": "친구한테 줬어요", "친구한테서 받았어요".
column2: 接受的人用 "한테/에게"；给的人 (从…) 用 "한테서/에게서"："친구한테 줬어요"，"친구한테서 받았어요"。

column1: When you give something to an older or higher person, use "드리다". "교수님께 드렸어요."
column2: 给年长或地位高的人东西时用 "드리다"。"교수님께 드렸어요."

column1: 빌리다 is to borrow, "빌려주다" is to lend: "돈을 빌렸어요" (I borrowed money), "돈을 빌려줬어요" (I lent money).
column2: 빌리다 是借 (入)，"빌려주다" 是借 (出)："돈을 빌렸어요" (我借了钱)，"돈을 빌려줬어요" (我把钱借给别人了)。

column1: I gave my friend a present.
My roommate gave me rice cakes on Seollal.
column2: 春节时室友给了我年糕。

column1: I got a letter from a friend.
When you get the package, please take a photo and send it.
column2: 收到快递后请拍照发给我。

column1: I bought fruit at the market.
I bought a used bicycle cheaply.
column2: 我便宜买了一辆二手自行车。

column1: Before going back to my country, I sold the things I used.
column2: 回国前，我把用过的东西卖了。

column1: I borrowed money from a friend.
I borrowed a Korean book from the library.
column2: 我从图书馆借了一本韩语书。

column1: I returned the book I borrowed.
Return the laptop you borrowed by today.
column2: 借的笔记本电脑今天之内还回来。

column1: I ask my senior about words I don't know.
When your name is called, answer "네".
Aisha, can you lend me a charger?
column2: 爱莎，能借我一下充电器吗？

column1: Sure, here. It's the one I got from a senior.
column2: 当然，给你。这是前辈给我的。

column1: Thanks. I'll use it and give it back right away.
Like English "open, close" and "turn on, turn off", Korean uses different words for doors and for machines.
column2: 中文的 "开、关" 门和机器都能用，但韩语中门和机器用不同的词。

column1: For doors use "열다·닫다"; for electricity use "켜다·끄다".
불을 열어요 (open the light) is wrong. For things that use electricity, use "켜다, 끄다" (turn on, turn off).
column2: 불을 열어요 是错的。用电的东西要用 "켜다，끄다" (开，关)。

column1: Opening and closing hours of shops and banks also use "열다, 닫다". "은행은 네 시에 문을 닫아요."
column2: 商店和银行的营业、关门时间也用 "열다，닫다"。"은행은 네 시에 문을 닫아요."

column1: 끄다 becomes 꺼요, "잠그다" becomes 잠가요 (ㅡ drops), and "열다, 풀다" become 여세요, 푸세요 (ㄹ drops).
column2: 끄다 变成 꺼요，"잠그다" 变成 잠가요 (ㅡ 脱落)，"열다，풀다" 变成 여세요，푸세요 (ㄹ 脱落)。

column1: The post office closes at six, so go quickly.
If it's hot, turn on the fan.
During class, turn off your phone's sound.
column2: 上课时把手机调成静音。

column1: Don't put too much detergent in the washing machine.
column2: 不要往洗衣机里放太多洗衣液。

column1: I took my passport out of my bag.
I took water out of the fridge.
Take your alien registration card out of your wallet.
column2: 从钱包里拿出外国人登录证。

column1: to lock, to shut off (a valve)
Be sure to lock the door.
Lock your room door when you go out.
to undo, to unlock, to solve
I forgot my password, so I can't unlock it.
to raise, to put up, to post
I posted a photo in the group chat.
I posted my vacation photos in the group chat.
column2: 我在群聊里发了假期的照片。

column1: Please turn the sound down a little.
Don't set the air conditioner temperature too low.
column2: 空调温度不要调得太低。

column1: What do you need to check before leaving the lecture room?
column2: 离开讲堂前要检查什么？

column1: Turn off the computer, turn off the lights and close the windows.
Put the remote control in the box and lock the door.
column2: 把遥控器放进盒子里，然后锁门。

column1: Learn verbs often used when you move house or put things in order, in pairs of opposites.
column2: 搬家或整理东西时常用的动词，成对记反义词。

column1: 풀다 is used for things that are tied, tightened or locked. In English it is "untie, loosen, unlock".
column2: 풀다 用于绑着的、拧紧的或锁着的东西，相当于中文的 "解开、松开、打开(锁)"。

column1: 싣다 is ㄷ irregular: 실어요, 실으세요, 실었어요.
column2: 싣다 是 ㄷ 不规则：실어요，실으세요，실었어요。

column1: 내리다 has many meanings: 차에서 내리다 (get off a car), 짐을 내리다 (unload), 온도를 내리다 (lower), 비가 내리다 (rain falls).
column2: 내리다 有很多意思：차에서 내리다 (下车)，짐을 내리다 (卸货)，온도를 내리다 (降低)，비가 내리다 (下雨)。

column1: I loaded the moving boxes into the car.
column2: 我把搬家的箱子装上了车。

column1: All the moving things can go in a small truck.
column2: 搬家的东西一辆小卡车就能装下。

column1: Unload the things from the truck.
column2: 把东西从卡车上卸下来。

column1: Be careful when you take your bags off the bus.
column2: 从公交车上拿包下来时要小心。

column1: Tie it tightly with a string.
Tie back long hair when you exercise.
column2: 运动时把长头发扎起来。

column1: The knot is tied too tight, so I can't untie it.
I tightened the bolts on my bicycle wheel.
column2: 我拧紧了自行车轮子上的螺栓。

column1: Put a sticker on the box.
I put a poster on the wall.
Put your name on your food in the fridge.
column2: 在冰箱里的食物上写上名字。

column1: to take off, to peel off
Please take off the price tag.
It's a present, so please take off the price tag.
column2: 这是礼物，请把价格标签撕掉。

column1: The professor starts class at nine.
I start studying Korean next week.
I eat breakfast and then start studying.
I have to finish this assignment by Friday.
column2: 这个作业我得在星期五之前完成。

column1: Sam, tie these boxes and load them into the car.
column2: 山姆，把这些箱子捆好装上车。

column1: Okay. Should I put stickers on them too?
Yes, take off the old stickers and put on new ones.
column2: 对，把旧贴纸撕掉，贴上新的。
明白了。我三点之前做完。

column1: Learn everyday actions in pairs of opposites.
column2: 日常动作要成对记反义词。

column1: English "wear / put on" is different verbs in Korean, depending on the body part. Clothes: "입다", shoes and socks: "신다", hats and glasses: "쓰다", gloves and rings: "끼다". To take any of them off, use "벗다".
column2: 中文的 "穿/戴" 在韩语里根据身体部位用不同的动词。衣服用 "입다"，鞋袜用 "신다"，帽子眼镜用 "쓰다"，手套戒指用 "끼다"。脱下来都用 "벗다"。

column1: In Korean homes, some restaurants and dorms, you take off your shoes before going in.
column2: 在韩国家庭、部分餐厅和宿舍，进去前要脱鞋。

column1: 잊어버리다 (to forget) and "잃어버리다" (to lose) sound similar: "약속을 잊어버렸어요", "지갑을 잃어버렸어요".
column2: 잊어버리다 (忘记) 和 "잃어버리다" (丢失) 发音相近："약속을 잊어버렸어요"，"지갑을 잃어버렸어요"。

column1: If it's cold, wear a coat.
It will be below zero tomorrow, so wear thermal underwear.
column2: 明天零下，穿上保暖内衣。

column1: Take off your shoes and come in.
In Korean homes, people take off their shoes.
column2: 在韩国家里，人们要脱鞋。

column1: Sit on the chair and wait.
On the bus, don't sit in the seats for the elderly and the weak.
column2: 在公交车上，不要坐老弱病残专座。

column1: I stood the whole time on the bus.
column2: 在公交车上我一直站着。

column1: On the escalator, stand on the right.
I go to bed at eleven.
During exam period, I go to bed late at night.
column2: 考试期间我晚上很晚才睡。

column1: Please get up from the chair.
I have to set two alarms to wake up.
column2: 我得定两个闹钟才能起床。

column1: Smile when we take a photo.
I cried after watching the movie.
I cried during a video call with my family.
column2: 和家人视频通话时我哭了。

column1: Be sure to remember the dorm address.
I left my umbrella on the bus.
column2: 我把伞落在公交车上了。

column1: I left my alien registration card in my room.
column2: 我把外国人登录证落在房间里了。

column1: Sam, you must wear indoor shoes when you go into the practice room.
column2: 山姆，进实习室时一定要穿室内鞋。

column1: Put on your uniform and your cap too. Be sure to remember.
column2: 穿上制服，也戴上帽子。一定要记住。

column1: Words for position come in the opposite order to English. Korean says "noun + position word".
column2: 表示位置的词和中文的顺序一样，韩语也说 "名词 + 方位词" (就像 "桌子上")。
韩语用 "名词 + 앞/뒤/위/아래/안/밖" 的顺序。

column1: Korean has three pointing words: 여기 (near the speaker), 거기 (near the listener), 저기 (far from both). 이것·그것·저것 work the same way.
column2: 韩语有三个指示词：여기 (离说话人近)，거기 (离听话人近)，저기 (离两人都远)。이것·그것·저것 也一样。
还要记住 "옆" (旁边)，"사이" (之间)，"가운데" (中间)，"맞은편" (对面)，"근처" (附近)。

column1: 밑 is also used with the same meaning as "아래": "책상 밑".
column2: 밑 和 "아래" 意思相同："책상 밑"。

column1: There is a convenience store in front of my house.
column2: 我家前面有一家便利店。

column1: I take the shuttle bus in front of the convenience store.
column2: 我在便利店前面坐校车。

column1: The key is on top of the fridge.
The bag is under the chair.
The fire extinguisher is under the stairs.
The wallet is in the bag.

In Korea cars drive on the right, so look left first.
column2: 在韩国车辆靠右行驶，所以先看左边。

When you come out of the bank and go right, there is a pharmacy.
column2: 从银行出来往右走，有一家药店。

The building you can see over there is the library.
column2: 那边看到的建筑是图书馆。

column1: The blue building you can see over there is the Star Center.
column2: 那边看到的蓝色建筑是 Star Center。

column1: Excuse me. Where is the library?
column2: 打扰一下。图书馆在哪里？

column2: 在这栋楼后面。在停车场右边。

column1: In the library, on the desk next to the door.

column1: Learn words for time in pairs.
column2: 表示时间的词要成对记。

column1: 아침, 점심, 저녁 are both times and meal names: "아침을 먹었어요" = I ate breakfast.
column2: 아침，점심，저녁 既是时间也是饭的名字："아침을 먹었어요" = 我吃了早饭。

column1: Learn the days in order: 그저께 (the day before yesterday), 어제, 오늘, 내일, 모레 (the day after tomorrow).
column2: 按顺序记日子：그저께 (前天)，어제，오늘，내일，모레 (后天)。

column1: Put "오전, 오후" before the time so it is not confusing: "오후 세 시" (3 p.m.).
column2: 把 "오전，오후" 放在时间前面，就不会混淆了："오후 세 시" (下午3点)。

column1: I went to the hospital yesterday.
The money I sent yesterday hasn't arrived yet.
Taking classes without breakfast is hard.
column2: 不吃早饭就上课很辛苦。

column1: I'll call you in the evening.
In the evening I have a video call with my family in Nepal.
column2: 晚上我和在尼泊尔的家人视频通话。

column1: I take classes during the day and work part-time at night.
On summer days, it's hard to exercise outside.
column2: 夏天白天很难在外面运动。

column1: Don't go out alone at night.
I go to the hospital in the morning.
If you go to the bank in the morning, there are few people.
column2: 上午去银行的话人很少。

column1: There is a group meeting at 2 p.m.
It will rain in the afternoon.
I have a hospital appointment in the afternoon, so I can't go to class.
column2: 我下午有医院预约，所以不能去上课。

column1: Go to the airport two hours before your flight leaves.
column2: 飞机起飞前两个小时去机场。

column1: Please come back in an hour.
Sam, do you have more morning classes or afternoon classes this semester?
column2: 山姆，这学期上午的课多还是下午的课多？

column1: More afternoon classes. And I work part-time from 6 to 10 p.m.
column2: 下午的课多。而且我晚上6点到10点打工。

column1: Then get a good sleep in the morning.
Learn words for order and speed in pairs. In Korean, these words come before the verb.
column2: 表示顺序和速度的词要成对记。在韩语里，这些词放在动词前面。

column1: 먼저·나중에, 처음·마지막, 일찍·늦게, 빨리·천천히 come before the verb.
In English these words come after the verb (go first, speak slowly), but in Korean they come before the verb (먼저 가요, 천천히 말해요).
column2: 和中文一样，这些词放在动词前面 (先走，慢慢说)：먼저 가요，천천히 말해요。

column1: One of the words you hear most in Korea is "빨리빨리" (quickly, quickly). Still, go slowly and carefully on the street.
column2: 在韩国最常听到的词之一是 "빨리빨리" (快点快点)。不过在路上还是要慢慢地、小心地走。

column1: Wash your hands first and then come.
If you are sick, tell the professor first.
column2: 不舒服的话，先告诉教授。

column1: I'm busy now, so I'll call you later.
column2: 我现在忙，等会儿给你打电话。

column1: If it's your first visit, take a number ticket.
The last bus is at eleven.
The last person, please turn off the lights and leave.
column2: 最后一个人请关灯离开。

column1: It's your first day, so come 10 minutes early.
column2: 今天是你第一天，早来10分钟。

column1: I went to bed late yesterday.
If you'll be late, let us know in advance.
column2: 要迟到的话，请提前告诉我们。

column1: If there is a fire, go outside quickly.
column2: 发生火灾的话，赶快到外面去。

column1: Okay. Can you come a little early tomorrow?
Thanks. Take care on your way.
Korean adds a counting word when counting things, like English "a sheet of" or "a pair of". The counting word changes with the shape and type of the thing.
column2: 韩语数东西时要加量词，和中文的 "一张纸、一双鞋" 一样。量词根据东西的形状和种类而变化。

column1: Most things use "개", paper "장", books "권", computers and cars "대", clothes "벌", shoes "켤레".
column2: 大多数东西用 "개"，纸用 "장"，书用 "권"，电脑和车用 "대"，衣服用 "벌"，鞋用 "켤레"。

column1: The order is different from English: "noun + number + counter". 3 apples = 사과 세 개.
column2: 顺序和中文不同："名词 + 数字 + 量词"。3个苹果 = 사과 세 개。

column1: For numbers use "하나, 둘, 셋"; before a counter they change to "한, 두, 세, 네". 스물 becomes "스무" (스무 개).
column2: 数字用 "하나，둘，셋"；在量词前变成 "한，두，세，네"。스물 变成 "스무" (스무 개)。

column1: If you don't know which counter to use, use "개". It works in most cases.
column2: 不知道用哪个量词的话就用 "개"。大多数情况下都可以。

column1: Five packs of ramyeon are 4,000 won.
There are ten cars in the parking lot.
I bought a set of clothes.
I need a suit to wear for interviews.
column2: 我需要一套面试穿的西装。

column1: Three pairs of socks are 5,000 won.
I bought a pair of sneakers.
Sam, bring 20 boxes and 100 sheets of paper from the department office.
column2: 山姆，从系办公室拿20个箱子和100张纸来。

column1: Okay. How many rolls of tape do you need?
Three. And bring two books too.
Korean also adds counting words for people and animals. The order is different from English, and the way of saying numbers is different too.
column2: 韩语数人和动物时也要加量词。顺序和中文不同，数字的说法也不同。

column1: People use "명", "분" when polite, animals "마리", and numbers are "한, 두, 세, 네".
column2: 人用 "명"，尊敬时用 "분"，动物用 "마리"，数字用 "한，두，세，네"。

column1: The order is different from English: "noun + number + counter".
column2: 顺序和中文不同："名词 + 数字 + 量词"。

column1: Count with "하나, 둘, 셋", not "일, 이, 삼", and the form changes before a counter: 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네.
column2: 用 "하나，둘，셋" 来数，不用 "일，이，삼"，在量词前形式会变：하나 → 한，둘 → 두，셋 → 세，넷 → 네。

column1: Three people share our dorm room.
column2: 我们宿舍房间住三个人。

column1: How many people are in your party?
Five guests are coming to our department today.
column2: 今天有五位客人来我们系。

column1: Come in one at a time.
Two people have to do this assignment together.
column2: 这个作业要两个人一起做。

column1: There are fifty monkeys at the zoo.
column2: 动物园里有五十只猴子。

column1: Four. One more will come a little later.
column2: 四位。等一会儿还有一位来。

column1: Then five in total. Please come this way.
Is a whole chicken in samgyetang?
column2: 参鸡汤里放的是一整只鸡吗？

column1: Yes, a whole chicken goes in.

column2: 名词 + 数字 + 量词 (학생 세 명 = 3个学生)

column1: Food and drinks are counted by the container they are in, like English "a glass of, a cup of, a bowl of, a plate of".
column2: 食物和饮料按盛放的容器来数，就像中文的 "一杯、一碗、一盘"。

column1: Things in bottles are counted with "병", in cups "잔", rice and soup "그릇", and meat "인분".
column2: 瓶装的用 "병"，杯装的用 "잔"，饭和汤用 "그릇"，肉用 "인분"。

column1: Only "인분" is counted with "일, 이, 삼": 일 인분, 이 인분, 삼 인분. Others use "한, 두, 세".
column2: 只有 "인분" 用 "일，이，삼" 来数：일 인분，이 인분，삼 인분。其他的用 "한，두，세"。

column1: 한잔하다 means to go for a drink (alcohol): "오늘 한잔할까요?" (Shall we have a drink today?)
column2: 한잔하다 的意思是去喝一杯 (酒)："오늘 한잔할까요?" (今天去喝一杯吗？)

column1: At Korean BBQ restaurants, you usually have to order at least two servings.
column2: 在韩式烤肉店，一般至少要点两人份。

column1: Two more bottles of beer, please.
I'll drink just one bottle of soju and go home.
column2: 我只喝一瓶烧酒就回家。

column1: Would you like a cup of coffee?
Just a glass of water, please.
I drink only two cups of coffee a day.
Please add one more bowl of rice.
There are four of us, so let's order four servings of meat.
column2: 我们有四个人，点四人份的肉吧。

column1: One more plate of kimchi, please.
How much is a plate of dumplings?
Please wrap up a plate of dumplings to go.
I ate two slices of pizza.
Two servings of bulgogi and two bowls of rice, please.
column2: 请给我两人份烤牛肉和两碗米饭。

column1: One bottle of cola and two glasses of water, please.
column2: 请给我一瓶可乐和两杯水。

column1: These are words for counting things by package, not one by one. They are used in supermarkets, convenience stores and shops.
column2: 这些是按包装而不是一个一个数东西时用的词。在超市、便利店和商店里使用。

column1: Packages are counted with "상자, 봉지, 묶음, 통", and "씩" means "each, per".
column2: 包装用 "상자，봉지，묶음，통" 来数，"씩" 的意思是 "每，各"。

column1: 씩 means "each, per": "열 개씩" (ten at a time), "한 사람씩" (one person at a time). You often hear it in class too: "두 명씩 앉으세요." (Sit in twos.)
column2: 씩 的意思是 "每，各"："열 개씩" (每次十个)，"한 사람씩" (一个人一个人地)。课堂上也常听到："두 명씩 앉으세요." (两个人一组坐。)

column1: A tray of eggs is 30 eggs.
Pattern for dividing things: "(number) 개씩 한 (봉지/상자)에 넣으세요."
column2: 分装东西的句型："(数字) 개씩 한 (봉지/상자)에 넣으세요."

column1: I bought a box of ramyeon.
When I moved, I packed five boxes of things.
column2: 搬家时我打包了五箱东西。

I ate a roll of gimbap for lunch.
column2: 我午饭吃了一条紫菜包饭。

column1: I ordered a tray of tofu.
A tray of eggs lasts me a week.
column2: 一板鸡蛋我能吃一个星期。

column1: I bought two tubs of ice cream.
I got a tub of kimchi.
Please bring one more container of water.
Put five of these snacks in each bag.
Okay. How many bags do we need to make in total?
Fifty bags. Put ten bags in each box.
These are units for length, weight and volume, and words for counting times and order. Korea uses the international (metric) units used in most countries.
column2: 这些是长度、重量和容量的单位，以及表示次数和顺序的词。韩国使用大多数国家通用的国际单位 (公制)。

column1: Measuring units are read with "일, 이, 삼"; "번" for times is read with "한, 두, 세".
column2: 计量单位用 "일，이，삼" 来读；表示次数的 "번" 用 "한，두，세" 来读。

column1: Measuring units (미터, 킬로그램, 리터) are read with "일, 이, 삼", and "번" for times is read with "한, 두, 세".
column2: 计量单位 (미터，킬로그램，리터) 用 "일，이，삼" 来读，表示次数的 "번" 用 "한，두，세" 来读。

column1: 번 has two uses: "세 번" (three times) and "삼 번" (number 3): "삼 번 버스를 세 번 탔어요." (I took bus number 3 three times.)
column2: 번 有两种用法："세 번" (三次) 和 "삼 번" (3号)："삼 번 버스를 세 번 탔어요." (我坐了三次3路公交车。)

column1: It's 300 meters from the dorm to the library.
Set the space between them to 5 centimeters.
Checked bags on the plane can be up to 23 kilograms.
column2: 飞机托运行李最多23公斤。

column1: Drink 2 liters of water a day.

column2: 右边第二个房间是我的房间。

column1: The department office is on the 3rd floor.
How many floors does this building have?

column2: 把这张纸裁成30厘米一段。

column1: Okay. How many do you need?

column2: 二十张。每张长度检查两遍。

column1: Before a counter, the form of the number changes. English doesn't have this rule, so you need to practice it.
column2: 在量词前，数字的形式会变化。就像中文 "二" 在量词前要说 "两" 一样，需要多练习。

column1: Before a counter, 하나·둘·셋·넷·스물 become 한·두·세·네·스무.
column2: 在量词前，하나·둘·셋·넷·스물 变成 한·두·세·네·스무。

column1: Only five numbers change: 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷, 스물. The last part also changes, like 열하나 → 열한 개, 스물둘 → 스물두 명.
column2: 只有五个数字会变：하나，둘，셋，넷，스물。末尾部分也会变，如 열하나 → 열한 개，스물둘 → 스물두 명。

column1: When you say only the number without a counter, use "하나, 둘": "몇 개 드릴까요?" "하나 주세요."
column2: 不加量词只说数字时用 "하나，둘"："몇 개 드릴까요?" "하나 주세요."

column1: From 100, people usually use the "일, 이, 삼" numbers: "백 개, 이백 명".
column2: 从100开始，一般用 "일，이，삼" 数字："백 개，이백 명"。

column1: Do you deliver even if I buy just one?

column2: 两个人一起抬就很轻松。

Please load four bottles of water into the car.

I first came to Korea when I was 20.
column2: 我第一次来韩国是20岁的时候。

to be in, to be contained

Korean has two sets of numbers. To tell the time, "시" (hour) is read with "한, 두, 세" and "분" (minute) with "일, 이, 삼".
column2: 韩语有两套数字。说时间时，"시" (点) 用 "한，두，세" 来读，"분" (分) 用 "일，이，삼" 来读。

column1: 시 is read with 한·두·세, and "분" with 일·이·삼.
column2: 시 用 한·두·세 来读，"분" 用 일·이·삼 来读。

column1: You mix the two number sets in one phrase, like "세 시 삼 분". Saying "삼 시" or "세 분" is wrong.
column2: 一个短语里要混用两套数字，如 "세 시 삼 분"。说 "삼 시" 或 "세 분" 是错的。

column1: 시 (o'clock, a point in time) and "시간" (hours, length of time) are different: "세 시에 만나요", "세 시간 공부했어요".
column2: 시 (点，时间点) 和 "시간" (小时，时长) 不同："세 시에 만나요"，"세 시간 공부했어요"。

column1: I have lunch at half past twelve.

column2: 12:30之前去食堂的话，排队的人少。

column2: 休息时间两点五十结束。

column1: There is a group meeting at 8 a.m.
At three o'clock. There are 20 minutes left.
Age is said with "살" or "세", and dates are read with "일, 이, 삼".
column2: 年龄用 "살" 或 "세" 来说，日期用 "일，이，삼" 来读。

column1: Age is "스무 살" or "이십 세", and dates go "year → month → day".
column2: 年龄说 "스무 살" 或 "이십 세"，日期按 "年 → 月 → 日" 的顺序。

column1: Dates go in the order "year → month → day", which is different from English (13 November 2026 / November 13, 2026): 2026년 11월 13일.
column2: 日期按 "年 → 月 → 日" 的顺序，和中文一样 (2026年11月13日)：2026년 11월 13일。

column1: Month names add "월" to the number. Only two months change sound: June is "유월" and October is "시월".
column2: 月份是在数字后加 "월"。只有两个月的发音会变：六月是 "유월"，十月是 "시월"。

column1: To ask an older person's age, say "연세가 어떻게 되세요?". Koreans often ask your age to decide how politely to speak.
column2: 问长辈的年龄时说 "연세가 어떻게 되세요?"。韩国人常常问年龄来决定说话的礼貌程度。

column1: How old is your younger sibling?

column2: 在韩国，初次见面时人们常常问年龄。
