column2: 我过生日时室友送了我蛋糕。

column1: What is your date of birth?
column2: 您的出生日期是什么时候？

column1: Money and phone numbers are read with "일, 이, 삼". Unlike English, big numbers are split into units of "만" (ten thousand).
column2: 钱和电话号码用 "일，이，삼" 来读。和中文一样，大数字以 "만" (万) 为单位划分。

column1: Money is read in units of "만", and 0 in phone numbers is "공".
column2: 钱以 "만" 为单位来读，电话号码里的0读作 "공"。

column1: Korean splits numbers every four digits (만, 억). English has "hundred thousand, million", and Korean says "십만, 백만": 백만 = one million, 십만 = one hundred thousand.
column2: 韩语每四位数划分一次 (만，억)，和中文的 "万、亿" 完全一样：백만 = 一百万，십만 = 十万。

column1: 10,000 is not "일만", just "만". 1,000 is "천" and 100 is "백".

column2: 我每个月的零花钱是300美元。

column1: I received 2,000,000 won as a scholarship.

column2: 韩国的手机号码以010开头。

column2: 我想往孟加拉国汇1,000,000韩元。

column1: The fee is 5,000 won. Please write the receiver's phone number.
column2: 手续费5,000韩元。请写上收款人的电话号码。

column1: Even the same number is read differently when counting things and when saying a number (name).
column2: 同一个数字，数东西和说号码 (名称) 时读法不同。

column1: For how many, use "한, 두, 세"; for numbers, use "일, 이, 삼".
column2: 表示多少个用 "한，두，세"；表示号码用 "일，이，삼"。

column1: To say how many, use "한, 두, 세"; for numbers used like names, use "일, 이, 삼".
column2: 说多少个时用 "한，두，세"；像名字一样使用的号码用 "일，이，삼"。

column1: Words used with numbers: 번 (bus, turn), 호 (room, subway line), 층 (floor), 동 (apartment or dorm building), 번지 (address), 반 (class group).
column2: 和数字一起用的词：번 (路，次序)，호 (房间号，地铁线)，층 (楼层)，동 (公寓或宿舍楼栋)，번지 (门牌号)，반 (班)。

column1: Korean buildings have basement floors. "지하 일 층" is B1.
column2: 韩国的建筑有地下楼层。"지하 일 층" 是B1。

column1: I shared three apples with my roommates.
column2: 我和室友们分了三个苹果。

column1: Bus number 3 stops in front of the school.
Go down one floor by the stairs.
If you only go up one floor, use the stairs, not the elevator.
column2: 只上一层的话，走楼梯，别坐电梯。

column1: The cafeteria is on the 1st floor.
Pick up packages at the security office on the 1st floor.
I lost the key to Room 305.
column2: 我把305号房间的钥匙弄丢了。

column1: Take bus number 7 and go three stops.
What floor is the office on?
It's the 2nd floor. Just go up one floor.
For lengths of time we also use the two number sets. Many of them can be said in two ways with the same meaning.
column2: 表示时长也会用到两套数字。很多可以用两种方式表达同一个意思。

column1: In speaking use "한 달, 하루"; in documents use "일 개월, 일 일".
column2: 口语中用 "한 달，하루"；文件中用 "일 개월，일 일"。

column1: 한 달 is used in speaking, and "일 개월" in documents and formal speech. Visa documents use "개월".
column2: 한 달 用于口语，"일 개월" 用于文件和正式场合。签证文件用 "개월"。

column1: 하루, 이틀, 사흘, 나흘 are native Korean words for counting days. From 나흘 (4 days), people use "사 일, 오 일" more.
column2: 하루，이틀，사흘，나흘 是数天数的韩语固有词。从 나흘 (4天) 开始，人们更多地用 "사 일，오 일"。

column1: It's been a month since I came to Korea.
I call home once a month.
column2: 我一个月给家里打一次电话。

column1: Life in Korea was hard for the first month.
column2: 第一个月在韩国的生活很辛苦。

column1: The language course is three months long.
Please come back in one month.
If you don't use the card for over a month, it gets blocked.
column2: 卡一个月以上不用的话会被停用。

column1: I studied in the library for two hours.
column2: 我在图书馆学习了两个小时。

column1: After studying two hours, I rest for ten minutes.
column2: 学习两个小时后，我休息十分钟。

column1: I'm on vacation for two weeks.
The results will come out in two weeks.
A visa extension takes about two weeks.
column2: 签证延期大约需要两周。

column1: On weekends I work part-time five hours a day.
column2: 周末我一天打工5个小时。

column1: If you want a day off, tell us in advance.
column2: 想请一天假的话，请提前告诉我们。

column1: The package will arrive in two days.
Please come back in three days.
I was sick for three days.
We get three days off for Seollal.
I have studied at Jeonju University for three years.
column2: 我在全州大学学习了三年。

column1: I lived in Korea for three years.
I'll study hard for three years and get a job at a hotel.
column2: 我要努力学习三年，然后在酒店找工作。

column1: Sam, how long has it been since you came to Korea?
It's been one year and six months.
How long is left until graduation?
About a year and a half.
English "older brother, older sister" becomes different words in Korean depending on whether the speaker is a man or a woman.
column2: 中文的 "哥哥、姐姐" 不分说话人性别，但韩语里根据说话人是男是女用不同的词。

column1: Men say "형, 누나"; women say "오빠, 언니".
Unlike English, Korean uses "형, 오빠, 누나, 언니" for close older people who are not family. At school, too, people call close seniors "형" or "언니".
column2: 和中文类似，韩语也用 "형，오빠，누나，언니" 称呼关系亲近的非亲属年长者。在学校里，人们也把亲近的前辈叫作 "형" 或 "언니"。

column1: 아빠, 엄마 are used by children or between close people. When talking to others, "아버지, 어머니" sounds more polite.
column2: 아빠，엄마 是小孩或亲近的人之间用的。跟别人说起时，用 "아버지，어머니" 更礼貌。

column1: Call younger siblings by name. Don't call "동생!". Add "아/야" after the name: "민하야", "샘아".
column2: 叫弟弟妹妹时叫名字，不要叫 "동생!"。在名字后面加 "아/야"："민하야"，"샘아"。

column1: My older brother helped me a lot.
Hey (older brother), do you want to go to Nepal together next month?
column2: 哥，下个月要不要一起去尼泊尔？

column1: My older brother is a graduate student.
Oppa, can you look at this document for me?
column2: 哥，能帮我看一下这份文件吗？

column1: My older sister lives in Singapore.
My older sister got married, so I sent wedding money.
column2: 我姐姐结婚了，所以我寄了礼金。

column1: My older sister is two years older than me.
Unni, where did you buy this makeup?
column2: 姐，这个化妆品在哪儿买的？

column1: My younger sibling goes to school.
I send money for my younger sibling's school fees.
(보고 싶다 = to miss, want to see)
I had a video call with my father on his birthday.
column2: 爸爸生日那天我和他视频通话了。

column1: My mother's food is the most delicious.
The gochujang my mother sent has arrived.
column2: 妈妈寄来的辣椒酱到了。

column1: I sent photos to my parents.
I worry most about my parents' health.
Sam, how many brothers and sisters do you have?
column2: 山姆，你有几个兄弟姐妹？

column1: I have one older brother, one older sister and one younger sister.
column2: 我有一个哥哥、一个姐姐和一个妹妹。

column1: They live in Dhaka with my older brother.
column2: 他们和我哥哥住在达卡。

column1: At Korean universities, people call each other by titles like "교수님" and "선배님" more than by name. This is different from English, where people often use first names.
column2: 在韩国大学里，人们更常用 "교수님"、"선배님" 这样的称谓而不是名字来称呼对方，这和中文用 "王老师"、"师兄" 称呼人的习惯很像。

column1: Call professors "family name + 교수님", and classmates "name + 씨".
column2: 称呼教授用 "姓 + 교수님"，称呼同学用 "名字 + 씨"。

column1: Calling an older or higher person "name + 씨" is very rude. Don't say "임 씨" or "현정 씨"; say "임 교수님" or "교수님".
column2: 用 "名字 + 씨" 称呼年长或地位高的人非常不礼貌。不要说 "임 씨" 或 "현정 씨"，要说 "임 교수님" 或 "교수님"。

column1: In Korean names, the family name comes first. In "김민하", "김" is the family name and "민하" is the given name. Job titles go after the family name.
column2: 韩国人的名字姓在前，和中文一样。"김민하" 中 "김" 是姓，"민하" 是名。职位放在姓的后面。

column1: I've finished the assignment. (to the TA)
The TA taught me how to register for classes.
Until what time is the department office open today? (to the TA)
column2: 助教，系办公室今天开到几点？

column1: Please ask the head of the department.
The head of the department is in class now.
I handed in my scholarship application form. (to the department head)
column2: 系主任，我交了奖学金申请表。

column1: Thanks to you (my senior), I got used to it well.
column2: 多亏了前辈，我很快就适应了。

column1: to get used to, to adapt
I'll buy you a meal next time. (to a senior)
column2: 下次我请你吃饭。(对前辈说)

column1: Aisha, the professor is looking for you.
honorific title (after a name or job title)
column2: 尊称 (加在名字或职位后)

column1: Sam, this is Professor Im Hyeonjeong, who just joined us.
column2: 山姆，这位是新来的林贤贞教授。

column1: Nice to meet you, Professor. My name is Sam.
column2: 教授，很高兴见到您。我叫山姆。

column1: Nice to meet you, Sam. Let's have a good semester.
column2: 山姆，很高兴见到你。这学期好好相处吧。

column1: These are words for calling people you don't know. Korean borrows family words for this, like "uncle" or "aunt".
column2: 这些是称呼陌生人的词。和中文的 "叔叔、阿姨" 一样，韩语也借用亲属称谓来称呼。

column1: Call strangers "저기요", staff in restaurants "여기요", and shop owners "사장님".
column2: 称呼陌生人用 "저기요"，称呼餐厅服务员用 "여기요"，称呼店主用 "사장님"。

column1: The safest words are "저기요" and "여기요". You can use them with anyone. To call staff in a restaurant, say "여기요".
column2: 最稳妥的是 "저기요" 和 "여기요"，对谁都可以用。在餐厅叫服务员时说 "여기요"。

column1: 아줌마 can sound rude, so use "아주머니", "이모님" or "사장님". Young women don't like being called "아주머니".
column2: 아줌마 可能听起来不礼貌，所以用 "아주머니"、"이모님" 或 "사장님"。年轻女性不喜欢被叫作 "아주머니"。

column1: Shop owners, men or women, like being called "사장님".
column2: 店主不论男女都喜欢被叫作 "사장님"。

column1: Excuse me (owner), how much is this?
to pay, to calculate the bill
Please give me a discount on this.
Auntie, the side dishes are really good.
Sir, please let me off in front of City Hall.
column2: 师傅，请在市政府前面让我下车。

column1: Sir, is this the right way?
Ma'am, does this bus go to the market?
column2: 阿姨，这辆公交车去市场吗？

column1: Ma'am, how much is this fruit?
Ma'am, is there a pharmacy near here?
Excuse me, you left your umbrella.
column2: 这位顾客，您的伞落下了。

column1: May I see your ID, please?
column2: 这位顾客，可以看一下您的身份证吗？

column1: Excuse me, may I ask the way?
column2: 打扰一下，可以问个路吗？

column1: Excuse me, you dropped your wallet.
column2: 打扰一下，您的钱包掉了。

column1: Excuse me, does this bus go to City Hall?
column2: 打扰一下，这辆公交车去市政府吗？

column1: excuse me, over here (to call staff)
column2: 这里，服务员 (叫服务员时)

column1: Excuse me, I'd like to pay.
Yes, what can I get you?
Auntie, one doenjang jjigae and one bowl of rice, please.
column2: 阿姨，请来一份大酱汤和一碗米饭。

column1: Okay, I'll bring it right away.
An action a person does (문을 열다) and something that happens by itself (문이 열리다) use different words. English uses "open" for both, but Korean has a pair.
column2: 人做的动作 (문을 열다) 和自己发生的事 (문이 열리다) 用不同的词。中文都说 "开"，但韩语里是一对词。

column1: If a person does it, "을/를 열다"; if it happens by itself, "이/가 열리다".
column2: 人做的用 "을/를 열다"；自己发生的用 "이/가 열리다"。

column1: The particle shows the difference. For what a person does, use "을/를"; for what happens by itself, use "이/가": "문을 열어요", "문이 열려요".
column2: 用助词来区分。人做的事用 "을/를"，自己发生的事用 "이/가"："문을 열어요"，"문이 열려요"。

column1: When you report a problem, use the "by itself" verb: "문이 안 열려요", "컴퓨터가 안 켜져요", "불이 안 꺼져요".
column2: 报告问题时，用 "自己发生" 的动词："문이 안 열려요"，"컴퓨터가 안 켜져요"，"불이 안 꺼져요"。

column1: It smells, so please open the window.
to open (by itself), to be opened
The door opens when you touch your card.
Close the door when you go out.
Close the door when you turn on the air conditioner.
to close (by itself), to be closed
The door closed because of the wind.
Don't put your hand in when the elevator door is closing.
column2: 电梯门正在关的时候，不要把手伸进去。

column1: If it's dark, turn on your phone's flashlight.
column2: 太黑的话，打开手机手电筒。

column1: to turn on (by itself), to come on
When night comes, the streetlights come on.
Turn off the lights when you leave the lecture room.
I turn off the light before I go to sleep.
Be sure to turn off the electric blanket when you go out.
column2: 出门时一定要关掉电热毯。

column1: to go off, to go out (light, machine)
The battery ran out, so my phone turned off.
column2: 电池没电了，手机关机了。

column1: The lecture room door won't open. (to the TA)
Did you open it with the key?
Yes, I tried with the key, but it won't open.
column2: 是的，用钥匙试过了，但还是打不开。

column1: Really? Are the lights on inside?
open the door ↔ the door opens
close the door ↔ the door closes
turn on the light ↔ the light comes on
turn off the light ↔ the light goes out
When things break, snap or fall, Korean shows whether someone did it or it happened by itself.
column2: 东西破了、断了、掉了的时候，韩语会区分是有人做的还是自己发生的。

column1: If you did it, "깼어요, 떨어뜨렸어요"; if it happened by itself, "깨졌어요, 떨어졌어요".
column2: 自己做的说 "깼어요，떨어뜨렸어요"；自己发生的说 "깨졌어요，떨어졌어요"。

column1: When you report a mistake, say it honestly: "제가 ~을/를 ~했습니다". "제가 컵을 깼습니다. 죄송합니다."
column2: 报告失误时要诚实地说："제가 ~을/를 ~했습니다"。"제가 컵을 깼습니다. 죄송합니다."

column1: When you don't know who did it, or it happened by itself, say "~이/가 ~졌습니다": "유리가 깨져 있었습니다." (The glass was already broken.)
column2: 不知道是谁做的，或是自己发生的，就说 "~이/가 ~졌습니다"："유리가 깨져 있었습니다." (玻璃已经碎了。)

column1: I broke a plate. I'm sorry.
column2: 我打碎了一个盘子。对不起。

column1: I broke a bowl while washing the dishes.
column2: 我洗碗时打碎了一个碗。

column1: Wrap broken glass in newspaper and throw it away.
column2: 碎玻璃要用报纸包好再扔。

column1: to cut, to hang up, to quit
Since I quit drinking, I'm saving money.
to break, to be cut off
The internet went down, so I can't make the call.
I dropped my phone in the toilet.
column2: 我把手机掉进马桶里了。

column1: Please fix my room's door handle.
column2: 请修一下我房间的门把手。

column1: Boss, I'm sorry. I dropped a box of cups.
column2: 老板，对不起。我把一箱杯子摔了。

column1: No, I'm okay. But two cups broke.
column2: 没有，我没事。不过碎了两个杯子。

column1: Okay. Thanks for telling me right away. Be careful next time.
column2: 好的。谢谢你马上告诉我。下次小心。

column1: Words for starting and ending also come in pairs: what a person does and what happens by itself.
column2: 表示开始和结束的词也是成对的：人做的和自己发生的。

column1: If a person does it, "시작하다, 끝내다, 바꾸다"; if it happens by itself, "시작되다, 끝나다, 바뀌다".
column2: 人做的用 "시작하다，끝내다，바꾸다"；自己发生的用 "시작되다，끝나다，바뀌다"。

column1: 몇 시에 끝나요? asks when the class ends; "몇 시까지 끝내요?" asks by when you have to finish it.
column2: 몇 시에 끝나요? 是问课几点结束；"몇 시까지 끝내요?" 是问要在几点之前做完。

column1: Notices and announcements often use the "by itself" verbs: "수업 시간이 바뀌었습니다", "시험 날짜가 정해졌습니다". They don't say who decided.
column2: 通知和公告常用 "自己发生" 的动词："수업 시간이 바뀌었습니다"，"시험 날짜가 정해졌습니다"。不说是谁决定的。

column1: I start a part-time job next week.
When the rainy season starts, it gets very humid.
column2: 雨季一开始就变得很潮湿。

column1: Finish tidying up, then go home.
What time does the class end?
When the semester ends, I'll go back to my hometown.
column2: 学期结束后，我要回老家。

column1: I changed my part-time job hours.
I changed my money into dollars.
Please hand in the documents by Thursday.
column2: 请在星期四之前交材料。

column1: I get my part-time pay on Friday.
There is a club gathering on Friday night.
column2: 星期五晚上有社团聚会。

column1: I work my part-time job on Saturdays too.
I go to the market on Saturday.
Can you go to the library on Saturday?
column2: 你星期六能去图书馆吗?

column1: I go to church on Sundays.
What date is your appointment at the immigration office?
column2: 你在出入境管理事务所的预约是几号?

column1: What day is the group meeting?
What day do we throw out the trash?
Words for talking about time, based on today.
column2: 以今天为基准说时间的词。

column1: The order is 어제, 오늘, 내일, 모레.
Don't put "에" after "오늘, 내일, 어제, 매일". But do put it in "주말에", "다음 주에".
column2: 오늘、내일、어제、매일 后面不加 "에"。但 "주말에"、"다음 주에" 要加。

column1: In the same way there are "이번 달, 지난달, 다음 달" (this month, last month, next month) and "올해, 작년, 내년" (this year, last year, next year).
column2: 同样还有 "이번 달、지난달、다음 달" (这个月、上个月、下个月) 和 "올해、작년、내년" (今年、去年、明年)。

column1: Did the money I sent yesterday arrive?
I'm going to Greece the day after tomorrow.
The day after tomorrow is my birthday.
Please finish it by the day after tomorrow.
I have a lot of assignments this week.
There is a health check this week.
The things I ordered last week haven't come yet.
There is a test next week.
What do you do on the weekend?
Are you open on weekends too?
I do morning exercises every day.
I work my part-time job on Saturday and rest on Sunday.
column2: 我星期六打工，星期天休息。

column1: How to say the hour and minutes. "시" and "분" use different numbers.
column2: 说几点几分的方法。"시" 和 "분" 用不同的数字。

column1: For hours use "한, 두, 세"; for minutes use "일, 이, 삼".
column2: 点 用 "한, 두, 세"，"分" 用 "일, 이, 삼"。

column1: For "시" use "한, 두, 세"; for "분" use "일, 이, 삼": 세 시 삼십 분 (3:30).
column2: 시 用 "한, 두, 세"，"분" 用 "일, 이, 삼"：세 시 삼십 분 (3:30)。

column1: Korean uses the 12-hour clock and puts "오전" (a.m.) or "오후" (p.m.) in front, like a.m./p.m. in English. Do not say "13 o'clock".
column2: 韩语用12小时制，前面加 "오전" (上午) 或 "오후" (下午)，和中文的上午、下午一样。不说 "13点"。

column1: Lunch time starts at twelve o'clock.
column2: 午饭时间从十二点开始。

column1: The bus comes every five minutes.
column2: 公交车每五分钟来一趟。

column1: There is a class in the morning.
I go to school at 8 a.m.
They see patients only in the morning.
Do you have time in the afternoon?
Let's meet at half past three.
I eat lunch at half past twelve.
Class finishes at half past six.
What time is the last bus?
I get up early in the morning.
I drink coffee in the morning.
Please come to the dorm cafeteria by 7 in the morning.
column2: 请在早上七点前到宿舍食堂。

column1: I have my part-time job this evening.
It's half past two. There is a class at three.
Verbs for the things you do from morning to night.

column1: How to count Korean money and say prices. US money is called "달러" (dollars).

column2: 钱用 "일, 이, 삼" 数字说。1000韩元不说 "일천 원"，只说 "천 원"。

column2: 韩国餐厅和食堂常见的食物名称。

column1: A Korean meal is made of rice, soup and side dishes.
column2: 韩国的一顿饭由米饭、汤和小菜组成。

column2: 밥 먹었어요? (吃饭了吗?) 也可以当作问候语，和中文的 "吃了吗?" 一样。

column1: Rice, soup and side dishes (반찬) come out together. Side dishes are shared.
column2: 米饭、汤和小菜 (반찬) 一起上桌。小菜大家一起吃。

column1: I eat ramyeon when I study for exams.
We give you more rice for free.
Please leave the meat out of the bibimbap.
to take out, to leave out
When guests come, I serve bulgogi.
column2: 客人来时我做烤肉招待。

column1: Please make the tteokbokki less spicy.
column2: 辣炒年糕请做得不那么辣。

column1: One cold noodle soup and one spicy mixed cold noodles, please.
column2: 请给我一份水冷面和一份拌冷面。

column1: Kimchi is self-service. Please get it over there.
column2: 泡菜是自助的，请到那边拿。

column1: I pack gimbap when I go on a picnic.
column2: 去郊游时我做紫菜包饭带着。

column1: We eat samgyeopsal at club gatherings.

Bulgogi is the most delicious. Kimchi is a little spicy.

column1: For drinks, use "마시다" and count them with "잔, 병".

column1: For drinks, use "마시다" (to drink), just like "drink" in English.
column2: 饮料用 "마시다" (喝)，和中文的 "喝" 一样。

column1: 차 has two meanings: tea and car.
column2: 차 有两个意思：茶和车。

column1: I changed my phone plan to a cheaper one.
column2: 我把手机套餐换成了更便宜的。

column2: 从下个月开始，校车时间会变。

column1: Did you decide where to travel?
We decide the presentation date together with our group members.
column2: 我们和组员一起决定发表日期。

When your date for going home is decided, let me know.
column2: 回国日期定下来的话告诉我。

column2: 这个作业要在什么时候之前完成？

column1: It's like English "go, come", but Korean strictly decides by where the speaker is now. "다니다" means going back and forth regularly.
column2: 和中文的 "去、来" 相似，但韩语严格根据说话人现在的位置来决定。"다니다" 表示定期来回。

column1: Moving away is "가다", coming closer is "오다", and going back and forth regularly is "다니다".
column2: 离开是 "가다"，靠近是 "오다"，定期来回是 "다니다"。

column1: When you go to someone who is calling you, Korean says "가요": "샘 씨, 이리 와요!" "네, 지금 가요." Don't say "와요" like English "I'm coming!"
column2: 有人叫你、你往他那边去时，韩语说 "가요"："샘 씨, 이리 와요!" "네, 지금 가요." 不要像中文 "来了！" 那样说 "와요"。

column1: About your school, "전주대학교에 다녀요" means you are a student there. "학교에 가요" means you are on your way there now.
column2: 说到自己的学校时，"전주대학교에 다녀요" 表示你是那里的学生。"학교에 가요" 表示你现在正在去的路上。

column1: What time are you coming tomorrow?
My friend is coming to Korea this month.
column2: 我朋友这个月要来韩国。

I go to church every weekend.
Have a good trip. (Come back safely.)
I'll go to the pharmacy and come back.
I'll go to the bank and come back.

column2: 我去趟便利店。要我帮你买点什么吗？

When class ends, I go back to the dormitory.
Vacation is starting, so I'm going back to my home country next month.
column2: 要放假了，所以我下个月回国。

column2: 山姆，你在哪个学校上学？

column2: 我在全州大学上学。我是酒店管理专业的学生。

column1: I'm going to the bank. I'll be right back.
I attend the school (go every day)
column2: 我在这所学校上学 (每天去)

These are English "give" and "receive". If the receiver is someone above you, use "드리다" instead of "주다".
column2: 这些是中文的 "给" 和 "收"。如果接受的人地位比你高，就用 "드리다" 代替 "주다"。

column1: When I give, use "주다". When I give to someone above me, use "드리다". When I receive, use "받다".
column2: 我给别人时用 "주다"。给地位高的人时用 "드리다"。我接受时用 "받다"。

column1: Like English "do something for someone", Korean adds "give" after a verb: "-아/어 주다", "-아/어 드리다": "도와줘요", "도와드릴게요".
column2: 和中文的 "给…做、帮…做" 一样，韩语在动词后加 "给"："-아/어 주다"，"-아/어 드리다"："도와줘요"，"도와드릴게요"。

column1: The giver is shown with "한테서, 에게서" (for an organization, "에서"): "학교에서 장학금을 받아요", "친구한테서 선물을 받았어요".
column2: 给的人用 "한테서，에게서" 表示 (机构用 "에서")："학교에서 장학금을 받아요"，"친구한테서 선물을 받았어요"。

column1: When you give something to or receive something from someone above you, use both hands.
column2: 给长辈东西或从长辈那里接东西时，要用双手。

column1: The school gave me a student ID card.
I gave my parents some pocket money.
column2: 我给了父母一些零花钱。

column1: On Teachers' Day, I gave flowers to my professor.
column2: 教师节那天，我给教授送了花。

column1: The professor gave me a book.
My mother gave me pocket money.
The cafe owner gave me a birthday present.
column2: 咖啡店老板给了我生日礼物。

column1: When you get your part-time pay, be sure to check it.
column2: 拿到打工工资时，一定要核对一下。

column1: I sent a photo to my friend.
I sent money to Uzbekistan with an app.
column2: 我用应用往乌兹别克斯坦汇了钱。

I'll give the umbrella back tomorrow.
When you go back to your country, they return the dormitory deposit.

column2: 好，收到了。你也发给助教了吗？

I give the assignment to the professor

Korean separates English "know" and "understand". "모르다" is a separate word that means the opposite of "알다".
column2: 韩语区分 "知道" 和 "理解"。"모르다" 是单独的一个词，意思和 "알다" 相反。

column1: The opposite of "알다" is "모르다", and you answer instructions with "알겠습니다".
column2: 알다 的反义词是 "모르다"，回答指示时用 "알겠습니다"。

column1: When you answer an instruction, say "알겠습니다", not "알아요". "알아요" sounds like "I already know", so it's rude.
column2: 回答指示时说 "알겠습니다"，不说 "알아요"。"알아요" 听起来像 "我早就知道了"，不礼貌。

column1: In "알다", the ㄹ sometimes drops: 압니다, 아세요, 아는 사람. "모르다" changes to "몰라요, 몰랐어요".
column2: 알다 的 ㄹ 有时会脱落：압니다，아세요，아는 사람。"모르다" 变成 "몰라요，몰랐어요"。

column1: Do you know the phone number?
Do you know a cheap restaurant near here?
column2: 你知道这附近有便宜的餐厅吗？

column1: If you don't know the way, look at a map app.
column2: 不认识路的话，看地图应用。

column1: Did you understand everything in class?
Yes, I understand. I'll do that.
column2: 好的，明白了。我会那样做的。

column1: I understand. I'll send it by tomorrow.
column2: 明白了。我明天之前发过去。

column1: I understand. I'll bring the assignment tomorrow.
column2: 明白了。我明天把作业带来。

column1: You spoke fast, so I didn't catch it.
column2: 你说得太快了，我没听懂。

column1: Now I understand a little spoken Korean.
column2: 现在我能听懂一点韩语了。

Please tell me the Wi-Fi password.
Do you know how to use this printer?

column2: 把学生证放在这里，然后按这个按钮。明白了吗？

column2: 对不起。我没听懂。请再给我演示一次。

column1: 하다 is what I do (do), and "되다" is what happens or gets done (become, be done, can). "되다" is also used for permission and "not allowed".
column2: 하다 是我做的事 (做)，"되다" 是发生或被完成的事 (成为、做好、可以)。"되다" 也用于表示允许和 "不行"。

column1: When I do it, use "하다". When it gets done, use "되다". Permission is "돼요", and "not allowed" is "안 돼요".
column2: 自己做用 "하다"。被完成用 "되다"。允许是 "돼요"，"不行" 是 "안 돼요"。

column1: Like English "can / may", "돼요" shows permission and possibility. "Can I?" is "돼요?", and "You can't" is "안 돼요".
column2: 和中文的 "可以" 一样，"돼요" 表示允许和可能。"可以吗？" 是 "돼요?"，"不可以" 是 "안 돼요"。

column1: When a thing doesn't work, say "안 돼요": "카드가 안 돼요", "전화가 안 돼요".
column2: 东西不能用时说 "안 돼요"："카드가 안 돼요"，"전화가 안 돼요"。

column1: On my day off, I do laundry and clean.
column2: 休息日我洗衣服、打扫卫生。

No thanks. I don't need a bag.
Professor, I'm all ready for the presentation.

column2: 那个，我可以去一下洗手间吗？

This separates English "look, see, show". Looking on purpose is "보다", something coming into your eyes by itself is "보이다", and letting others see is "보여 주다".
column2: 这里区分中文的 "看、看见、给…看"。有意去看是 "보다"，自然进入眼帘是 "보이다"，让别人看是 "보여 주다"。

column1: Looking on purpose is "보다", seeing by itself is "보이다", and letting others see is "보여 주다".
column2: 有意去看是 "보다"，自然看见是 "보이다"，给别人看是 "보여 주다"。

column1: The particles are different: "산을 봐요" (I look at the mountain), "산이 보여요" (I can see the mountain). "산을 보여요" is wrong.
column2: 助词不同："산을 봐요" (我看山)，"산이 보여요" (我能看见山)。"산을 보여요" 是错的。

column1: 보다 has many other meanings too: 시험을 보다 (to take an exam), 장을 보다 (to shop for groceries), 면접을 보다 (to have an interview), 아이를 보다 (to look after a child).
column2: 보다 还有很多其他意思：시험을 보다 (考试)，장을 보다 (买菜)，면접을 보다 (面试)，아이를 보다 (照看孩子)。

column1: After class, I watch Korean lessons on YouTube.
column2: 下课后，我在YouTube上看韩语课。

column1: I can see the bank over there.
Because of the fog, I can't see well ahead.
column2: 因为有雾，前面看不太清楚。

Show the doctor where you got hurt.
column2: 给医生看看你受伤的地方。

column1: I showed photos of my hometown to my professor.
column2: 我给教授看了我家乡的照片。

column1: It's my first time, but I'll give it a try.
column2: 虽然是第一次，但我试试看。

column1: Please show me your residence card.
column2: 请出示您的外国人登录证。

column1: Please look at this screen. Is your name correct?
column2: 请看这个屏幕。您的名字对吗？

column1: I'm sorry. The letters are small, so I can't see well.
column2: 对不起。字太小了，我看不太清楚。

column1: English "have" and "be (somewhere)" are both "있다" in Korean. You can tell the meaning by the particle in front.
column2: 中文的 "有" 和 "在" 在韩语里都是 "있다"。可以通过前面的助词来区分意思。

column1: 이/가 있다 is "have", "에 있다" is "be (somewhere)", and the opposite of both is "없다".
column2: 이/가 있다 是 "有"，"에 있다" 是 "在 (某处)"，两者的反义词都是 "없다"。

column1: Look at the particle to know the meaning. "이/가 있다" is "have", and "에 있다" is "be (somewhere)".
column2: 看助词就知道意思。"이/가 있다" 是 "有"，"에 있다" 是 "在 (某处)"。

column1: The opposite for both meanings is "없다" (not have, not be there). Don't say "안 있다".
column2: 两种意思的反义词都是 "없다" (没有，不在)。不要说 "안 있다"。

column1: The honorific form splits into two: "be (somewhere)" is "계시다", and "have" is "있으시다".
column2: 敬语形式分为两种："在 (某处)" 是 "계시다"，"有" 是 "있으시다"。

column1: Do you have time tomorrow? Let's eat together.

column2: 不，他现在不在这里。他在讲堂。

column2: 你有没有教授的电话号码？

column1: Yes, I do. Just a moment.
Listening on purpose is "듣다" (to listen), and sound coming into your ears by itself is "들리다" (to hear). "듣다" and "묻다" change to "들어요, 물어요", so they are easy to confuse.
column2: 有意去听是 "듣다" (听)，声音自然传进耳朵是 "들리다" (听见)。"듣다" 和 "묻다" 变成 "들어요，물어요"，所以容易混淆。

column1: Listening on purpose is "듣다", hearing by itself is "들리다", and asking about what you don't know is "묻다".
column2: 有意去听是 "듣다"，自然听见是 "들리다"，询问不知道的事是 "묻다"。

column1: In "듣다, 묻다, 걷다", ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel: 들어요, 물어요, 걸어요. But "듣고, 묻고, 걷고" stay the same.
column2: 듣다，묻다，걷다 的 ㄷ 在元音前变成 ㄹ：들어요，물어요，걸어요。但 "듣고，묻고，걷고" 不变。

column1: In noisy places, say "안 들려요" or "크게 말해 주세요". It's dangerous to say "네" when you didn't hear.
column2: 在吵闹的地方，说 "안 들려요" 或 "크게 말해 주세요"。没听见就说 "네" 是很危险的。

column1: 말을 듣다 also means "to obey": "동생이 말을 안 들어요." "수업을 듣다" means "to take a class".
column2: 말을 듣다 也有 "听话" 的意思："동생이 말을 안 들어요." "수업을 듣다" 是 "上课，听课"。

column1: On my way to school, I listen to Korean listening practice.
column2: 上学路上我听韩语听力练习。

column1: You're wearing a mask, so I can't hear you well.
column2: 你戴着口罩，我听不太清楚。

column1: Excuse me, may I ask you something?
column2: 打扰一下，我可以问您点事吗？

column1: A stranger asked about my visa.

column1: 넣다 is used for many things, not only objects: 설탕을 넣다 (to add sugar), 돈을 넣다 (to deposit money), 기름을 넣다 (to fill up with gas), 전원을 넣다 (to turn on the power).

column1: English uses one word, "put on, wear", but Korean uses different verbs for different parts of the body.

column1: Clothes are "입다", shoes and socks are "신다", and hats and glasses are "쓰다".
column2: 衣服用 "입다"，鞋袜用 "신다"，帽子和眼镜用 "쓰다"。

column2: 신발을 입다 和 "모자를 입다" 是错的。不要直接套用中文的 "穿、戴"。

column1: To describe what someone is wearing now, use "-고 있다" or "-았/었-": "빨간 옷을 입고 있어요", "안경을 썼어요".
column2: 描述某人现在穿着什么时，用 "-고 있다" 或 "-았/었-"："빨간 옷을 입고 있어요"，"안경을 썼어요"。

column1: In Korean homes and some restaurants, you take off your shoes before going in. It's the same in Myanmar.

column1: Things on your hands, arms, and neck also have their own verbs. Things you slip on are "끼다", things you strap around are "차다", things you tie are "매다", and accessories are "하다".
column2: 戴在手上、胳膊上和脖子上的东西也有各自的动词。套上的用 "끼다"，绑在周围的用 "차다"，系的用 "매다"，饰品用 "하다"。

column1: Gloves and rings are "끼다", watches are "차다", ties and seat belts are "매다", and accessories are "하다".
column2: 手套和戒指用 "끼다"，手表用 "차다"，领带和安全带用 "매다"，饰品用 "하다"。

column1: If you're not sure, "하다" also works. People will understand "장갑을 해요" or "넥타이를 해요".
column2: 如果不确定，用 "하다" 也可以。说 "장갑을 해요" 或 "넥타이를 해요" 别人也能听懂。

column1: During exams, you may be told to take off your watch. You must not wear a smartwatch.
column2: 考试时可能会要求你摘下手表。不能戴智能手表。

column1: When you get in a car, you'll hear "안전띠를 매세요". In Korea, you must wear a seat belt in every seat.
column2: 上车时你会听到 "안전띠를 매세요"。在韩国，所有座位都必须系安全带。

column1: Wear rubber gloves when you wash the dishes.

The verb for taking off also depends on the verb for putting on. 입다·신다·쓰다 use "벗다", 차다·매다 use "풀다", and 끼다 uses "빼다".
column2: 脱下的动词也取决于穿戴的动词。입다·신다·쓰다 用 "벗다"，차다·매다 用 "풀다"，끼다 用 "빼다"。

column1: Clothes, shoes, and hats are "벗다", watches and ties are "풀다", and gloves and rings are "빼다".
column2: 衣服、鞋和帽子用 "벗다"，手表和领带用 "풀다"，手套和戒指用 "빼다"。

column1: 풀다 has many meanings: 끈을 풀다 (to untie a string), 문제를 풀다 (to solve a problem), 짐을 풀다 (to unpack), 피로를 풀다 (to relieve tiredness).
column2: 풀다 有很多意思：끈을 풀다 (解开绳子)，문제를 풀다 (解题)，짐을 풀다 (打开行李)，피로를 풀다 (消除疲劳)。

column1: 빼다 means taking out something that is inside: 이름을 빼다 (to take a name off a list), 살을 빼다 (to lose weight), 돈을 빼다 (to withdraw money).
column2: 빼다 表示把里面的东西拿出来：이름을 빼다 (把名字从名单上去掉)，살을 빼다 (减肥)，돈을 빼다 (取钱)。

column1: The classroom was hot, so I took off my jacket.

column1: If your practice uniform or gloves are missing or torn, say so before practice starts: "장갑이 찢어졌습니다. 새것을 주십시오."

column1: Every pool has its own rules. Many pools say you must wear a swim cap.

column1: How to tell "good" and "like" apart. "좋다" says what something is like and uses "이/가". "좋아하다" is something you do, so it uses "을/를".

column1: Use the right particle: "커피가 좋아요", "커피를 좋아해요". "커피를 좋아요" is wrong.

column1: For other people's feelings, use only "좋아하다": "아이샤 씨는 커피를 좋아해요." "아이샤 씨는 커피가 좋아요" sounds unnatural.

column1: For good news use "기쁘다", while doing something "즐겁다", when excited "신나다", and for a deep feeling "행복하다".

column1: In English, "fun" is used widely, but Korean separates it: a movie is "재미있다", a trip or a party is "즐겁다", excitement is "신나다".

column1: When you are glad to meet someone, use "반갑다" rather than "기쁘다".

column1: If it's heavy going, use "힘들다"; if it's hard to work out, "어렵다"; if you want to rest, "피곤하다".
column2: 费劲用 "힘들다"；难懂用 "어렵다"；想休息用 "피곤하다"。

column1: English "tired / tiring" can be both "힘들다" and "피곤하다". If the work you are doing now is hard, say "힘들어요"; if your body wants to rest, say "피곤해요".
column2: 中文的 "累" 在韩语里可以是 "힘들다" 也可以是 "피곤하다"。正在做的事很辛苦，说 "힘들어요"；身体想休息，说 "피곤해요"。

column1: For "to the end" use "다", for all people or things "모두", and for counting a total "전부".
column2: 表示 "做完" 用 "다"，表示所有的人或事物用 "모두"，计算总数用 "전부"。

column1: 다 했어요? is a question you often hear when doing group assignments. Answer "네, 다 했습니다", "거의 다 했습니다", or "아직 못 했습니다".
column2: 다 했어요? 是做小组作业时常听到的问题。回答 "네, 다 했습니다"，"거의 다 했습니다" 或 "아직 못 했습니다"。

column1: 모두 and "전부" can also be used like nouns: "모두가 알아요", "전부를 주세요". "다" is not used that way.
column2: 모두 和 "전부" 也可以像名词一样用："모두가 알아요"，"전부를 주세요"。"다" 不能这样用。

column1: How many people are there in total?

column1: Words that link one sentence to another. "그리고" adds something (and, and then), and "그래서" links a reason and a result (so, that's why).

column2: 合成一个句子时，"그리고" 变成 "-고"，"그래서" 变成 "-아서/어서"："비가 와서 안 가요."

column1: To join two words, use "하고" rather than "그리고": "빵하고 우유".
column2: 连接两个名词时用 "하고"，不用 "그리고"："빵하고 우유"。

column1: I'm Sam. And this is Aisha.

column1: All of them mean "but". "그런데" is also used to change the topic (by the way).

column2: 表示对比用 "하지만，그렇지만"，转换话题用 "그런데"。

column1: When you join them into one sentence, they become "-지만" or "-는데": "비싸지만 맛있어요."
column2: 合成一个句子时，变成 "-지만" 或 "-는데"："비싸지만 맛있어요."

column1: Starting with "그런데" is a sign that you are bringing up something new: "그런데요, 교수님…"
column2: 用 "그런데" 开头是要提出新话题的信号："그런데요, 교수님…"

column1: If you answer an older person or boss right away with "하지만", it can sound like you are arguing. Start softly with "네, 그런데요…".
column2: 如果对长辈或上司一开口就说 "하지만"，听起来像在顶嘴。用 "네, 그런데요…" 委婉地开头。

By the way, did you eat?

It means "then, in that case". "그럼" is short for "그러면", but it is also used as an answer meaning "of course".
column2: 意思是 "那么，那样的话"。"그럼" 是 "그러면" 的缩略，但也用作回答，表示 "当然"。

column1: When saying goodbye, start with "그럼": "그럼, 안녕히 계세요", "그럼 들어가세요".
column2: 告别时用 "그럼" 开头："그럼, 안녕히 계세요"，"그럼 들어가세요"。

column1: 그럼요 is a happy "yes". With older people or bosses, "네, 물론입니다" is more polite.
column2: 그럼요 是愉快的 "是"。对长辈或上司说 "네, 물론입니다" 更礼貌。

column1: When you join it into one sentence, it becomes "-(으)면": "시간이 없으면 내일 하세요."
column2: 合成一个句子时，变成 "-(으)면"："시간이 없으면 내일 하세요."

column1: Then I'll come back tomorrow morning.
Well then, I'll be going now.
(먼저 가 보겠습니다 = I'll be leaving first)
Then I'll contact you again next week.
Can I go with you? Of course.
column2: 我可以和你一起去吗？当然。

column1: Of course. Ask me any time.
Can I go first? Yes, go ahead.
column2: 我可以先走吗？好的，请吧。
原来如此。我之前不知道。

column1: Oh, so that's how they do it in Korea. I see.
column2: 啊，原来韩国是这样做的。我明白了。

column2: 我明天按平时的时间来上班吗？

column1: 그러니까 gives the reason first and then the result (so), and "왜냐하면" gives the result first and then the reason (because).
column2: 그러니까 先说原因再说结果 (所以)，"왜냐하면" 先说结果再说原因 (因为)。

column1: To give the result use "그러니까", and to give the reason use "왜냐하면".
Before an order or a suggestion, use "그러니까", not "그래서".
column2: 在命令或建议之前，用 "그러니까"，不用 "그래서"。

column1: 때문에 is for bad results, and "덕분에" is for good results: "교수님 덕분에 잘 배웠습니다."
column2: 때문에 用于不好的结果，"덕분에" 用于好的结果："교수님 덕분에 잘 배웠습니다."

column1: We don't have time. So hurry up.
column2: 我们没时间了。所以快点。

column1: It's raining. So take an umbrella.

column2: 好的。可是为什么要先关电源呢？
因为它可能会突然转动。

column2: 明白了。多亏了您，我学到了很多。

column1: Question words for "what, which, what kind of". Some are used alone, and some come before a noun.
column2: 表示 "什么、哪个、什么样的" 的疑问词。有的单独使用，有的放在名词前面。

column1: Use "뭐" alone, "무슨" for type, "어떤" for what something is like, and "어느" for choosing.
column2: 뭐 单独使用，问种类用 "무슨"，问怎么样用 "어떤"，选择时用 "어느"。

column1: The place of the question word is different from English. English puts it first ("What are you doing?"), but Korean puts it before the verb: "뭐 해요?"
column2: 和中文一样，疑问词不需要放在句首 ("你在做什么？")，韩语放在动词前面："뭐 해요?"

column1: 뭐 is short for "무엇". Use "뭐" when speaking, and "무엇" in writing or formal speech.
column2: 뭐 是 "무엇" 的缩略。说话时用 "뭐"，书面语或正式场合用 "무엇"。

column1: 무슨 일 있어요? is a caring question: "Is something wrong?"
column2: 무슨 일 있어요? 是关心的问话："出什么事了吗？"

column1: For numbers use "몇", for prices "얼마", and for time and degree "얼마나".
column2: 数量用 "몇"，价格用 "얼마"，时间和程度用 "얼마나"。

column2: 不要写 "몇 일"；要写 "며칠"："몇 월 며칠이에요?"

column2: 몇 的发音随后面的词变化：몇 명 [면 명]，몇 개 [멷 깨]，몇 월 [며 둴]。

column1: All of them are close to "work" in English. In speech use "일"; work you hand in for a class is "과제"; a job students do for money is "아르바이트"; and working fixed hours at a place is "근무".

column2: 口语中用 "일"；课上要交的作业用 "과제"；学生打工用 "아르바이트"；按固定时间工作用 "근무"。

column1: Words for the money a student gets. Money from your parents is "용돈", money from the school is "장학금", money from a part-time job is "아르바이트비", and pay for one hour is "시급".

column1: 휴(休) means rest. A fixed day off is "휴일", days off you ask for are "휴가", and a short rest while you study or work is "휴식".
column2: 휴(休) 的意思是休息。固定的休息日是 "휴일"，申请的假期是 "휴가"，学习或工作中短暂的休息是 "휴식"。

column1: Fixed days are "휴일", days you ask for are "휴가", and a short break is "휴식".
column2: 固定的日子是 "휴일"，申请的是 "휴가"，短暂休息是 "휴식"。

column1: People say "휴가를 내다, 휴가를 쓰다, 휴가를 받다": "내일 휴가를 내고 싶습니다."
column2: 常说 "휴가를 내다，휴가를 쓰다，휴가를 받다"："내일 휴가를 내고 싶습니다."

column1: The red days on the calendar are "공휴일" (public holidays). For Seollal and Chuseok, you get three days off each.
column2: 日历上的红色日子是 "공휴일" (法定节假日)。春节和中秋节各放三天假。

column1: The "휴게" in "휴게실" (break room) and "휴게 시간" (break time) is the same "휴".

column1: All are close to "customer, guest" in English. People who come to a shop or a home are "손님"; the polite word banks and big stores use is "고객"; and a customer who comes often is a "단골".

Words for places in school life: "school, university, campus, department".
column2: 学校生活中表示地点的词："学校、大学、校园、系"。

column1: In general use "학교"; for school after high school, "대학교"; for the grounds and buildings, "캠퍼스"; and for your major, "학과".
column2: 一般用 "학교"；高中以后的学校用 "대학교"；校园的场地和建筑用 "캠퍼스"；专业用 "학과"。

column1: 학과 is often shortened to "과": "같은 과 친구" (a friend in the same department), "과대표" (department representative).
column2: 학과 常缩成 "과"："같은 과 친구" (同系的朋友)，"과대표" (系代表)。

column1: 캠퍼스 means all the grounds and buildings of a school. Jeonju University's campus has buildings such as 지역혁신관, 스타센터 and 자유관.
column2: 캠퍼스 指学校所有的场地和建筑。全州大学的校园里有 지역혁신관、스타센터、자유관 等建筑。

column1: Write down the school address in Korean.

Native Korean words used in speech pair up with Chinese-origin words used in documents. They mean the same but differ in style.
column2: 口语中用的韩语固有词和文件中用的汉字词成对出现。意思相同，但语体不同。

column1: In speech use "고치다, 바꾸다"; in documents and on signs use "수리, 교체, 점검".
column2: 口语中用 "고치다，바꾸다"；文件和标识上用 "수리，교체，점검"。

column1: Signs use Chinese-origin words: "수리 중" (under repair), "점검 중" (under inspection), "사용 금지" (do not use), "교체 필요" (needs replacing).
column2: 标识上用汉字词："수리 중" (修理中)，"점검 중" (检修中)，"사용 금지" (禁止使用)，"교체 필요" (需要更换)。

column1: 교체 means replacing an old thing with a new one, and "교환" means swapping one thing for another. In shops, you see "교환, 환불" (exchange, refund).
column2: 교체 是用新的换掉旧的，"교환" 是把一个东西换成另一个。在商店里会看到 "교환，환불" (换货，退款)。

column1: Please correct the wrong name on this document.
column2: 请改正这份文件上写错的名字。

column1: It takes two days to repair.
How much does it cost to repair a phone screen?
Can I change to a room on the first floor?
column2: 我可以换到一楼的房间吗？

column1: The fluorescent light is flickering, so please replace it.
column2: 日光灯一闪一闪的，请换一下。

column1: Please exchange it for another size.
column2: 请给我换一个别的尺码。

column1: You can exchange it if you have the receipt.
It's too small, so I'd like to exchange it for a bigger size.
column2: 太小了，我想换大一号的。

column1: Check your assignment once more before you submit it.
column2: 提交作业前再检查一遍。

column1: The dormitory checks the fire extinguishers every month.

I reported our team project's progress to the professor.

column2: 我觉得是皮带磨坏了。需要换吗？

column2: 是的，得换了。贴上 "修理中" 的牌子。

column1: Words for finishing something. If it ends by itself, use "끝나다"; if you finish it, "마치다, 끝내다"; in documents, "완료하다".
column2: 表示结束的词。自己结束用 "끝나다"；自己把事情做完用 "마치다，끝내다"；文件中用 "완료하다"。

column1: If it ends by itself, "끝나다"; if you finish it, "끝내다, 마치다"; in documents, "완료".
column2: 自己结束用 "끝나다"；把事情做完用 "끝내다，마치다"；文件中用 "완료"。

column1: When you say you are done, use "다 했습니다", "마쳤습니다", "완료했습니다". Each one is more formal than the one before.
column2: 说自己做完了时，用 "다 했습니다"，"마쳤습니다"，"완료했습니다"。一个比一个正式。

column1: On screens or documents, "완료" means "completed", "진행 중" means "in progress", and "예정" means "scheduled".
column2: 在屏幕或文件上，"완료" 是 "已完成"，"진행 중" 是 "进行中"，"예정" 是 "预定"。

column1: 끝 is a noun: "이제 끝이에요" (It's over now), "끝까지 하세요" (Do it to the end).
column2: 끝 是名词："이제 끝이에요" (现在结束了)，"끝까지 하세요" (坚持做到最后)。

column1: -원 means a person who belongs to and works at a place. It is like "staff" or "worker" in English, but it goes at the end of the word.
column2: -원 表示属于某个地方并在那里工作的人。就像中文的 "员" (职员、店员)，也放在词的末尾。

column1: Words that end in "-원" are people who work at that place.
column2: 以 "-원" 结尾的词指在那里工作的人。

column1: The order is the same as in English: bank + worker = 은행 + 원.
column2: 和中文的顺序一样：银行 + 员 = 은행 + 원。

column1: Even if you have never seen a word before, if it ends in "-원", it is often a person: 상담원 (counselor), 배달원 (delivery person), 연구원 (researcher).
column2: 即使是没见过的词，只要以 "-원" 结尾，往往就是指人：상담원 (咨询员)，배달원 (送货员)，연구원 (研究员)。

column1: The dorm security guard is kind.
At night, a security guard goes around the school.
column2: 晚上有保安在学校巡逻。

column1: I left my package with the security guard.
column2: 我把快递寄放在保安那里了。

If you don't know something, ask the office staff.

column2: 我向手机店的店员询问了手机套餐。

column1: -사 is a person who works with a skill or qualification they learned. It is close to English endings like "-er" and "-ist" (teacher, pharmacist).

column1: Words that end in "-사" are people with a skill or qualification.
column2: 以 "-사" 结尾的词指有技术或资格的人。

column2: 称呼对方时加 "님"：기사님，간호사님，약사님。称呼医生用 "의사 선생님"。

column2: 其他带 "-사" 的词：변호사 (律师)，미용사 (美发师)，교사 (教师)，운전기사 (司机)。

column1: Words about Jeonju University's dormitory: its buildings, rooms, facilities and how to apply, based on the school's guide.
column2: 关于全州大学学生生活馆（宿舍）的楼栋、房间、设施和申请方法的词。内容以学校指南为准。

column1: Jeonju University's dormitory has Star Tower (18 floors, single, double and four-person rooms, each with its own shower and toilet) and Star Ville and Star Home (double rooms with shared showers). Together they take 1,885 students.
column2: 全州大学学生生活馆有Star Tower（地上18层，单人间、双人间、四人间，每间都有独立淋浴间和卫生间），以及Star Ville和Star Home（双人间，公用淋浴间）。共可容纳1,885名学生。

column1: You can stay for a year (52 weeks, early March to the end of next February), half a year (26 weeks, start of semester to end of vacation) or a semester (16 weeks, start of semester to the start of vacation). Apply on inSTAR (instar.jj.ac.kr).
column2: 入住期限有全年（52周，3月初~次年2月底）、半年（26周，学期初~假期结束）和学期（16周，学期初~放假前）。请在inSTAR（instar.jj.ac.kr）上申请。

column1: Questions: Star Tower office 063-239-5500, Star Ville and Star Home office 063-239-5520.
column2: 咨询：Star Tower运营办公室 063-239-5500，Star Ville·Star Home运营办公室 063-239-5520。
学生生活馆（宿舍的正式名称）

column2: 学生生活馆有Star Tower、Star Ville和Star Home。

column1: You apply for the dormitory on inSTAR.
I move into the dorm next week.
Don't miss the dorm application period.
column2: 不要错过宿舍申请时间。

column1: At the dorm, '입사' means moving in to live.
column2: 在宿舍，'입사' 是指搬进去住。

Clean your room when you move out.

column2: 退宿日期请咨询宿舍办公室。

column2: Star Ville和Star Home都是双人间。

column1: Star Tower has single, double and four-person rooms.
column2: Star Tower有单人间、双人间和四人间。

column1: The convenience store and café are amenities too.
column2: 便利店和咖啡馆也是配套设施。

在inSTAR上申请入住就可以了。

column2: Star Tower。Star Ville和Star Home使用公用淋浴间。

column1: Can I live there during the vacation too?
If you apply for a full year or a half year, you can stay during the vacation too.
column2: 申请全年或半年的话，放假期间也可以住。

column1: These are words for going to Jeonju University by city bus or the school commuter bus in Jeonju.

column1: These are the names of buildings and places on the Jeonju University campus. English-track students mainly study in 지역혁신관, 스타센터 (Star Center) and 자유관.
column2: 这些是全州大学校园里的建筑和地点名称。英语授课项目的学生主要在지역혁신관、스타센터（Star Center）和자유관上课。

column2: 名称后面的 "관" 是"馆、楼"的意思：자유관、지역혁신관、진리관。教室用"楼名 + 房间号"表示：자유관 305호（305室）。

column1: Common test instructions: "다음을 듣고 맞는 것을 고르십시오" (Listen and choose the correct answer), "빈칸에 들어갈 말을 고르십시오" (Choose the word for the blank).

column2: 林教授，我想在韩国公司工作。不过我担心签证问题。

column1: Ask the International Office about the job-seeking visa. An internship over the vacation would also help.
column2: 去国际交流院问问求职签证的事吧。假期去实习一下也会有帮助。

column1: Yes, I'll start by preparing my résumé.
column2: 好的，我先从准备简历开始。

Thank you so much for these four years.

column2: 谢谢您一直以来教了我这么多。

column2: 多亏了学长学姐，我才能毕业。

column2: 多亏了教授，我学到了很多。

column1: I had a great time thanks to all of you.
column2: 多亏了大家，我过得很开心。

column1: I'll keep in touch even after I go home.
column2: 回国以后我也会联系你的。

column1: I'll contact you when I arrive in Athens.

column2: 教授，请您一直保重身体。
一直以来谢谢你了。保重。

column2: 我们一定要在首尔再见面。

column2: 我还会再来全州的。一定要再见面。

column2: 沈教授，一直以来谢谢您。多亏了您，我才能毕业。

column1: You worked hard. Keep in touch after you go back to Greece.
column2: 辛苦了。回希腊以后也要保持联系。

column1: Yes, I'll be sure to contact you. Please stay healthy.
column2: 好的，我一定会联系您的。请您一直保重身体。

column1: International students must get permission before they start a part-time job. Learn the key words.
column2: 留学生开始打工之前必须获得许可。来学习一些必备的词吧。

column1: International students start a part-time job only after they get permission.
column2: 留学生要在获得许可后才能开始打工。

column1: D-2 students must get part-time work permission (시간제 취업 허가) before the first day of work, not after.
column2: D-2留学生必须在开始工作之前（而不是之后）获得兼职就业许可（시간제 취업 허가）。

column1: Permission is given for a specific workplace and period. If you change shops, apply again.
column2: 许可是针对特定的工作地点和期间发放的。换店的话需要重新申请。

column1: The rules change often. Check with the international office (국제교류처) and hikorea.go.kr.
column2: 规定经常变化。请向国际交流处（국제교류처）咨询，并在hikorea.go.kr上确认。

column1: I work part-time at a convenience store on weekends.
You have to get permission before you start a part-time job.
column2: 开始打工前必须获得许可。

column1: I applied for part-time work permission.
International students can work only with part-time work permission.
column2: 留学生必须有打工许可才能工作。

column1: You must not work without permission.
To work at a new shop, you need to get permission again.
column2: 要在新的店工作，必须重新获得许可。

column1: The boss asked me to show my residence card.
column2: 老板让我出示外国人登录证。

column1: You need your passport and residence card when you apply for permission.
column2: 申请许可时需要护照和外国人登录证。

column1: I'm going to the immigration office.
column2: 我要去出入境管理事务所。

column1: I made an appointment to visit the immigration office.
column2: 我预约了去出入境管理事务所。

column1: If you can't do it online, you have to go to the immigration office in person.
column2: 如果不能在网上办理，就必须亲自去出入境管理事务所。

column1: Working without permission is illegal work.
column2: 没有许可就工作属于非法就业。

column1: If you work illegally, you may pay a fine or have visa problems.
column2: 非法打工可能会被罚款或签证出问题。

column1: Boss, I'd like to work here.
Are you an international student? Do you have part-time work permission?
column2: 你是留学生吗？有打工许可吗？

column1: Not yet. I'll ask the school first.
Good. Call me when you get permission.
column2: 好的。拿到许可后联系我。

column1: International students have a limit on working hours. The semester and the vacation are different.
column2: 留学生的工作时间是有限制的。学期中和假期不一样。

column1: In the semester your hours are limited; in vacation you can work more.
column2: 学期中工作时间有限制；放假时可以多工作一些。

column1: Undergraduate (bachelor's) students who meet the Korean-level and grade conditions can work up to 25 hours a week in the semester (rules as of 2026). If you don't meet them, the limit is lower.
column2: 本科生如果满足韩语水平和成绩条件，学期中每周最多可以工作25小时（以2026年规定为准）。不满足条件的话，上限会更低。

column1: During vacation the hour limit is wider (for many students there is no weekly cap), but you still need permission.
column2: 放假期间时间限制更宽松（很多学生没有每周上限），但仍然需要许可。

column1: Your exact limit depends on your program, year and TOPIK level. Check with the international office.
column2: 具体上限取决于你的学位课程、年级和TOPIK级别。请向国际交流处确认。

column1: During the semester you can't work long hours on weekdays.
column2: 学期中，工作日不能长时间工作。

column1: During the semester there is a fixed limit on hours per week.
column2: 学期中每周可工作的时间是有规定的。

column1: You can work more during vacation.
column2: 放假期间可以多工作一些。

column1: I want to work at a cafe during summer vacation.
column2: 暑假我想在咖啡馆打工。

column1: I work three times a week.
How many hours a week do you work?
You must not go over the hours you are allowed per week.
column2: 不可以超过每周允许的工作时间。

column1: Part-time jobs for international students have an hour limit.
column2: 留学生打工有时间限制。

column1: The limit depends on your year, Korean level and grades.
column2: 时间限制根据年级、韩语水平和成绩而不同。

column1: TOPIK is a Korean proficiency test.
If you meet the Korean level condition, you can work longer.
column2: 满足韩语水平条件的话，可以工作更长时间。

column1: My grades last semester were good.
If your grades are too low, you may not get permission.
column2: 成绩太低的话，可能拿不到许可。

column1: Minha, can I work a lot during the semester?
column2: 敏夏，学期中可以多打工吗？

column1: No, international students have an hour limit.
column2: 不行，留学生有时间限制。

column1: Up to how many hours a week?
column2: 每周最多可以工作几个小时？

column1: It depends on your Korean level and grades. Ask the international office.
column2: 要看韩语水平和成绩。去问问国际交流处吧。

column1: To get permission you need the school's confirmation and some papers. Learn what to say when you apply.
column2: 要获得许可，需要学校的确认和一些材料。来学习申请时要说的话吧。

column1: Get the school's confirmation, then apply for permission on HiKorea.
column2: 先获得学校的确认，然后在HiKorea上申请许可。

column1: Usual order: find a job → sign a contract → get the school's confirmation → apply on HiKorea or at the immigration office → permission → start work.
column2: 一般顺序：找到工作 → 签合同 → 获得学校确认 → 在HiKorea或出入境管理事务所申请 → 获得许可 → 开始工作。

column1: It takes time to get permission, so prepare early.
column2: 获得许可需要时间，所以要提前准备。

column1: Always confirm the needed documents with the international office and the immigration office.
column2: 所需材料请务必向国际交流处和出入境管理事务所确认。

column1: The boss gave me the business registration and the work contract for my documents.
column2: 老板把营业执照和劳动合同给了我，作为申请材料。

column1: After you get the school's confirmation, you can apply on HiKorea.
column2: 获得学校确认后，就可以在HiKorea上申请。

column1: I got a confirmation form from the international office.
column2: 我在国际交流处拿到了确认书。

column1: If you don't know something, ask the staff at the international office.
column2: 有不懂的地方，请问国际交流处的工作人员。

column1: Can international students work at a cafe too?
column2: 留学生也可以在咖啡馆打工吗？

column1: I'm in my first year of Korean. Am I allowed to work?
column2: 我学韩语第一年。可以打工吗？

column1: You have to get permission first
You have to get permission first.
You have to get permission before you work.
column2: 工作之前必须先获得许可。

column1: Boss, I need to get permission first, so I can start from next week.
column2: 老板，我需要先获得许可，所以下周开始才能上班。

By when do I need to submit the papers?
column2: 材料最晚什么时候要交？

column1: If I work next month, by when should I apply?
column2: 如果下个月开始工作，最晚什么时候要申请？

column1: Getting permission takes time, so apply early.
column2: 获得许可需要时间，所以请尽早申请。

column1: I came to get a confirmation form
I came to get a confirmation form.
I came to get a part-time work confirmation form.

column1: Hello, I came to get the part-time job confirmation form.
column2: 您好，我是来领打工确认书的。

column1: Hello. I came to get a part-time work confirmation form.
column2: 您好。我是来领兼职就业确认书的。

column1: OK. Did you bring your work contract?
column2: 好的。劳动合同带来了吗？

column1: Yes, here it is. I have the business registration too.
column2: 带来了，给您。营业执照也带了。

column1: Good. After you get the form, apply on HiKorea.
column2: 好的。拿到确认书后，请在HiKorea上申请。

column1: Can I work before I get permission?
column2: 获得许可之前可以工作吗？

column1: No, you have to get permission first.
column2: 不可以，必须先获得许可。

column1: Job ads show the hourly wage, hours and place. Learn words often seen in ads.
column2: 招聘广告上会写时薪、时间和地点。来学习招聘广告中常见的词吧。

column1: In a job ad, check the wage, hours and experience needed.
column2: 在招聘广告上确认时薪、工作时间和经验要求。

column1: Many people find jobs on apps like 알바몬 (Albamon) and 알바천국 (Alba Heaven).
column2: 很多人在알바몬（Albamon）和알바천국（Alba Heaven）这样的应用上找工作。

column1: Look for words like 주 2일 (2 days a week), 주말 (weekends) and 경력 무관 (no experience needed).
column2: 注意看 주 2일（每周两天）、주말（周末）、경력 무관（无需经验）这样的词。

column1: The hourly wage must not be lower than the 2026 minimum wage (10,320 won).
column2: 时薪不能低于2026年的最低工资（10,320韩元）。

column1: I found a cafe job ad on Albamon.
column2: 我在Albamon上找到了一则咖啡馆的招聘广告。

The wage in the ad must not be lower than the minimum wage.

column2: 请先问一下外国人能不能应聘。

column1: Jinha, please look at this ad.

10,500 won. They say no experience is OK.
column2: 10,500韩元。他们说没有经验也可以。

column1: You call the shop after seeing an ad. Learn phrases for that call.
column2: 看到招聘广告后给店里打电话。来学习打电话时用的表达吧。

column1: Call about the ad and ask if the job is open and when the interview is.
column2: 看到广告后打电话，询问职位是否还空着以及面试时间。

column1: When you call, say your name and 공고 보고 전화드렸어요 first.
column2: 打电话时，先说自己的名字和 공고 보고 전화드렸어요。

column1: If you didn't catch something, say 다시 한번 말씀해 주시겠어요? (Could you say that again?).
column2: 没听清的话，就说 다시 한번 말씀해 주시겠어요?（您能再说一遍吗？）。

column1: It's also fine to send a text message first.

column2: 我是看到招聘广告打来的

column1: Are you still looking for someone?
Are you still hiring for weekends?
Sorry, I wonder if you are still hiring.
column2: 不好意思，我想问一下您是否还在招人。

column1: I'm an international student. Can I apply?
column2: 我是留学生，可以应聘吗？

column2: 是的，在招。您是韩国人吗？

column1: No, I'm an international student from Nepal. Can foreigners apply?
column2: 不是，我是来自尼泊尔的留学生。外国人也可以应聘吗？

column1: Yes, that's fine. Can you come for an interview tomorrow at four?
column2: 可以的，没问题。明天四点能来面试吗？

column1: Yes, I'll come tomorrow at four. Thank you.
column2: 好的，我明天四点过去。谢谢。

column2: 在打工面试中，要做自我介绍并说明可以工作的时间。

column2: 面试时，介绍自己、经历和可以开始工作的日期。

column1: Bring your residence card and any permission papers to the interview.
column2: 面试时请带上外国人登录证和与许可相关的材料。

column1: Tell the boss honestly that, as a student, your hours are limited.
column2: 要如实告诉老板，因为是留学生，工作时间有限制。

column1: Using -습니다 endings sounds more polite in an interview.
column2: 面试时用 -습니다 结尾会显得更礼貌。

I came ten minutes early so I wouldn't be late for the interview.

column1: I'm Tom from the United States.
I'm Aung from Myanmar. I'm a Jeonju University student.

I look forward to working with you.

column1: I'm Aung from Myanmar. I'm a second-year student at Jeonju University.
column2: 我是来自缅甸的昂。我是全州大学二年级的学生。

column1: Yes, I've worked at a cafe in Myanmar.
column2: 是的，我在缅甸的咖啡馆工作过。

column1: I can start as soon as I get permission. I'll work hard.
column2: 拿到许可后我马上就可以上班。我会努力的。

column2: 打工也必须签书面劳动合同。来学习合同上的词吧。

column2: 确认合同期限、工作地点、工作内容、工作时间和时薪后再签字。

column1: The 2026 minimum wage is 10,320 won per hour (Ministry of Employment and Labor notice). It changes every January.
column2: 2026年最低工资为每小时10,320韩元（雇佣劳动部公告）。每年1月调整。

column1: If your scheduled hours are 15 or more a week and you come on all scheduled days, you are entitled to weekly holiday pay (주휴수당).
column2: 如果每周规定的工作时间在15小时以上，并且规定的日子都出勤，就可以享受周休津贴（주휴수당）。

column1: International students have the same rights to minimum wage and weekly holiday pay as Korean workers.
column2: 外国留学生和韩国劳动者一样，享有最低工资和周休津贴的权利。

column1: The 2026 minimum wage is 10,320 won an hour.
International students must not be paid less than the minimum wage either.
column2: 留学生的工资也不能低于最低工资。

column1: I bought books with my part-time pay.
I think this month's pay was calculated wrong.
column2: 我觉得这个月的工资算错了。

column1: If you work 15 hours or more a week, you can get weekly holiday pay.
column2: 每周工作15小时以上，就可以领周休津贴。

column1: If you come on all your scheduled days, you get weekly holiday pay.
column2: 规定的日子都出勤的话，就有周休津贴。

column1: During the semester, night shifts can be hard on your studies.
column2: 学期中上夜班可能会影响学习。

column1: You calculate it as hourly wage times hours.
column2: 按时薪乘以工作时间来计算。

column1: You can calculate weekly holiday pay with an app.
column2: 可以用应用计算周休津贴。

column1: It's extra pay if you work 15 hours or more a week.
column2: 是每周工作15小时以上能额外拿到的钱。

column1: Then you can get it. What's your hourly wage?
column2: 那你可以领。时薪是多少？

column1: That's the 2026 minimum wage. Check the weekly holiday pay on your pay slip too.
column2: 这是2026年的最低工资。也要在工资单上确认周休津贴。

column1: Part-time pay usually goes into your bank account. Learn words about payday and pay slips.
column2: 打工工资一般打到银行账户里。来学习关于发薪日和工资单的词吧。

column1: On payday the money goes into your account; check it with the pay slip.
column2: 发薪日钱会打到账户里，请用工资单核对。

column1: By law, wages must be paid at least once a month on a fixed day.
column2: 根据法律，工资必须每月至少支付一次，并在固定日期支付。

column1: Employers must give you a pay slip. Check the hours and amounts.
column2: 雇主必须给你工资单。请核对工作时间和金额。

column1: Write down your work days and hours in a notebook or on your phone.
column2: 最好把工作日期和时间记在本子或手机上。

column1: Payday is the 10th of every month.
Payday has passed, but the money hasn't come in yet.
column2: 发薪日已经过了，但钱还没到账。

column1: You can open an account at a bank near school.
column2: 可以在学校附近的银行开户。

column1: Bring your residence card and passport when opening an account.
column2: 开户时请带上外国人登录证和护照。

column1: Please tell me your account number.
I sent my account number by text.
If the account number is wrong, you can't get paid.
column2: 账号错了的话就收不到钱。

column1: My pay was deposited in my account.
column2: 打工工资已经打到我的账户里了。

column1: Boss, I don't think the payment has come in yet.
The pay slip shows the hours worked.
column2: 工资单上写着工作时间。

column1: Check the hourly wage and holiday pay on the pay slip.
column2: 请在工资单上确认时薪和周休津贴。

column1: A little tax was taken out of my pay.
column2: 我的工资被扣了一点税。

column1: If you don't know why tax was taken, ask the boss.
column2: 如果不知道为什么扣税，请问老板。

column1: Boss, when is payday this month?
column2: 老板，这个月的发薪日是哪天？

column1: The 10th of every month. Did you give me your account number?
column2: 每月10号。你把账号告诉我了吗？

column1: Not yet. I'll send it by text.
column2: 还没有。我用短信发给您。

column1: OK. I'll deposit it and give you a pay slip too.
column2: 好的。我打钱的时候也会给你工资单。

column1: Convenience store jobs are popular with students. Learn the words used there.
column2: 便利店打工很受留学生欢迎。来学习在便利店用的词吧。

column1: At a convenience store you work the counter, stock shelves, check expiry dates and change shifts.
column2: 在便利店要收银、上货、检查保质期和交接班。

column1: There are many convenience stores near campus, so it's easy to work after class.
column2: 学校附近有很多便利店，下课后去打工很方便。

column1: Night shifts can be tiring during the semester. Also think about your hour limit.
column2: 学期中上夜班可能会很累。也要考虑工作时间限制。

column1: At shift change, check the cash and cigarette count together.
column2: 交接班时要一起核对现金和香烟数量。

column1: There are many customers at the counter.
Please refill the bags next to the counter.
column2: 请把收银台旁边的袋子补满。

column1: When new goods arrive, you have to stock them.
Put the items with the shortest expiry date at the front.
column2: 请把保质期短的商品放在前面。

column1: This milk is past its expiry date.
At night I check the expiry dates on the triangle gimbap and sort them.
column2: 晚上我检查三角饭团的保质期并整理。

column1: I'll see if there's stock in the storeroom.
column2: 我去看看仓库里有没有库存。

column1: I counted the stock and reported to the boss.
column2: 我清点了库存并向老板汇报了。

column1: When we change shifts, we count the money together.
column2: 交接班时一起清点现金。

column1: The next worker came late, so I couldn't change shifts.
column2: 下一班的人来晚了，所以没能交接班。

column1: I'd like to send a parcel.
You can send parcels at the convenience store.
I weigh the parcel box and enter it in the machine.
column2: 我称一下快递箱的重量，然后输入机器。

column1: Aung, please start by stocking the drinks today.
column2: 昂，今天请先把饮料上架。

column1: OK. I put the short expiry ones in front, right?
column2: 好的。把保质期短的放在前面，对吧？

column1: Right. Do we have cola in stock?
There are two boxes in the storeroom.
Good. You change shifts with Jinha at ten.
column2: 好的。十点你和珍夏交接班。

column1: Learn what to say to customers at the convenience store register.
column2: 来学习在便利店收银台对顾客说的话吧。

column1: At the register you ask about bags, cards, receipts and points.
column2: 在收银台要问顾客袋子、刷卡、小票和积分的事。

column1: Use polite forms like -세요 and -드릴까요? with customers.
column2: 对顾客要用 -세요、-드릴까요? 这样的礼貌表达。

column1: In Korea you can buy alcohol and cigarettes from the year you turn 19. Always check ID.
column2: 在韩国，从满19岁那一年起才能购买烟酒。一定要查看身份证件。

column1: If an unfamiliar payment comes up, say 잠시만요 and ask a senior coworker.
column2: 遇到不熟悉的付款方式，就说 잠시만요，然后问一下有经验的同事。

column1: Do you need a bag? It's 100 won.
You have a lot of things. Do you need a big bag?
column2: 您的东西很多，需要大袋子吗？

column1: The card didn't work. Please insert it again.
Shall I throw away the receipt?
You need the receipt to exchange it, so I'll give it to you.
column2: 换货需要小票，所以给您。

column1: Would you like to collect points?
Do you have a points card?
I'll add points with your phone number.
column2: 我用您的手机号帮您积分。

column1: Sorry, but please show me your ID.
column2: 不好意思，请出示一下身份证件。

column1: You must check ID before selling alcohol and cigarettes.
column2: 卖烟酒时必须先查看身份证件。

column1: Shall I heat it up for you?
Shall I heat the lunch box?
The microwave is over there. Heat it for about a minute.
column2: 微波炉在那边。加热一分钟左右。

column1: OK. Do you need a bag?
No, it's fine. I'll pay by card.
Please insert your card. Would you like a receipt?
Learn what to say when a customer is looking for something.
column2: 来学习顾客找东西时帮忙的说法吧。

column1: Tell customers where items are, when they're sold out and what's on offer.
column2: 告诉顾客商品的位置、是否售罄以及有什么促销活动。

column1: Common offers: 1+1 (buy one get one) and 2+1 (buy two get one).
column2: 常见的便利店促销：1+1（买一送一）和2+1（买二送一）。

column1: If the customer is a foreigner, you can help in English. That's a strength.
column2: 如果顾客是外国人，你可以用外语（比如中文、英语）帮忙。这也是你的优势。

column1: Excuse me, are you looking for something?
column2: 您好，请问您在找什么吗？

column1: If you're looking for something, please let me know.
column2: 如果您在找什么，请告诉我。

column1: Milk is at the very bottom of that fridge.
column2: 牛奶在那个冰箱的最下面。

column1: Sorry, that milk is sold out right now.
column2: 对不起，那款牛奶现在卖完了。

column1: It's sold out now, but more comes in tomorrow morning.
column2: 现在卖完了，明天早上会到货。

column1: This drink is buy one get one free.
column2: 这款饮料正在搞买一送一的活动。

column1: If you buy two, you get one more free.
It's 1+1, so please bring one more.
column2: 这是买一送一，请再拿一个。

column1: If it's the same price, you can bring another flavor.
column2: 如果价格一样，可以再拿一个别的口味的。

column1: Excuse me, where is the milk?
It's in that fridge over there.
Sorry, it's sold out right now. It comes in tomorrow.
column2: 对不起，现在卖完了。明天到货。

column1: That's buy one get one free. Please bring one more.
column2: 那款是买一送一。请再拿一个。

column1: To work at a cafe you need to know the menu words.
column2: 在咖啡馆打工需要知道菜单上的词。

column1: You can talk about cafe drinks, ice, sizes and extra shots.
column2: 能够谈论咖啡饮品、冰块、杯型和加浓缩。

column1: 따뜻한 거 means hot and 차가운 거 or 아이스 means iced.
column2: 따뜻한 거 是热的，차가운 거 或 아이스 是冰的。

column1: Take a photo of the menu and memorize it to learn fast.
column2: 把菜单拍下来背，可以学得很快。

column1: If a customer asks about allergies, tell them the exact ingredients.
column2: 顾客问到过敏问题时，要准确告知原料。

column1: For an americano, pull the shot first and add water.
column2: 做美式咖啡要先萃取浓缩，再加水。

column1: You make a latte by steaming milk.
column2: 拿铁是用加热的牛奶做的。

column1: A latte with soy milk costs 500 won more.
column2: 换成豆奶的拿铁要多收500韩元。

column1: We ran out of ice, so I checked the ice machine.
column2: 冰用完了，所以我检查了制冰机。

column1: Mark extra-shot orders on the cup.
column2: 加浓缩的订单请在杯子上做标记。

column1: If you change the size, the price changes.
column2: 换杯型的话，价格会不一样。
今天的甜点是芝士蛋糕。

column1: Take the dessert out of the fridge and put it on a plate.
column2: 从冰箱里拿出甜点放到盘子上。

column1: Maria, it's your first day, right? Let's start with the menu.
column2: 玛丽亚，今天是你第一天吧？我们先从菜单学起。

column1: OK. An americano is shots and water, right?
column2: 好的。美式咖啡就是浓缩加水，对吧？

column1: How much is an extra shot?
500 won. Desserts are in the fridge.
Learn the phrases for taking orders at a cafe.
column2: 来学习在咖啡馆点单时用的表达吧。

column1: At a cafe, ask the drink, hot or iced, for here or to go, and give the buzzer.
column2: 在咖啡馆要问顾客点什么、要热的还是冰的、堂食还是外带，然后给取餐呼叫器。

column1: Many cafes use mugs instead of disposable cups for customers staying in.
column2: 很多咖啡馆给堂食顾客用马克杯，而不是一次性杯子。

column1: Repeat the order back to the customer to avoid mistakes.
column2: 点单后再复述一遍确认，就能减少失误。

column1: Many shops use kiosks. Help customers who find them difficult.
column2: 很多店使用自助点餐机。顾客不会用的话，请帮帮他们。

column1: Hello, may I take your order?
Look at the menu and take your time ordering.
Would you like it hot or iced?
Would you like the latte hot?
I'll make it iced. Normal ice?
column2: 给您做冰的。冰块正常放可以吗？

column1: If you're drinking in the store, I'll give it to you in a mug.
column2: 如果您在店里喝，我用马克杯给您装。

column1: Here's your buzzer. Come when it rings.
column2: 这是您的呼叫器。响了请来取。

column1: The buzzer rings when your drink is ready, so have a seat and wait.
column2: 饮料做好时呼叫器会响，请坐下稍等。

column1: Customer number 35, your drink is ready.
Your drink is ready. It's hot, so be careful.
column2: 您点的饮料好了。很烫，请小心。

column1: It's busy, so it'll take a bit long. Please wait a moment.
column2: 现在人很多，需要多等一会儿。请稍等。

column1: I'll bring the cake out. Please wait a moment.
column2: 我去把蛋糕拿出来。请稍等。

column1: OK, one iced latte to go. Come when the buzzer rings.
column2: 好的，一杯冰拿铁外带。呼叫器响了请来取。

column1: At closing time you clean and tidy up. Learn the words for closing.
column2: 咖啡馆打烊时要打扫和整理。来学习打烊时用的词吧。

column1: At closing you wash dishes, clean the machine, sort recycling and tidy up.
column2: 打烊时要洗碗、清洁咖啡机、垃圾分类和整理。

column1: Closing work is working time. You should be paid for the time you work after closing.
column2: 打烊工作也算工作时间。打烊后工作的时间也应该拿到时薪。

column1: Separate food waste, general waste and recycling.
column2: 厨余垃圾、一般垃圾和可回收垃圾要分开扔。

column1: Take a photo of the closing checklist; it's handy.
column2: 把打烊检查清单拍下来会很方便。

column1: Before closing, write down how many cakes are left.
column2: 打烊前记下剩下的蛋糕数量。

column1: Please wash the mugs right away.
On busy days the dishes keep piling up.
column2: 客人多的日子，碗会一直堆积。

column1: I turned off the coffee machine.
The coffee machine is hot, so wear gloves.
Wash the cloth and hang it up.
column2: 请把抹布洗干净挂起来。

column1: We use separate cloths for tables and for the bar.
column2: 擦桌子的抹布和吧台的抹布要分开用。

column1: Rinse plastic cups and put them in recycling.
column2: 塑料杯冲洗干净后分类回收。

column1: In Jeonju, the days and times for recycling are fixed.
column2: 在全州，垃圾分类回收的日期和时间是固定的。

column1: Please arrange the cups by size.
column2: 请把杯子按大小整理好。

column1: Tidy the ingredients and leave a note for the next person.
column2: 为下一班的人整理好原料并留下便条。

column1: Tom, let's do the closing together today.
column2: 汤姆，今天我们一起打烊吧。

column1: OK. I'll start with the dishes.
Good. I'll clean the coffee machine.
Where do we put the recycling?
Behind the shop. When you're done, please wash the cloths too.
column2: 扔到店后面。弄完后请把抹布也洗了。

column1: Learn phrases for greeting guests in a restaurant.
column2: 来学习在餐厅迎接客人时用的表达吧。

column1: Greet guests, ask how many and about reservations, then show them to a table.
column2: 迎接客人时要打招呼，询问人数和是否预约，然后带客人入座。

column1: Say 어서 오세요 clearly when guests come in.
column2: 客人进来时要大声说 "어서 오세요"。

column1: 분 is the polite word for 사람; ask guests 몇 분이세요?
column2: 분 是 사람 的敬语；问客人时说 몇 분이세요?

column1: Many restaurants bring water and a wet towel first.
column2: 很多餐厅会先给客人上水和湿毛巾。

column1: For dishes not on the menu, I'll ask the boss.
column2: 菜单上没有的菜，我去问一下老板。

column1: Welcome. We have a few seats right now.
column2: 欢迎光临。现在还有几个座位。

column1: How many? If you're four, the inner seats are good.
column2: 几位？四位的话，里面的座位比较好。

column1: We're cleaning, so please sit here in a moment.
column2: 我们正在打扫，请稍后坐这边。

column1: Do you have a reservation? What's your name?
column2: 请问您有预约吗？请问您贵姓？

column1: There are many reservations today, so you'll have to wait 30 minutes.
column2: 今天预约的客人很多，您需要等三十分钟。

column1: I'll clear the table. Please wait a moment.
Please write your name on the waiting list and wait a moment.
column2: 请在等位名单上写上名字，稍等一下。

column1: That's fine. Please sit here. Here's the menu.
column2: 没关系。请这边坐。这是菜单。

column1: Learn phrases for taking orders and serving food in a restaurant.
column2: 来学习在餐厅点单和上菜时用的表达吧。

column1: Take the order, confirm it, serve the food and offer more side dishes.
column2: 点单、确认、上菜，并询问是否需要加小菜。

column1: Jeonju has many bibimbap and bean sprout soup restaurants. Learn those menu names.
column2: 全州有很多拌饭和豆芽汤饭餐厅。请记住这些菜名。

column1: Repeat the order to confirm: 비빔밥 두 개, 맞으세요?
column2: 点单后复述确认：비빔밥 두 개, 맞으세요?

column1: Always carry hot bowls on a tray.
column2: 端热碗时一定要放在托盘上。

column1: What would you like to drink? We have cola and cider.
column2: 您要喝点什么？我们有可乐和雪碧。

column1: How many servings of pork belly?
For two people, most order three servings.
column2: 两位的话，一般点三人份。

column1: Here you are (the food is ready)
Here's the bean sprout soup with rice you ordered.
All your food is here. Enjoy your meal.
column2: 您的菜都上齐了。请慢用。

column1: Call me if you need anything. Enjoy.
column2: 还需要什么请叫我。请慢用。

column1: The bowl is hot, so be careful.
The stone pot is very hot, so don't touch it.
Would you like more side dishes?
You can get more side dishes from the self-serve corner.
column2: 小菜可以到自助区自己添加。

column1: Two bibimbap and one bean sprout soup, please.
column2: 请给我两份拌饭和一份豆芽汤饭。

column1: OK, two bibimbap and one bean sprout soup, right?
column2: 好的，两份拌饭和一份豆芽汤饭，对吗？

column1: Here's your food. It's hot, so be careful.
column2: 您点的菜来了。很烫，请小心。

column1: Thanks. A bit more kimchi, please.
column2: 谢谢。请再给我一点泡菜。

column1: Learn words for working as a kitchen helper.
column2: 来学习在餐厅厨房当帮工时用的词吧。

column1: In the kitchen you wash your hands, cut and boil ingredients and tidy the dishes.
column2: 在厨房要洗手、切菜、煮东西和整理餐具。

column1: The kitchen has knives and fire, so it's dangerous. Ask if you're not sure.
column2: 厨房里有刀和火，很危险。不清楚的话一定要问。

column1: The floor can be slippery; wear non-slip shoes.
column2: 地面可能很滑，请穿防滑鞋。

column1: If you get hurt at work, industrial accident insurance can cover treatment (see K5-K).
column2: 工作时受伤的话，可以通过工伤保险接受治疗（参见K5-K）。

column1: Before opening, take out the ingredients for today.
column2: 开店前，把今天要用的食材拿出来。

column1: Please slice the green onions thinly.
Be careful with your hands when cutting with a knife.
column2: 用刀切的时候要小心手。

column1: You must wash your hands after using the toilet.
Please put the dishes back in place.
Don't touch broken dishes with bare hands.
The shop gives you an apron.
Before going into the kitchen, put on an apron and a cap.
column2: 进厨房前要穿上围裙、戴上帽子。

column1: Boil the broth for ten minutes.
When boiling a big pot, two people move it together.
column2: 煮大锅的时候，两个人一起搬。

column1: Vishal, please help in the kitchen today.
column2: 维沙尔，今天请帮忙厨房的工作。

column1: OK. What should I do first?
Wash your hands and put on an apron. Then please slice some onions.
column2: 先洗手穿上围裙。然后请切一些洋葱。

column1: Five. Be careful with the knife.
Some jobs are not allowed for international students. Always check before you start.
column2: 有些工作留学生是不能做的。开始工作前一定要确认。

column1: Delivery riding, manufacturing and construction are generally not permitted for students.
